texts.label: 117/1 = R25, ff. 95r-95v, 12 Sept 1758
texts.summary: The nuncio's secret account of the attempt of 3 Sept 1758 on José I: coming back from a lady "delle prime famiglie" (the young Marchioness of Távora), the king was fired on in his calesse, his valet and favourite Pedro Teixeira badly wounded and the king hit in the right arm. The blow was thought to come from her relatives or from Teixeira's enemies.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1757, Italian, modern spelling: the plain share is the bar): the sweep scored the whole file, header and notes included (plain 0.526, explicit 0.737). '## Reading' heading added before the body; body alone: plain 0.87 (20/23), explicit 1.0 (23/23). The three failing sentences hold; their unknown words are the name Texeira, the marked [?Vilasso], and caualcante/bilancino/lasciandoui (period words the list lacks). Keeps read. Earlier: Read from the Secretariat of State's own clear decipherment, attached to the DECODE record as a png and transcribed here (texts/R25_decipherment.txt), aligned word by word with the key decode (texts/R25_align.tsv; code values consistent across the four letters); _check_reading.py on the body 0.87 (20 of 23 sentences); 'Vilasso' after Texeira kept from the decipherment, unconfirmed by the figures.

texts.label: 117/2 = R195, f. 98r, Sept 1758
texts.summary: The public version of the king's injury is illness; the arm is said to be broken. Fleets and ships are held back, to the merchants' loss.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1757, Italian, plain share is the bar): the sweep scored the whole file with notes (plain 0.448, explicit 0.655). '## Reading' heading added; body alone: plain 0.818 (9/11), explicit 0.818 (9/11). The two failing sentences are the two [?] stretches the figures do not confirm ('pare [?solamente] [?assicurato]' and one in the last paragraph); the rest holds. Keeps read. Earlier: Read from the Secretariat of State's own clear decipherment, attached to the DECODE record as a png and transcribed here (texts/R195_decipherment.txt), aligned word by word with the key decode (texts/R195_align.tsv; code values consistent across the four letters); _check_reading.py on the body 0.91 (10 of 11 sentences); the decipherer's one hole ('poiché non . . .', margin 'non s'intende') read on the cipher image: 'poiché non ha da durare', as in the draft; two stretches not confirmed by the transcribed figures are marked [?].

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1758, Italian, plain share is the bar): the entry named no reading and the sweep scored Lasry's raw decryption (decode/DOC_R25_D3231_3231.txt, plain 0.355, explicit 0.774). title: The 22 'unsolved' ADFGVX radio messages, Eastern Front, November 1918 (Childs corpus; Schmeh's list)

documents.shelfmark: James Rives Childs transcription, pages 73-217 (list provided by George Lasry on Schmeh's blog, 2017)

plaintext.source: Readings of 9 messages and parts of 3 in the comment thread under Schmeh's 2017 post (Norbert, Armin, Lasry and others); 10 never read.

transcription.source: Schmeh's blog page (msgs.txt), from the Childs transcription
transcription.notes: Count is the sum of the per-message letter counts in the NOTES table (22 messages, marked gaps excluded). msgs.txt mixes blog prose with the ciphertext, so --measure gives no clean figure. Mutilation in transmission (lost or added letters, marked gaps) is the obstacle.

system.summary: ADFGVX: 6x6 Polybius substitution to letter pairs followed by columnar transposition under a three-day key (lengths 16-19).
system.sibling_key: Fourteen published period keys (Lasry, Niebel, Kopal, Wacker) plus Lasry's sixteenth CHI key of 13 Nov 1918 from the 2017 thread, rebuilt here; used.
system.notes: Three published squares damaged by PDF dash collapse and repaired; transposition convention settled on page 100.

prior_solution.where: Published keys (Lasry et al.) and the 2017 comment thread under Schmeh's post (9 solved, 3 partial)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: block-edit search with German quadgram model (blocks.py, lm_de.py)
key-free transposition annealer (keyless.py) with planted controls

solution.what: Made the fourteen published keys machine-readable; repaired three squares damaged by the PDF text layer.
Settled the transposition convention and reproduced page 100 by insertion search over all keys (score 140.7).
Read the 70 comments of the 2017 thread: 9 solved, 3 partial, 10 open; Lasry's sixteenth key found and its square rebuilt (24 of 36 cells).
Norbert's block-edit method reimplemented; re-derives 7 solved pages blind and finds the 22-24 Nov partial.
Two block edits against fifteen keys on the ten open messages; CHI key on the two page-153 messages.
Key-free attack on a planted 224-letter control does not recover the key; open messages (84-240 letters) are below reach.

Outcome split into parts per period key (one key per entry): six keys with their messages (9 solved, 3 partial) and the ten messages no known key fits (not solved), from the NOTES table; README one row per part.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): msgs.txt (Lasry's list of the 22 ciphertexts) as transcription; the readings table copied verbatim from NOTES.md to texts/residue22_decryption.md; keys.json (fifteen keys incl. the rebuilt CHI key) as key file. Ten messages have no reading.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): texts/residue22_decryption.md read message by message. The nine full readings build German sentences; the three partial readings have "..." gaps in most sentences and ten messages have no reading. The entry split into a read entry and a decoded, not read entry; class already solved -> read in part; fraction_read unknown -> 0.49 (letters).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b24): searched for readings of the residue messages published after 2017. Found a decipherment of a 27 Nov 1918 message of about 170 letters posted by 'prinz' on 17 Sept 2026 (reported by The Neuron, 18 Sept 2026, and news sites): keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG, plaintext 'EIN ENGLISCHER KREUZER EINLIEG X SEWASTOPOL X S4STEN X EIN GESCHWADER DER X ALLIIERTEN FOLGT 26STEN X'. Childs p. 217 has 170 letters.

Known-plaintext check on p. 217 (b24_adfgvx_217.py): the transposition by TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG turns the 170 received letters into 85 pairs that map one to one onto the 85 plaintext letters (23 distinct pairs, 23 distinct letters, no conflict), and the recovered cells form a keyword-shaped square (T R U P E 4 / N . S C 2 H). Accepted; texts/p217_reading.md and _en.md. The same transposition and cells applied to the nine other open messages give noise.

VGADA (Childs p. 215): Norbert's two inserted groups with the Nov 22-24 key reproduce his raw decrypt exactly; aligned letter by letter with Baertl's 2017 corrected text (b24_adfgvx_vgada.py): 97 of 129 letters carried by both cells, 11 by one, 1 by none, 20 of Baertl's letters contradict the received cells and only 5 of those are one-cell errors ('S4N' twice where he reads '24N'; p. 217 has 'S4STEN' too). Partial reading kept (texts/vgada_partial_reading.md, 0.00 clean); stays decoded, not read.

VGADA residual search with the three length-22 keys and two free edits (gaps.py anneal, 6 restarts) before Norbert's edits were applied: noise (-7.4 per letter); his group insertions at the marked gap and after group 43 are what make it decrypt.

v3 verification: residue22 entry scored on its table file (0.188); the nine full readings extracted to texts/residue22_reading.md and rescored with v2_score.py: 0.87 explicit-hole (plain 0.565). Keeps read; reading field added.

Consistency pass (cl): outcome.texts summary reworded for docs/_check_terms.py (outcome words 'read', 'undeciphered', 'unsolved' replaced by what happened: deciphered, given a value, transcribed, no decipherment known); facts unchanged.

Consistency pass (cl): the closed item (p. 217) was still a bullet in NOTES Remaining gaps, which the checker reads as an open gap without a blocker; restated below the list as Closed. outcome.gaps unchanged (it already lists only the open pieces).

outcome.method_basis: The fourteen period keys published by Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker for the Childs corpus, plus Lasry's sixteenth (CHI) key from the 2017 Cipherbrain comment thread, were applied with a block-edit search; the only full reading (page 100) had already been read in 2017.
outcome.notes: Nothing read here that the 2017 readers had not read; the thread consolidated and the sixteenth key rebuilt. Ten messages remain open, needing the Childs originals or an unlisted key. Split into outcome.parts per period key on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry, parts because the messages form one filed set): 9 solved, 3 partial, 10 open. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: the readings table split into two entries, the nine messages that read (state read) and the thirteen partial or open ones (decoded, not read); class already solved -> read in part, fraction_read 0.49 by letters. 23 Oct 2026 (b24): p. 217 read from the decipherment reported in Sept 2026 ('prinz', keyword TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG), verified here as known plaintext (85 pairs, one-to-one); VGADA's 2017 reading checked letter by letter (20 of Baertl's letters against the cells): stays partial.

texts.label: 22 ADFGVX messages, Childs pages 73-217 (Nov 1918): the nine read in full (pp. 100, 105, 109, 132, 146, 171, 176, 187 part 1 and its part 2 AFAFF)
texts.summary: German ADFGVX radio messages of November 1918 from James Rives Childs's transcription, listed by George Lasry on Schmeh's blog in 2017 among the messages with no known decipherment. The readings, consolidated from the 2017 comment thread (Norbert, Armin, Baertl, Lasry), are routine traffic: march reports towards Belgrade, a repeat-telegram order, the Kertsch radio station, rouble rates after the break with the Soviet government; no decipherment of the other ten messages is known.

title: Adrian of Utrecht, the Admiral and the Constable of Castile to Charles V, Vitoria, 30 Dec 1521, AGS Estado leg. 8 no. 150

documents.shelfmark: AGS Estado leg. 8 no. 150 (PARES 13002542)

plaintext.source: Claudio Perez Gredilla's decipherment, printed by Danvila, Memorial Historico Espanol 38 (1899), pp. 703-705, with about 25 groups unread

transcription.source: PARES images (~1000 px), crop and upscale

title: Andreae, Chymische Hochzeit Christiani Rosencreutz, Strassburg 1616: printed secret-script inscriptions (DECODE R4502)

documents.shelfmark: Embassy of the Free Mind (Ritman Library), Amsterdam; Chymische Hochzeit, Strassburg 1616, pp. 73, 95, 97, 116; DECODE R4502

plaintext.source: The novel glosses the pp. 95 and 97 inscriptions in the following paragraphs (pp. 96, 98); Foxcroft 1690 / crcsite.org edition footnotes 12, 14, 15, 21 give all four, the sign lines as the dates 1378 and 1459.

transcription.source: DECODE R4502 public images P3-P8 (about 1450 px per opening)
transcription.notes: Letter inscriptions only; the two symbolic date lines (about 10 signs each) are described in NOTES, not transcribed. The three dotted variants for M/N/O were assigned with the plaintext in view.

system.summary: Simple substitution in an invented type-cut alphabet, words divided, for two inscriptions; two further lines of alchemical and numeral signs give dates.

diacritics.note: M, N and O are dotted variants of one base shape.

system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: U and V share one sign; one capital form (initial H).

prior_solution.where: The novel itself (glosses on pp. 96, 98); Foxcroft, The Hermetick Romance (1690), as footnoted on crcsite.org.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target from the catalogue; DECODE cookie already on file.

solution.what: Repo and web search for R4502 / Andreae cipher; no decipherment found under that description.
Fetched DECODE record, metadata and 8 public images; identified the item as a printed copy of the Chymische Hochzeit, not a letter.
The p.95 and p.97 inscriptions are the texts the page boy speaks on pp.96 and 98; tested as a simple substitution.
Aligned BEGRABEN, FRAW, GLUCK, FRUCHT, BAUMS etc.; built a 19-sign table consistent over both inscriptions.

title: Johan Banér to Torsten Stålhandske, Hof, 29 December 1640: intercepted copy in Kircher's correspondence (APUG 568 f. 239), posted unsolved on Cipherbrain 2019

documents.shelfmark: Archivio della Pontificia Università Gregoriana, APUG 568 f. 239r-v (Kircher correspondence); images as posted on Cipherbrain, 2 June 2019
documents.route: Johan Banér (Hof, Upper Franconia) to Major General Torsten Stålhandske (Silesia); intercepted, copy

plaintext.source: No decipherment with the copy as posted; none found in print or online (Cipherbrain comments 2019-2020: attempts failed).

transcription.source: Philip Neal's transcription (Cipherbrain), checked figure by figure against the Museo Galileo scans of APUG 568 f. 239r-v (1469x2304 px)
transcription.notes: 274 two-digit values and 14 three-digit code words (--drop-first). Four figures corrected from the scans: S4 66->86, S4 36->86, S5 57->47, S7 illegible->92.

system.summary: Two-digit homophonic alphabet (1-6 values per letter, 2-98) inside clear German, with three-digit code words (361-568 names and nouns, 766-783 short words or syllables).
system.notes: Not banded like the Swedish chancery keys of 1634-40 on DECODE (R4123, R4325), and not any of the Banér keys there. The 7xx codes sit where the dropped letters of darau(ff), au(ss), ko(mm)en fall; they may be syllable or double-letter codes.

prior_solution.where: Cipherbrain post 2 June 2019 and comments (Neal, SantaColoma) report failed attempts; DECODE has no record of the letter; web search 22 Sept 2026 found no reading.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: DECODE API scan of Riksarkivet Chifferklaver box II

solution.what: Fetched the Cipherbrain post (2 June 2019): two page images, Neal's transcription, the comments. Identified '568 239r' as APUG 568 (Kircher correspondence); the Museo Galileo image database needs a registered login; EMLO has no record.

Took Neal's transcription into ct_neal.txt as seven segments S1-S7 (274 two-digit values, 74 distinct; 14 three-digit codes); checked it against the blog images, which are too small to confirm single figures.
Unconstrained homophonic annealing with the de-1500s 5-gram model: overfits to en/ne/sie strings.
Crib 'auf den [442]' before 'loszugehen': produces 'due' elsewhere; dropped.

Scanned the Riksarkivet key box (Chifferklaver låda II, DECODE R4103-R4329) through the API and the archivists' cover labels; transcribed and tried the Banér keys R4122 (Horn-Banér), R4123 (Banér 1634, = R4325 'Generalis Campi Marschalli Johan Banneris Cyffer'), R4325's other alphabets and R4266, as is and with value offsets -30..+30.

From the Swedish keys: values in four bands, each band a permutation of the alphabet. Banded swap annealer (solve3.py) recovers a synthetic control enciphered with R4123 when given about 8 crib values; on the letter no band layout scores near a true solution.

Synthetic control (1630s German from Theatrum Europaeum, same segment lengths, R4123 key): true plaintext scores -279 against -390..-430 for unconstrained optima, so the search needs cribs; with 8 crib values a multiset model (4 homophones per letter, no bands) reaches -275.
S6 opens after 'mich aber von zeit zu zeit' with 40 16 23 28 29 = durch; 16 64 40 = und. With these fixed the multiset annealer produced 'nach der ... pfaltz und' in S3.
S3 = 'nach der Oberpfaltz und gegen die [442]' (Banér's march from Hof into the Upper Palatinate towards Regensburg): 20 values fixed, all consistent with durch/und.

Key extended word by word from the context and cross-checked across segments: Schlesien agirende, dazu ziehen, etwa auch (S4); gute acht geben, sobaldt, ehender, solche, Fürsichtigkeit nachvolgen (S5); wohin er seine(n) Marche zu richte(n) entgegen (S7); Johann, über (S2). 70 values in key.json.
decode.py applies key.json: 239 of 274 cipher tokens read as sense (87.2%); unread: a name in S2, 14 tokens in S5, 4 tokens in S1, 2 in S6, the illegible figure in S7; all 14 code words open.
Found the Museo Galileo Kircher scans served openly (archimede.imss.fi.it/kircher/568/large/239r.jpg, 239v.jpg); the login only guards the search database.
Re-read every cipher line on the scans: Neal right except four figures (S4 66->86, 36->86; S5 57->47; S7 = 92).

Re-measured with the corrected transcription: 244 of 274 (89.1%); S1 = Jobs[508] (Jobst), S7 complete. Digit-confusion search (emend.py) finds nothing for the S5 stretch; the copy itself is corrupt there.

Freed every value in the unread stretches and treated the 7xx codes as letters: the annealer returned 'auf solche Weise' (772 f, 766 W) and 'dass sie mögen' (783 g, 60 m) unprompted; 246 of 274 (89.8%). All three-digit numbers as letters does not read.

Re-transcribed every unread stretch (S2 name, S5 'eisen o vi rechte' and 'o 2 ein', S6) from the Museo Galileo scan of 239r at 2x zoom. All figures confirm the transcription except S6, where the manuscript has '13. 12. 32' and Neal dropped the 12: 'Espionen' is complete and 12 = p (also used in the S2 name, 'ohrs p acbuet', still no name).

S5 stretch '[766]eise n o u i r e c h t e zu' tried as 'auf solche Weise movirte/moviret/nachrichte/noch richte' with de-1640s in context: no candidate both fits the confirmed figures and scores clearly better; 'o 2 ein guten' as 'mit einer guten' needs two figures changed. Not counted.

Checked the measure: decode.py counts every token outside hand-marked unread spans, so the 'n' after code 513 in S2 was counted though it makes no word. New measure_sense.py splits the decrypt into the reading's words, counts only tokens inside sense words and asserts the split matches the decrypt: 246 of 275 (89.5%).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 252 tokens, 77 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -1.731 per letter; random keys -5.997 (z 10.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.583 (mean -2.692, z 11.8); annealer on the real text -2.583. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked ct_neal.txt (Philip Neal's transcription with the manuscript checks), reading.md (segment-by-segment decryption, code words left as [nnn]) and key.json.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, graded C): reading.md read through with the clear context. The cipher runs are inserts in clear German sentences; four of seven read whole and two mostly, so every sentence of the letter can be built, with the code words and the S2 name and S5 stretch open. Grade overturned: kept read in part, reading_review B; no figure changed.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 1 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.736; polyphony 0.004; 37 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.583

outcome.method: key recovered based on adjacent plaintext
outcome.method_basis: The homophonic key (70 values) was rebuilt from cribs taken from the clear German around the cipher passages ('durch' after 'mich aber von zeit zu zeit', then 'und'), which let the constrained annealer produce 'nach der Oberpfaltz und gegen die [442]'; the key was then extended word by word from context. The Swedish Banér keys on DECODE (R4122, R4123/R4325, R4266) were tried and did not fit.
outcome.fraction_read_source: measure_sense.py over ct_neal.txt (corrected against the APUG 568 scans, 12 restored in S6): two-digit cipher tokens inside words read as sense, 246/275; code words excluded

gaps.item: S2 name after 'Johann' (11 tokens)
gaps.detail: Figures confirmed on the manuscript scan; values fixed elsewhere, so the only known copy is corrupt; the sent original or a Swedish register copy is not digitised.

gaps.item: S5 'eisen o vi rechte' (14), 'o ?' (2), stray e (1)
gaps.detail: Figures confirmed on the manuscript scan; the copy is corrupt; another witness needed.
No key survives; each occurs once. 766, 770, 772, 778, 783 read as letters.

outcome.notes: First reading of the letter. Key rebuilt here from context cribs; no Swedish key on DECODE matches. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit (graded C): re-read; the cipher runs complete the clear sentences with scattered code words, so the grade is overturned (reviewed B). A full English translation (not only the sense paragraph) still to add.

texts.label: Banér to Stålhandske, Hof, 29 Dec 1640
texts.summary: An intercepted copy, sent to Athanasius Kircher, of a letter from the Swedish general Johan Banér to Torsten Stålhandske, commanding in Silesia: Banér means to march into the Upper Palatinate, expects the enemy to gather against him and draw in the forces operating in Silesia, and tells Stålhandske to keep good watch, follow with caution when the enemy moves, report through spies and tell him where to direct his march.

reading_review.note: The seven cipher runs are inserted in clear German sentences; S1, S3, S4 and S7 read whole ('nach der Oberpfaltz und gegen die [442]', 'wohin er seinen Marche zu richten'), S5 and S6 mostly, and with the clear context each sentence of the letter can be built and translated. Open: the courier's name in S2, a 14-token corrupt stretch in S5 (corrupt in the copy itself) and the code words.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 84.6% of the words of APUG568-239_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

system.summary: A Dutch homophonic letter table accompanies an alphabetical codebook with fifteen marked number series and names.

diacritics.note: Fifteen blocks selected by overhead marks or struck digit; see NOTES.md.

system.notes: 1417 is the merged count (1393 earlier codes plus 24 new codes in 27 additional rows) of distinct transcribed dictionary codes, not the full historical codebook. Letter table 2–98; main blocks 99–999; names on key scans 59 and 78–82.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary decipherments on inv. 401 scans 28R, 32R (19 December 1686, four numbered passages), 42R–43R and 101R; no edition found in the prior-art search.

conditions.human_role: Decipherment by Feyseel Nur with Claude and Codex; original division of transcription work undocumented.

solution.what: De Leeuw 2000 describes Fagel codebooks, not Battier; no edition found; letters absent from DECODE.
Named Battier key NA 1.10.29 inv. 1209, DECODE R2794; old 5345 citation corrected.
Letter table and about 1400 codebook values transcribed; marked cipher tokens and inventory retained.
Key applied to five focus letters and supporting letters; the earlier volume estimate was roughly 55%, with no revised denominator for the 235-token addition.

First two validation letters: 1113/1132 comparable tokens agree (98.3%); 94.7% key-alone; 18 positions not comparable. Third validation: 19 December 1686, four passages and 186 tokens, reproduces the contemporary list on 32R apart from spelling and gedaan/afgedaen. Confirms 15:325 = wat and 12:409 = syn; strengthens the identification of inv. 1209 as Battier's key. Comparison is not blind.
300-permutation control: 72% spelled runs segment into Dutch, mean 1.2%, maximum 4.1% shuffled.

Codex software re-decoding, not paleography: 19 Dec 186/186 is validation of contemporary plaintext; 24 April 1687 passes strict sense without a known contemporary decipherment, 230/235 (97.9%), as does 8 April 1688, 313/323 (96.9%), conservatively 312/323 (96.6%). Dec 1687 94.3% and Feb 1688 92.3% do not pass.

WAINUT (PR #65): folder key applied to scan 67R cipher lines 1-3 (June 1687, listed as not read): 45 tokens, 21 letters and 24 codes, 8 code rows looked up in the key scans; grades H 41, M 3, I 1 (885 open). Gastañaga's expenses and 'soigneuslyke borse' to the 'totale ruïne' of the Spanish Netherlands. Key-rotated-by-one control loses the sense (weak for codes). Key row correction: 11:718 soetjens, 11:719 soetelaars (key s59L1); neither occurs in tokens/.

WAINUT (PR #65): single Gemini pass against this folder's checked tokens: same number 88% (58R) / 95% (59L) but same decoded value only 71% / 78%, so no machine-only transcription is offered as a reading.

WAINUT (PR #67): folder key applied to seven 1687 letters listed as not read: 16 Jan (207 groups, 11 uncertain), 13 Feb (272/11), 27 Feb (575/8), 13 Mar 55L only (66/1), 10 Jun 67R (152/6), 20 Nov (60/1), 18 Dec 94R ll. 1-5 (57/1); 1,389 groups, 39 uncertain, every group checked by eye on the scans. Codes from key/dict 586, letters 645, and 158 from an unchecked machine read of the code book (wainut/r24_1687/key_rows_machine.tsv). Each letter beats 20 row-shifted and 200 shuffled keys under a Dutch 4-gram model (control script not included). The 2 Jan 1687 letter (35R, 36L) has heavy interlinear decipherment: inv/orch_letters.tsv was wrong to list it as 'no'.

title: Benedict XIII's cipher letters to Francesc Climent, 1399-1403, Arxiu Capitular de Barcelona (catalogue 334)

documents.shelfmark: Arxiu Capitular de Barcelona, Cisma d'Occident paper series (Puig's 'Documentos inéditos del obispo Çapera' nos. 1063, 409 and others; Meister 1906: capsa 'Documentos referentes a la familia Luna I')
documents.route: Benedict XIII, Avignon -> Francesc Climent, Barcelona
documents.language: Latin with Catalan and Castilian phrases

plaintext.source: Puig y Puig, Pedro de Luna, último papa de Aviñón (Barcelona 1920), appendix, cipher passages in italics; key rebuilt by Puig from Climent's partial decipherment lines on docs. 1063, 461, 463.

transcription.source: Only one page is imaged: Puig 1920 p. 475, a halftone facsimile of the last page of XXXV (doc. 1068), via Google Books (1826 x 2500 px), deskewed and read line by line at 3-5x. Every cipher run on the plate checked word by word against Puig's text (148 words, 826 plaintext letters; src/plate475_check.tsv); no free-standing sign transcription.
transcription.notes: Ten ciphered letters of Benedict XIII in Puig's appendix (XXVI, XXVII, XXXV, XXXVI, XXXVII, XXXIX, XLI, XLII, XLIII, LII), treated as one set. About 2,200 deciphered words. The plate check covers the only imaged page (XXXV, doc. 1068). The letters of his circle (Santa Cruz, Jafet, Exea, Comuel) and the 1398 Vico line were split off on 14 Oct 2026.

system.summary: Simple substitution, one invented or letter-shaped sign per letter (20 values: a hook, b T-bar, c and i a single o, o a double loop, d double cross, e delta, f flagged sigma, g 4-shape, h 2-shape, l looped d, m footed epsilon, n n, p inverted T, q double-barred upright, r upright stroke, s T, t c with superscript, u/v joined cb, x alpha-shape), signs joined by hair-lines with no word division, mixed into clear Latin; a dotted V for the King of Aragon; groups of lambda/z-like signs as null separators at sentence breaks. Rebuilt from the p. 475 facsimile against Puig's text (key.md).
system.sibling_key: Two keys of Climent in the same papers (doc. 595) that Puig could not apply to any document; not printed. Clement VII's Lavinde alphabets (Meister 1906, Schlüsselsammlung I) are the nearest printed keys.
system.notes: c and i share one small o on the 1920 halftone (o is a double loop) and d/p are hard to separate; the original may distinguish them. Key rebuilt from known plaintext (Puig's reading), not ciphertext-only. Verified on doc. 1068 only; that Benedict's other letters use it rests on Puig having built his key from Climent's lines on three of them (docs. 1063, 461, 463).

prior_solution.where: Puig y Puig, Pedro de Luna (Barcelona 1920), appendix: deciphered by Puig himself from Climent's partial glosses; not cited by Meister (1906, earlier), Galende 2013, or the cryptologic literature checked.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and posed the target with /goal from the archive-scan lead (catalogue 334), naming Puig y Puig 1920 as the outstanding check. No target-specific intervention.
tools: Google Books in-volume search endpoint (jscmd=SearchWithinVolume2) and page-image endpoint (jscmd=click3)

solution.what: HathiTrust record 100676638 (Puig 1920) tried in curl and the built-in browser: Cloudflare challenge, not solved. archive.org: no copy.

Butllari de Catalunya (Fundació Noguera 2016), IFC 2024 Benedicto XIII volume, Cuella's Bulario IV, Suárez Fernández's Castilian documents, zaguan 2023 paper grepped for cifra/xifra/criptog: no mention of the ACB cipher letters.

Baucells i Reig 1978 (ACB Cisma d'Occident catalogue, PDF from the ACB site): codices and parchments only; the paper part (1,532 pieces) was uncatalogued; archivist Mas's note that Puig took Schism papers home 1920-30 and many were not returned.
Google Books full-view copy of Puig 1920 found (id CuOlkxWnk-EC, Wisconsin). Book pages and PDF were CAPTCHA-walled, but the in-volume search endpoint and signed page-image URLs answered.

In-volume search for cifra/clave/descifr: p. 466 n. 2 says italics mark the deciphered phrases and Puig rebuilt the key 'a fuerza de paciencia' from lines Climent left on docs. 1063, 461, 463; preface p. 2: 'los diez u once escritos con desconocida clave' deciphered. Appendix index lists 14 'Carta cifrada' items, 1399-1416.
Appendix pages of every cipher item fetched and checked for gaps and for what Puig left unread (page-by-page check by a subagent).

Found that Puig p. 475 carries an uncaptioned, sideways photogravure of the last page of XXXV (22 June 1400, doc. 1068), clear Latin alternating with cipher runs, with Puig's text of the same passage beside it; fetched at the maximum 1826 x 2500 px, rotated and deskewed (0.7 deg), lines segmented.

Known-plaintext alignment of two runs against Puig's italics: line 1-2 'cum duce Burgundie' after a dotted-V sign for the King of Aragon, line 8 'et presertim scribe qu...'. Consistent values u = cb (3x), e = delta (4x), s = T (2x), m = t (2x), d = double cross (2x), c/i = o, b = T-bar; one clash.

Attempted a sign-level transcription of the long run (lines 8-16, about 450 letters of known plaintext) at 3-4x with contrast enhancement: delta/d-with-mark/o/a and joined strokes cannot be separated consistently at this resolution; 'quo modo se habet' did not align. Stopped; recorded as blocked (illegible).

Second session. Tried for a sharper image of p. 475: Google Books serves 1826 x 2500 at most (w=4000 and zoom 4-6 give nothing larger); the second Google copy (wP0wAQAAMAAJ) is snippet view; HathiTrust still behind Cloudflare in curl; Claude in Chrome not connected; no other digitised copy found by web search.

Plate re-cut from the page, rotated, deskewed -0.7 deg by maximising the row-profile contrast, 26 line centres found from the smoothed ink profile; each cipher run cut into ~500-750 px strips and viewed at 3-5x with autocontrast, alongside Puig's text of p. 475-476.

Known-plaintext alignment over all cipher runs of the plate (lines 1-6, 8-17, 23-25), word by word against Puig's italics. One sign per letter emerges: a hook, b T-bar, c/i/o o, d double cross, e delta, f flagged sigma, g 4-shape, h 2-shape, l looped d, m footed epsilon, n, p inverted T, q double-barred upright, r upright, s T, t c', u/v cb, x alpha-shape; dotted V = King of Aragon (4x). The first session's clash was a misread of joined strokes.

Word-by-word tally (src/plate475_check.tsv): 148 words, 826 plaintext letters; 125 words confirmed sign by sign, 16 with 1-3 blurred signs, 7 illegible (line 4, underlined/overwritten in the original). 755/826 letters confirmed (91.4%; 96.3% of legible runs); no sign contradicts the key.

The key corrects Puig in three places: 'te sicudum' (line 4) is 'tenendum' (c' delta n delta n dcross cb m-sign; the clear text just before has 'in suspenso tenendum'); 'abique congerio' is 'absque congedio'; 'necesaria' is written 'necessaria'. Four separator groups (lambda/z signs) stand where Puig prints ';' or a dash and are not printed by him: read as null punctuation.

Write-up pass: line 24 (modis ... absque) re-read at 5x and transcribed sign by sign as seen, 58 signs, for the site's decipher replay. It showed that o is a double loop, distinct from the single o used for c and i; one tall stroke in 'istorum' unexplained.

Split under the one-key rule: the letters of Benedict's circle (Santa Cruz 1399, Jafet 1400, Exea 1408, Comuel 1415 and 1416), whose key is not shown to be his, each moved to its own entry (santacruz1399, jafet1400, exea1408, comuel1415, comuel1416), and the 1398 Vico line in an unknown key to vico1398; this entry keeps Benedict XIII's ten letters of 1399-1403.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): src/plate475_check.tsv (word-by-word check of the only ciphertext image, the p. 475 plate) as transcription; Puig's 1920 printed decipherment linked by its Google Books URL (no local text copy yet); key.md as key file.

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the entry's text in the repository is the p. 475 plate check, which builds Latin clauses; the ten letters are Puig's print (Google Books, blocked). Kept read for the plate only, with an excerpt note; fraction_read_source restated as the plate's sign-confirmed share.

outcome.method_basis: The text is Puig y Puig's printed decipherment (Pedro de Luna, 1920, appendix), found before the attempt; the project then rebuilt Puig's unprinted key by aligning his printed text against the p. 475 facsimile (external plaintext) and confirmed 91.4% of the plate's letters sign by sign.

texts.label: BnF fr. 3034 ff. 156r-157v, Bologna, 4 November 1529
texts.summary: Ambrogio Bizozola reports to Maximilian Sforza, then in France, that the Emperor's council has several times discussed dividing the state of Milan among the Duke of Savoy, the Marquises of Monferrato and Mantua and the Duke of Ferrara, and whether Duke Francesco would have to be satisfied. The Emperor is at the Certosa outside Bologna, with his entry the next day (Charles V entered Bologna on 5 November 1529); the letter also deals with misere Iulio, Trivulzio and Alessandro Attavante.

Re-read our 21 Sept transcription against the key: bars on 72/79, 3ᵈ split, 'tu' one glyph; several of our letters lumped distinct key shapes.

Compared each of the 98 glyphs with the cell of view 112 it matches (alignment.tsv): 86 key, 3 probable, 6 off page (Tomokiyo), 3 conflict (re[c]ognoissant has b, one s without an S cell, acompagne[z] = E3 or Z2).

George Lasry (PR #61): his 2022 CTTS project for the Henri IV-Brèves key, improved with Opus 5.5 in Oct 2026: full CTTS key (letters, comma-letter words, barred numbers, repeat sign s-), a second document in the key (two crops, 766 cipher elements, 763 valued) with French reading and English translation, and his decryption of the 10 Nov 1610 passage, agreeing with Dudout's reading.

Review on merging PR #61: verify.py passes (hashes, deterministic token alignment, links); the second s of recognoissant is Lasry's repeat sign s-, used ten times in the longer document, which closes one conflict (96/98 Marie glyphs supported); re[c]ognoissant stays a B1/C conflict; the table's M column has a/b/c/d-shaped signs while Lasry's CTTS labels a=M, b=C, c=S, d=P are glyph names, not facsimiles; 'm, = dict' checked on the assembled key image ('Dict - m,'), not a typo. system.summary: Two-tier cipher: a small sign over a base stroke (7, m, n, a, t, 4), with bracket-L signs for whole words.

system.notes: Two analyses disagree: R1133/7c gave one letter per column (fixed1519.json), R1130/4c a syllabary, upper = consonant, base = vowel (pairX/key.json); the factorised rebuild (syl_fact.py) learns the base tier only. distinct_symbols = column types in R1128.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE R1126-R1140 metadata and images; Vestigia searches Caprile (52) and Cistarelli (20); contact sheets. R1128 and R1129-R1135 are in the 1519 two-tier cipher.
Vestigia: 1519 cipher originals filed as 'a' with 'b'/'c' clear copies; ASMo inventory dates them to 1882. R1129-R1135 read at the time or in 1882.

R1130 (no. 4a) aligned with its 1882 decipherment 4c (pairX/): the 1519 cipher is syllabic, upper sign = consonant, base = vowel (7 none, m e, n o), bracket-L = CV syllables; about 20 values, held-out 16/18 against 8.1 shuffled. R1131/5b alignment failed (water stain).

R1128's 1519 two-tier system: R1133 transcribed in full (1327 columns) and aligned with its 1882 decipherment 7c; one letter per column, homophonic (c/7=o, m/n=r, x/7=t ...); bracket-L signs are nomenclator words ([d][s][&] = de vostra maesta).
Language-model anneal over the 1519 columns with 9 fixed values; R1128 (21% code words) not read.

Known keys on R1128 (knownkeys.py): pairX syllabary from R1130/4c covers 32 % of columns, LM -3.22 vs -3.24 for a random key with the same values; fixed1519 covers 13 %; key1519_ann is fitted on R1128 (no evidence).

R1128: factorised syllabary (column = consonant of the upper sign + vowel of the base) trained by hard EM on R1130/4c and R1133/7c (syl_fact.py); base tier learns cleanly (7 = none, m = e, n = o) but the upper tier does not (most uppers map to '' as often as to a consonant); R1128 beam decode scores LM -2.92/char against -2.41 for the same tables permuted, i.e. worse than the control: not read.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from caprile1519, which had joined three ciphers of the same ASMo file: the 1519 two-tier cipher (caprile1519), the 1520-21 sign cipher (caprile1520) and Cistarelli's figure cipher (cistarelli1520). This profile keeps the documents and steps of the 1519 two-tier cipher (R1128, with R1129-R1135 as key material) only.

Method checked after George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separated key and text: stays not solved, because the tables rebuilt from the sibling decipherments give no signal on R1128, so no key for this letter was obtained.

outcome.method_basis: R1128 has no decipherment; the 1519 tables rebuilt from the sibling decipherments (R1133/7c, R1130/4c) give no signal on it against random-key and permuted controls, and the factorised syllabary rebuild failed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: No column of R1128 is claimed as read (knownkeys.py r1128, syl_fact.py).
outcome.notes: Attempted, open. The key material exists: R1129-R1135 in the same cipher were deciphered in 1882 (b/c copies) or interlined, so the gap is work (a careful transcription of R1132 against 6b and R1131 against 5b), not an outside blocker. Split 14 Oct 2026 from caprile1519, which also held the 1520-21 sign cipher (now caprile1520) and Cistarelli's figures (now cistarelli1520).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of about 49 invented signs for Italian letters, no word division, crossed ligatures for s and q.
system.notes: Key values in targets/caprile1520/key21.json (majority) and key21_counts.json; V1921 values in read_v1921.py. The 1519 two-tier cipher (caprile1519) and Cistarelli's figure cipher (cistarelli1520) are other systems with their own entries.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE R1126-R1140 metadata and images; Vestigia searches Caprile (52) and Cistarelli (20); contact sheets. The 1520-21 sign cipher is in R1136, R1138, R1139 and Vestigia 1920, 1921.
Somogyi 2025 (Scriptorium VI) prints decipherments of the 16 Feb 1521 postscript (R1138 and V1920).
A subagent transcribed the 1520-21 sign cipher in five texts (2,278 signs, 49 labels): R1139, R1136, R1138, V1920, V1921.
Monotone EM alignment of V1920 against Somogyi's text from a uniform start.
Ciphertext-only homophonic anneal over the 1520-21 corpus with a 16th-c. Italian 4-gram model and a unigram penalty; fragments like scritti, regno, Ungaria.
EM alignment seeded by the anneal key: 714 letters aligned on V1920 and R1138, 90% consistent; homophonic key.
Key applied to R1139 and R1136: phrases read (il custode, tornato governator, deli danari del suo, voler andar in Italia; questo episcopato, de Ungaria, tal debito).

R1139 second pass for the quotation list (30 Sept): signs re-checked on the image, three transcription errors corrected, key21 counts + it-cinquecento beam search proposals checked sign by sign; L05-L07 now continuous ('li go fato moto deli danari del suo de[b]ito, come mi dise messere [Alfonso]. Lui m'ha resposto, dice de voler andar in Italia'), L08-L09 in phrases; L01-L03 still phrases (r1139_pass2.txt).

Vestigia records of the Caprile/Cistarelli files listed for the cipher flag ('titkosirás'): only V1853, V1874, V1876, V1919-V1922; no further letter uses the 1520-21 key. V1921 (no. 12) was the only one never reported as read.
V1921's six cipher runs re-checked sign by sign on v1921_2.jpg: L01 'z t' is one crossed z (z+), L02 'm p' is m+ with a looped descender, L03 'x t' is x+, L04 HH is ff; 166 signs (v1921_signs.txt).
Mechanical decrypt with key21.json treating the lone o as a null (decrypt21_raw.txt) gave only 'ogni cosa', 'il custode', 'Agria era data', 'suo signore'.

Lone o as a null ruled out: context forces o = h ('ha', 'ch'a', 'che') and o = u ('qui', 'suo', 'quantunque'), matching the EM counts (o 28, h 13, u 10) and V1920 'che' = PHI o y; oo = b ('beni', R1139 'debito'); z+ = q and x+ = q; EL = f ('oficio'); K = et (M).

V1921 read in context: 'il custode e stato quel ch'a persuaso ... a dire che Agria era data d'anti il suo advento, e[t] che lo toglia in oficio ... suo signore ... sopra soi beni, quantunque siano in reg[no]'. 160/166 signs read as sense (96.4 %, 88.0 % at grade C); 6 unread (two minims, two stray signs, two at the torn edge).
it-cinquecento order-5 model: reading -1.79 per char, the same letters shuffled with word breaks kept -4.12 (20 runs); best_language ranks it-modern first.
Grade-M words not resolved: 'dicixe' (L01, disse?) and 'revelta' (L02, rivela?); 'regno' at the page edge not legible.
R1136 L10 'x p a ss m+ f o/o' = questo shows x + looped p is one q-sign (xp); V1921 L06 'quantunque' then needs no stray sign: 161/166 (97.0 %).

beam21.py: beam decoder over key21_counts priors plus the V1921 values (lone o = h/u/null, oo = b, z+/x+ = q, EL/AMP = p/f, K = t/et), it-cinquecento order 5 without spaces, off-key letters allowed at a penalty and flagged; run on R1139 and R1136 (beam21_out.txt).

R1139 pass 3: phrases checked on the crops and regraded; 'debito' now at key values (oo = b), 'gubernator', 'messer Alfonso', 'Agria in o[f]icio'; 83.8 % of decoded letters inside claimed phrases (regrade21.py), mostly M; L01 and L03 still phrase-level.

R1136 pass 3: 'transferse a Buda il custode', 'in oficio questo episcopato, et a epso custode', 'dicono esser conclusi', 'potra far al custo[d]e per questa via de Ungaria sopra il suo', 'in questo loco niente', 'tal debito'; 59.4 % inside claimed phrases; crops disagree with the single transcription in L03, L05-L08.

R1136 second transcription from the original image at native resolution (r1136_pass4.txt): 11 of 12 lines changed, e.g. L03 TH -> lone o, CE x p -> c xp; L05 'U? K m t o SL o f QB n f QB QB' -> 'U q f B QB B n t QB'; L04/L06 o+ (crossed lone o).

R1136 pass 4: new values o+ = s, D = b/x, plain c = o; new phrases 'Lactantio, ho inteso, qual', 'congregati ... Bachiensis, che ogni episcopa-', 'l'altro in titolo, et a questo modo excludera', 'vostra Excelentia, quel si-'; 66.9 % of decoded letters inside claimed phrases (was 59.4 %).

R1139 second pass on the unread stretches at native resolution (r1139_pass4.txt): Z+ = q 'quando', Zp = q 'qual', xp 'quel'; L01 'il custode, quando a Buda, come i' scrisi, e tornato gubernator de', L03 'credo dia ogni ato e qualche cosa a le ma[n] di [l]o custode; per anchora si n'e in-', L09 've ne daro; vedro quel mi dara, e il tuto [re]portaro'; 88.7 % (was 83.8 %). system.notes: Runs such as 2201 che, 2205 ci, 2211 di, 2221 fi, 2230 l, 2231 l', 2232 la and 2082-2084 del, dell', della are alphabetical; the runs themselves are scattered. R9586/R9588 use a second code and have their own entry (r9586).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE session cookie, Claude Code with Opus 5, problem posed with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched metadata for DECODE R9542-R9590 through the API and the 28 images of the target and of box 2317/2337 siblings with the shared cookie.
Web search for a printed or published decipherment of the 1816-19 Castelcicala despatches.
Transcribed 331 groups from R9553 p.1, R9582 and R9585; identified the recipient (Circello) and the code name (Cifra della Segreteria di Stato).
Compared with the box 2317 record R9549 that DECODE suggests holds the plaintexts: its cipher uses a different code (frequent groups 441, 486, 563, 1144; range to ~1999).
Checked the decrypted box 2337 siblings: 1850s-60s telegrams and letters in other codes.
Frequency and repeat count: 208 distinct groups in 331 over a ~2,500-group code, repeated multi-group phrases; too little text for a ciphertext-only attack.
DECODE API metadata for R9532-R9591 and 100 page images fetched with the session cookie.
Web search for a printed decipherment of Castelcicala's Paris despatches.
Neighbouring 'Decrypted' records of busta 2337 checked for the same code: R9569, R9571 and R9589 (1823) share it and carry interlinear glosses; R9590 (1830) is another code.
All 27 records transcribed from full-resolution crops by two sub-agents (9,400 main-code groups); R9566 p3 found to carry a contemporary interlinear decipherment.
Glosses aligned group by group: about 110 values, syllabic and word-level, homophonic; 5-figure groups fall where the gloss has nothing (nulls); local alphabetical runs noticed.
Key extended by hand from repeated contexts (1714 = i, 2318 = ta and ~50 weaker values); 46% of groups get a value.
Per-group candidate scoring with the it-modern 5-gram LM over known neighbours (length bonus, then PMI): no discrimination between candidates.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 4482 tokens, 260 types, it-modern order 4: reading -1.831 per letter; random keys -2.472 (z 7.4); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -1.84 (mean -1.86, z 2.1); annealer on the real text -1.811. Verdict: underdetermined.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from castelcicala1816, which had included R9586 and R9588, two Castelcicala letters in a different code (values about 100-1100), with the despatches in the Segreteria di Stato code. This profile keeps the Segreteria di Stato code (25 documents) only.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per-record transcriptions transcripts/R*.txt (with the contemporary glosses) and cipher/R*.txt; decryption reading_partial.txt (apply.py partial decode, converted from Latin-1 to UTF-8, text unchanged), and the interlinear glosses for R9566, R9569, R9571, R9589; key.tsv. Most letters have only a partial decode: no full decryption exists.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). reading_partial.txt read letter by letter: about half the groups have no value, with unread groups between nearly every pair of known words (docs/_check_reading.py: 2 of 24 sentences clean); no sentence of the 23 despatches without a full gloss can be built. system.summary: The Grand Chiffre de 1691: a numeric nomenclator of 587 groups for letters, CV syllables, word stems, whole words and nulls.
system.sibling_key: Bazeries' reconstruction of the Grand Chiffre (../feuquieres/grand_chiffre_1691.tsv, 587 entries, 91 blank), used as the key.
system.notes: Six groups printed above 587 in 1819 and one damaged glyph stay unread; about a hundred groups fall on entries Bazeries left blank and are read from context.

prior_solution.where: Bazeries 1893 printed L1 and L3 in clear and parts of L2 and L4; L5-L7 never printed in clear

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: segment.py (dynamic-programming word segmenter over a period lexicon)

solution.what: Fetched MDZ hOCR and IIIF page images of Mémoires de Catinat t. II.
Tokenised the figures from the hOCR, dropping specks, running heads and show-through glyphs; split into seven letters.
Applied Bazeries' 1893 Grand Chiffre table and segmented the output with a period lexicon.
Aligned the decode of L1 and L3 with Bazeries' clear text: 98.1% and 99.1% of characters.
Checked 137 doubtful stretches on page crops; 7 OCR errors and 3 dates corrected.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE metadata and full-resolution images of R8490-R8497.
CSP Foreign vol. 21 pt 4, May-June 1588: calendars SP 77 Cobham letters only, not Harley 287.
Tested the catalogue's key record R8497 (f. 187).
Read 'in all LVZLTL' as ARMADA/ARMATA from context.
Found DECODE sibling records R8481, R8488, R8489, R8493 marked Decrypted, with interlinear decipherments.
Rebuilt about 20 letters of the alphabet from the f. 75 and f. 89 glosses; cross-checked with the cypher-7e session's key.
Applied the key to ff. 80r, 88r, 92r; shared s/t and r/y signs and unidentified signs stop a full reading.

Second pass with cypher-7e's harley287 key (narrow/wide caret = s/t): sign copies from close crops of ff. 80r, 88r, 92r; the caret forms and the l/p/h loop signs could not be told apart, so only context guesses ('expences', 'of letters').

Third pass: sign inventory by eye at full resolution from about 60 glossed words on ff. 75, 79, 89 (signs.tsv); separates p/l/h/m/w; shows s/t, r/y, o/a and l/t share signs; glossed code numbers 7, 10, 15, 16.
Applied the inventory to ff. 80r, 88r, 92r: 'armada(s)', 'to these termes', 'the action', '15' = Parma, 'captain'; most runs still unread because of polyphonic and unglossed signs.

Candidate-set word solver (solve.py): each sign a set of letters from signs.tsv, readings scored against a 1588 CSP Foreign word list with Elizabethan spelling normalised and up to 1-2 edits; over 22 transcribed runs it confirms these/terms, armada, action, captain, letters, charge; long runs on ff. 88 and 92 find no words, pointing to transcription errors.

Solver loop 1: re-read f.80/f.88 runs at 2x full resolution against solver candidates; 'haven' (f.80 and f.88, fixes c=a and L=e) and 'so forwarde in the action that he promised Q[ueen]' (f.80) confirmed; f.88: 'have promised the haven of ...' to Parma.

Solver loops on deskewed lines of ff. 88, 92, 96v with leads from harley287 READING and CSP Foreign 1588 (Semple to Scotland): Italians, Antonio, deliverd, divers, number of, within France, servants, priests, Portugals(?), Bruges(?).
Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 100 tokens, 22 types, en-modern order 4: reading -4.345 per letter; Verdict: too short.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the sign-level runs (runs.txt; f. 96v sign copies in reading_f96v.md) and the consolidated and per-folio readings (READING.md, reading_*.md); key = signs.tsv. Missing: sign transcription of the f. 97r runs, and no full transcription of the clear English of the four letters (decryptions give the cipher passages with their clear context only).

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). READING.md and the per-folio readings were read: the cipher passages yield isolated words and short phrases with grades between ellipses ("22 is so forwarde in the action that he promised Q to ... 27 to begin the ..."); only the surrounding clear English reads. docs/_check_reading.py: READING.md 28/58 sentences clean, most of them clear text; per-folio files 0-37%. All four letters relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> not solved; fraction_read 0.35 (estimated) -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b13). No decipherment, clear copy or print found again (neighbouring records R8491, R8493, R8494 checked; f. 97r of R8496 is blank). The clear of ff. 80r-80v, 92r and 96v transcribed as running text from the 7,200 px DECODE images in strips (f. 88r re-checked, f. 96r not transcribed); the cipher runs re-read at 0.5-1.0x (b13_crop.py). Relabelled (texts/R8490_corrections.tsv, texts/runs_corrected.txt): f. 80r AVmATA/AVmAT -> AV7ATA/AV7AT (7-form e, not ∽): treaties, treaty of [?Breda] (not armada); l. 18 ϸcAAUӾLA hostages; the l. 19-20 run divided into eight barred words (A··VA⊥ surety).

Partial readings with modern English (texts/R8490_reading.md ... R8496_en.md), every cipher word graded: plain only with all signs at their glossed values, [?word] for one doubtful sign or one solver edit, the 21 Sept guesses (Rain, spoil, Portugals, noblemen, Roper, Iohn) withdrawn to holes. Clean share (b13_score.py, en; E=1 maps Elizabethan spellings): R8490 0.114/0.514, R8492 0.0/0.118, R8495 0.0/0.074, R8496 0.2/0.35. All four stay decoded, not read: only R8490's hostages passage and f. 80v run build cipher sentences.

Method restored: key obtained by the glossed sibling letters in Harley 287 (key recovered based on adjacent plaintext); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

texts.label: R8490, ff. 80-81, Ostend 5 May 1588
texts.summary: Lord Cobham, one of Elizabeth's commissioners for the Bourbourg peace talks with Parma's deputies, writes to Walsingham from Ostend in clear English with short cipher passages; Julio Romeo, Cristophero Mondragon and Doctor Dale are named in clear, and the cipher words concern hostages, the haven and the armada.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8490_reading.md, texts/R8490_en.md, texts/R8490_corrections.tsv, texts/R8490-R8496_reread_log.md): the clear of ff. 80r-80v transcribed as running text; the "armada(s)" of 21 Sept is "treaties" / "treaty of [?Breda]" (the third sign is the 7-form e, not ∽ m), so the hostages passage reads (Touching hostages, yt ys honorable for [7] to [...] their surety to these termes, as usuall yn all treaties ...) and so does the f. 80v run (22 hath a desire to retourne from theym); the runs of ll. 8-11 and 31-34 keep holes in most words. Clean share 0.114 (0.514 with Elizabethan spellings mapped). Blocker: no-key-material (unglossed signs W, the square, codes 22 and 27; polyphonic signs).

texts.label: R8492, f. 88, undated 1588
texts.summary: The densest cipher of the four letters: captain Montgomery has lately gone into Scotland with 40 men, a haven has been promised to Parma (code 15), Italians are arriving, and other Scotsmen are coming; the clear lower half reports Parma's commissioners and 80 sail with saddles, bridles, boots and spurs.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8492_reading.md, texts/R8492_en.md): the f. 88r runs re-checked on the image; only the haven, there, Italians, Antonio and a few probable words read; the 21 Sept guesses (of Rain, spoil, Naples as certain) withdrawn. Blocker: no-key-material (signs K, ɔ and the polyphonic set glossed nowhere).

texts.label: R8495, ff. 92-93, 27 May 1588
texts.summary: News from Cobham to Walsingham: the Armada still at Lisbon, Gonzaga, 200 mariners at Sluys; the cipher passages mention men imprisoned in Bruges, letters, the ancient of Newport and Irish noblemen.
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R8495_reading.md, texts/R8495_en.md): the clear news of f. 92r transcribed as running text (Armada at Lisbon, Gonzaga at Watten, armour to Cambrai, Casimir, Guise); the ten cipher lines give scattered probable words only ([?Bruges], [?charge], [?letters], Newport, in [?prison]). Blocker: no-key-material.

plaintext.source: No decipherment known.

transcription.source: David Scheers, PDF 'Remarks devil's handwriting' (16 Oct 2026)
transcription.notes: Woodcut; strokes dropped and added in printing.

system.summary: Seven lines of invented-looking signs (31-40 classes) in a 1539 woodcut presented as the Devil's answer; system and language not established.
system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: If the signs are Ethiopic the text may be a Ge'ez note rather than a cipher.

prior_solution.where: Ambrogio's own account on f. 213r (1539), printed and translated by Houston and Rojas, Maya Decipherment, 6 Apr 2024, who still treated the signs as a possible alphabet; no decipherment anywhere.

conditions.human_role: Supplied the image, insisted on continuing, and forwarded David Scheers's PDF which identified the target and gave a transcription.

solution.what: Searched the repository, catalogue.json and the web (Schmeh's Encrypted Book List, Cipher Mysteries) for the image or a description of it.

Compared the signs with rendered charts of Samaritan, Phoenician, Ethiopic, Glagolitic, Tibetan, Old Italic, Old Hungarian, Georgian and Armenian; Ethiopic fits best (arch letters, ተ, ገ, ለ, አ, ። and numeral bars), Samaritan second; the commonest sign has no clear counterpart.
Tested the image rotated 180 degrees as upside-down Latin script.
Segmented the glyphs automatically and transcribed 174 signs into provisional classes from contact sheets.
Simple substitution into Latin (CLTK Caesar/Cicero/Sallust quadgrams), 12 annealing restarts, one-to-one key on the commonest classes.
Same solver on three shuffles of the transcription: shuffled -12.46 to -12.62 per quadgram against real -12.86, so the Latin fit is no better than chance.
Scheers PDF identified the target as Ambrogio 1539 f. 212v (Devil's Handwriting); searches confirm no published decipherment.
Compared further scripts (Hangul, kana with 90-degree rotation, Brahmi, Batak, Rejang, Hanunoo, Canadian syllabics, Tifinagh, Armenian, mirror and 180-degree readings).
Simple substitution of own transcription into Hebrew, Croatian, Russian, Amharic consonant rows, Latin and Italian, both directions.
Ethiopic visual consonant values with free vowels, scored against Italian and Latin; z = 0.27 / 0.33 against permuted values.
Scheers transcription, simple substitution into Latin and Italian: beats 15 shuffles (z about 4.5 and 2.8).
Bigram (Markov-1) surrogates of the Scheers transcription score as well or better, so the excess over shuffles comes from sign-pair habits, not language.
Calibration on 153 letters of Caesar: plain substitution solved (LM -9.0 to -9.7); with 6 homophones (25 signs) not solved by the same or a frequency-penalised homophonic solver.
Calibrated homophonic solver (C, 5-gram, 24 restarts x 3M): solves 6/6 held-out Latin and 6/6 held-out Italian 153-letter 31-sign controls (88-100%), scores -1.62 to -2.12.

Same solver on the Devil's text (Scheers and own transcription, both directions): Latin -2.37/-2.50, Italian -2.44/-2.45, inside the shuffle range -2.42 to -2.52; Hebrew, Spanish, French, German, Greek, Arabic, Amharic rows, vowel-dropped and vowel-merged Italian/Latin also at shuffle level.
17 Italian/Latin cribs from the question at every offset (15,970 placements, 2,449 consistent) with the calibrated solver; best -2.50, nowhere near solved-control scores (-1.6 to -2.1).

Machine segmentation (183 glyphs) and HOG clustering, then glyph-by-glyph labels: transcription_v3.txt, 161 signs, 38 classes; agrees with the first transcription. Calibrated solver on it: Italian -2.31, Latin -2.38, shuffles -2.34 to -2.37.

Abugida model (one consonant per sign family, one vowel per mark class) calibrated on Italian syllabary controls (3/4 solved); on the Devil's text Italian and Latin, both directions, -2.51 to -2.55 against shuffles -2.49 to -2.54.

Amadi's Letere diaboliche (c. 1588, redrawn by Scheers): 31 demon-named signs matching the woodcut's sign set; first letters of the names as values give no words, z = 1.35 (Italian) / 0.63 (Latin) against 2,000 random reassignments.

Read Ambrogio's own account (ff. 212r-213r, archive.org scan): the conjurer was later killed by peasants 'with as many iron tridents as the invoked Amon had drawn in his characters' (tot ferris tridentibus, quot invocatus Amon in suis characteribus effinxerat); the commonest sign (sideways E with long bar) is a trident, so the source's only meaning for the characters is a pictorial omen, consistent with the absence of any linguistic plaintext.

Houston and Rojas (2024) checked: they transcribe and translate the f. 212v-213r passage including the trident sentence and call the signs a 'pitchfork script', but treat them as a possible alphabet; the omen reading and the null tests are new here.

validation.notes: no reading: not a cipher; the tests are calibrated null results recorded in NOTES (matched controls and shuffles), not a key to validate

outcome.method_basis: Ambrogio's own account (f. 213r) gives the characters one meaning, a pictorial omen: the conjurer was later killed by peasants 'with as many iron tridents as the invoked Amon had drawn in his characters'; the commonest sign is a trident, and no letter-substitution plaintext exists in eleven languages under three transcriptions, with solvers that solve matched controls.
outcome.notes: Not a cipher on the evidence of the source and the tests: the characters depict tridents (an omen of the conjurer's death), not a text. A code of whole words or a meaningless pseudo-script cannot be excluded in principle; no linguistic content was found.

Deciphered here from the leaf; Scheurer (1969) prints the same text.

Tested paired-D and paired-D/CE null hypotheses on opening and six-line draft; no sustained readable output. Shortened scores are not direct evidence for null status.

Tested many-to-one French substitution on six-line compound-stroke variant, penalizing divergence from average model next-letter distribution. Produced fragments but no coherent or verified reading; no plaintext accepted.
Extended provisional transcript to sixteen main lines: 804 draft labels, 23 distinct; insertion omitted.
Full-text compound and null variants produced sustained French fragments; prior short probes failed.

Saved reproducible inferred key and uncorrected candidate French reading. Provisional address grand maistre de France cross-check supports nulls; full image audit, insertion and date remain unresolved.

Standard checker measures corrected body plus both insertions at 726 signs, 27 draft labels; aliases prevent treating the latter as historical alphabet size.
Targeted searches on the newly read titles and apparent date found no matching edition or confirmed year; no external plaintext used.

Native-image review distinguishes the left-extending bar in lextreme from plain plus/g. It still has only one occurrence, so x remains M. Native crops confirm the anomalous literal forms; no silent emendation. All main lines, both insertions, address and clear closing accounted for.

solution.what: Read Antal et al., HistoCrypt 2023 (the published description): box 636 holds six 1744 digit-cipher documents (five French, one German; one from Maria Theresa), no plaintext; keys in the fonds and the HHStA/Hungarian keys the authors tried do not match.

Looked for images: HCPortal (local harvest to id 1499 plus a live scan of ids 1500-2032: nothing from the Slovak National Archives' Esterházy fonds), DECODE (no Slovak National Archives records). Extracted the only published image, Figure 6 of the paper.
Transcribed the cipher block of Figure 6: a letter headed 'Moscau ce 5e d'octobre 1744' to 'Votre Majesté', 11 lines, 176 groups.
157 distinct of 176 groups; values 7-1737 and 3018-3297, spread evenly over the hundreds; six groups under 100. A code of about 2,000 entries with almost every group seen once.

Opened the HHStA Chiffrenschlüssel key records of 1740-1746 on DECODE: R1594 (German circular 1745, values to 1500), R1597/R1596 (French circular 1745, encipher and decipher tables, values 101-1355), R1595 (circular table 100-1499), R1593 (1746 multi-table), R1562 (1743, values under 1000), R1574 (1740 German), R1644, R1691. None reaches the 1500-1737 and 3000-3297 values of the sample.

Web search for a reading of box 636 or the Moscow letter: none. Found the Dorotheum lot of 17 Dec 2024 (Maria Theresa to Esterházy, Vienna 31 July 1744), described as a three-digit word code whose key copy is in the Austrian State Archives.
Ciphertext-only attack not run: 176 groups from a code of about 2,000 entries, 89% of them distinct, give nothing for a solver to fit. Needs the other five documents or the 1744 key.

Also ruled out: R2233 (1801 small homophonic system), the 1790s Orange name key R2240, Dutch codebooks R1035 (1803) and R1891 (1798), and siblings R2236/R2237/R2239 in the same old inventory number.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R2238 record and its three page images with the session cookie; page 3 carries the cipher, pages 2 and 1 are clear.
Transcribed the cipher passage (128 groups, one interlinear insertion) and the clear context.
Grand Chiffre du Stadhouder (R1024, 1782) via the DECODE key transcription, direct lookup.
Grand Chiffre with the additive Tableau (11 rows x 17 values) from every row and column start, scored on syllable fit of dot-joined groups.
R2240 Orange key (letters 1-100, names 100-6006); R1035 and R1891 Dutch codebooks; siblings R2236, R2237, R2239 in the same inventory number.
Fagel family key sets NA 1.10.29 inv. 1257-1267 (DECODE R2842-R2852), one interior page each: all Dutch-vocabulary codes.
Grand Chiffre R1024 with every constant offset -2600..+2600, scored on syllable fit: best offsets give nonsense.

Swept all 6,396 DECODE key records for keys dated 1790-1815 (149) and French-language keys from 1780 (30): apart from those already tested, none is Dutch or Orange; the BL Add MS 32257/32264/32292 French keys are intercepted French government ciphers. Web search found no printed decipherment and no KHA cipher key online.

Queried the current KHA A31 online inventory. DECODE's old inv. nr. 337 no longer corresponds to the modern catalogue. The target belongs contextually in A31-2306-2308 (Batavian compensation negotiations, 1802-1804), especially files 2307/2308; adjacent A31-2292-2293 includes Fagel, D'Yvoy, Van Olden and a catalogue note on fl. 500,000 for the French.

Contemporary sources identify the negotiation, the opposing plenipotentiaries, the proposed five-million-guilder settlement, and Fagel and D'Yvoy's short German journey immediately after the letter. This strongly constrains the subject but does not uniquely determine the 128 code groups.

Checked DECODE transcription views and searched Robert Fagel correspondence while logged in. R2238 and R2236 have no contributed transcription; R2237 is decrypted but uses a visibly different small-number system. No other Robert Fagel correspondence record supplies a parallel text.

Inspected BL Add MS 32264 candidates R8963/R8964 (French Cypher 1798-1799), R8984 (1805), and adjacent records R8965-R8983. Their ranges are about 1-750 or 1-250, or they are short correspondence specimens; none matches the verified four-digit groups 1531, 1731, and 2510.
Checked the current Nationaal Archief catalogue for Fagel 1.10.29 inv. nr. 1909. The relevant Robert Fagel series is marked PHYSICAL and exposes no digital object or IIIF scan.

Searched the complete OCR of Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken IV (1908), including documents 790-804 and 813. The 18 June 1804 letter is not printed, but the edition confirms the exact compensation/bribery context and prints later Robert Fagel reports from Paris.

The current Royal Collections catalogue identifies KHA A31-902, a separate one-packet file of papers concerning ciphers used at court, broadly dated to the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries. It has no online scans and is the strongest physical target for the missing 1804 key.

outcome.method_basis: The 128 code groups on DECODE R2238 were transcribed, and every candidate Orange, Fagel and DECODE key of 1780-1815 (the Grand Chiffre R1024 with its tableau and renumberings, R2240, R1035, R1891, R2842-R2852) was ruled out; no key or clear copy was located.
outcome.notes: Key not located. The code (about 2500 groups) is too large for 128 groups of text to yield a unique exact reading without the key. Best physical target: KHA A31-902 (court cipher papers), followed by A31-2307/2308 (and A31-2292/2293) plus NA 1.10.29 no. 1909, asking for the codebook or a duplicate/deciphered copy of the 18 June 1804 letter.

texts.label: Feuquières to Catinat, Pignerol, 25 Jan 1691
texts.summary: Feuquières acknowledges Catinat's letter of the 24th and sets out the plan for the surprise of Veillane (Avigliana): the enemy will not defend it seriously, he cannot see how to get the eighty horse to Sant'Ambrogio, and he will attack at two points and keep the dragoons from escaping. It matches Catinat's 'Mémoire pour l'entreprise de Veillane' of 19 Jan; printed in cipher in the 1819 Mémoires de Catinat, t. II pp. 283-284.
texts.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (1691 French; the fr word list knows the period spelling, so the plain share is a bar too): the sweep scored texts/feuquieres1691_decryption.md with its header and commentary (plain 0.469, explicit 0.75). The reading alone, texts/feuquieres1691_reading.md: plain 0.545 (6/11), explicit 0.545 (6/11), hole rate 0.123. The five failing sentences carry three to six unread groups each (9, 19, 54, 122, 132, 257, 271, 292, 333, 353, singletons or doubletons of the petit chiffre with no value in either printed letter) plus supplied words ([par], [À]). The story is clear (Veillane, the 80 horse for Saint-Ambroise, the two roads, the dragoons), but under the bar on both measures: decoded, not read. Not workable here: no further text in this code is known; the original is at the SHD (A1 1079).

texts.summary: Louvois tells d'Herleville, governor of Pignerol, that the King permits him to demand the contribution of the country of Mondovì and, if he sees fit, to exempt it and let the inhabitants raze the citadel, and awaits news of his enterprise on Villefranche. Printed in cipher with its contemporary 'traduction' in the 1819 Mémoires de Catinat, t. I pp. 140-142; the alignment of the two gave the key.

system.summary: French homophonic cipher of the 1560s for German affairs (Tomokiyo's reconstructed table): two to four signs per letter, a few code words and nulls.

diacritics.note: Crossed and barred strokes distinguish signs (four cross shapes, ⊢ = q, ⊣ = r, + = o); the looped y-shape serves both s and p in the contributed reading.

system.doubled_letters: eight doubled-letter signs (ee ff ii ll mm nn rr ss), and pp = ff
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo, Cryptiana frencheastern.htm, 'French Ciphers for German (and Eastern) Affairs': key reconstructed for this volume.
system.notes: All 44 pages are in one key (one-key rule checked from the contributed key.tsv: one table, inferred values added). contributed/data/key.tsv has 95 entries (72 from Tomokiyo's table, 23 inferred): 12 word codes, 8 doubled-letter signs, 20 named null groups. Sign names are the contributor's; key in contributed/data/key.tsv.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo published the reconstructed key for this volume (Cryptiana frencheastern.htm) but no reading of the passages; the volume holds one contemporary decipherment (view 23 right) of the 15 Nov 1567 letter. Contributor's prior-work check found no earlier reading.

conditions.human_role: Contributed result: Harumi-Matsuba's account (created 19 Oct 2026) reports that a person chose the target and decided to publish; transcription, decoding and checks were by Claude and OpenAI Codex. In this project the result was checked by Claude (Opus 5.5) at Daniel Bourdeau's request.

solution.what: Contributor took Tomokiyo's reconstructed table (Cryptiana frencheastern.htm) as the key and named its signs (key.tsv); values for signs not in the table and nulls inferred from context (16 = ce, ꝭs = t, ρ = e, ꝑꝑ = ff).

Contributor: Claude transcribed 44 pages (822 lines, 29,707 signs) from BnF IIIF line crops; disagreements with Codex runs checked on enlarged crops by Codex and Claude Sonnet, corrected only where both agreed.

Contributor: 1000 shuffled keys per page scored by trigram French-likeness; none reaches the true key on any page. Independent Codex second transcription agrees 85.0-93.6% by value (lowest run per page).
Contributor: mechanical decode of every page and line-by-line conjectural readings of five letters (READING.en.md); most lines marked inferred (word division, supplied spelling, s/p choice).

Project re-measure (measure.py): contributed key re-applied by our own decoder; fr-1530-despatches LM -2.37 to -3.42 per char against -4.38 to -5.31 for the best of 200 shuffled keys per page (0 of 8,800 reach the true key); lexical coverage 81.0% of decoded letters in French words against 27.6% for shuffled keys and 90.3% for clean French.

Calibration on the contemporary decipherment (view 23 right), read here by eye: 1,000 of 1,193 letters (83.8%) of the decipherment matched by the contributed decode of view 22 right; 98 of 182 words of 3+ letters intact. A code group read SAXE where the decipherment has the duke of Wirtemberg; palatin missing.

Spot check on the Gallica images (views 22 and 99): view 22 right lines c01 and c03 compared sign by sign, 40/40 and 25 of 26 signs consistent with the contributed names, one not confirmed at this resolution; view 23 left found to carry about 17 further cipher lines of the 15 Nov 1567 letter, not in the contributed transcription.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Harumi-Matsuba's per-page transcriptions and mechanical decodes (contributed/data/), the line-by-line readings of five letters (READING.en.md) and the contemporary decipherment of view 23 right (calib_v023r.txt); view 23 left (15 Nov 1567, second cipher page) is not transcribed

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the 23 decoded_*.txt files are unspaced mechanical output (0-17% of sentences clean, docs/_check_reading.py) and READING.en.md was read through: f. 79r and f. 94r build into French sentences with scattered holes (kept read, reviewed B, those pages only); f. 39r-v, f. 100r and f. 158r have "..." holes in most lines. 21 letters relabelled decoded, not read; the two letters with a read first page kept read for that page. fraction_read 0.997 -> 0.056 (estimated).

Applied key 1: paolo, di madonna, madonna (twice), a Lugo read cleanly; the long runs on lines 7 and 11 and the line-4 run did not.
Meister 1902 p. 50 prints the key; Somogyi 2016 reproduces it; Guasti's Albizzi commissions and other sources do not print the letters.
Fetched siblings R3755 (Responsive 3 no. 21), R3756 (no. 91), R3757 (no. 92) and R3753; placed the letter in Galeotto's Urbino mission of Feb 1424/25.

Read the three unglossed long runs sign by sign with glosses as seeds and key for alignment: MADONNA [È] PURE FEMINA E SOSPETOSA (fixed by two O signs five apart), PARENTI [E] CITADINI, ACOMANDINO A LUI.
Subagent harvest of sibling runs to test the new sign values; cut off twice by usage limits.
Checked new values against Gabbrielli's null row: q confirmed null (run C reread without the S), ɤ shown to be an A he misfiled, +o distinct from his o+ null.
Tested new values on siblings: ɤ = A on no. 91 (mandato); 9 = N, +o = O, ô = T on no. 21 (andarono, tante e tali). ‖ = T, # = I, ᴗ = C, π = S, ʓ = S rest on no. 171 alone.
Re-transcribed the clear text from line strips and produced a final continuous reading; word signs ■⊡ (il Papa?, from Gabbrielli's mark), E (ella?) and ≠ (il Conte) read from context.

George Lasry noted DECODE R3754 should be marked Decrypted (an interlinear decryption exists) and that siblings such as R3755 could give the full key, to be uploaded only after checking the key is not elsewhere in the collection. Not yet done.

Checked for a fuller key before extending: Gabbrielli vol. 1 frames 58-3 (key 1), 58-4 (key 2, Carlo Fibindacci commissarius: other values, not this cipher), 58-5/58-6 (keys 3-4, Latin syllabic); Meister 1902 and Somogyi 2016 print only key 1; DECODE holds Gabbrielli's volume as key records R5687-R5698 (1424 frames R5687-R5690), not linked to R3754-R3757, with nothing beyond key 1.
Re-read Gabbrielli's key 1 from the film at full size: ▽ is his E (not D), ⊓̍ his second I, 8̊ his S, ô his T, # his second L, plain 9 his B; the NOTES tabulation corrected.

Transcribed the glossed cipher runs of no. 21 (26 runs), no. 91 (8) and no. 92 (6) sign by sign from 2-4x crops, paired with Gabbrielli's glosses (TRANSCRIPTION.md). The rest of no. 92 (about fifteen glossed runs) not reached.

Tried to align eleven further glossed runs (21-1, 21-14, 21-28, 91-1b, 91-3, 91-6, 91-7, 92-2/3, 92-4 start, 92-5, 92-6): glosses faint, partly blotted or not matching sign counts.

Re-transcribed all 99 cipher tokens of no. 171 and deciphered them with the extended key (cipher171.tsv, READING.md): PAVOLO, CINTADINI, the Conte word sign three times, [Dieci], MADON[null]NA, PURE with a null; 'a lui' withdrawn (A LO…); the heavy pair on line 4 is a null plus one word sign.

texts.summary: Gramont writes to Montmorency as Clement VII sets out for Bologna (October 1529): he vouches for the Pope's secret alignment with France; Clement dreads the general council and plans to grant it in principle and then stall it, offers to feign illness on the road to wait for the Admiral Chabot, fears soothsayers who foretell his deposition or death "du costé de" the Emperor, and had a dream before leaving Rome (enclosed).
