texts.label: f. 119 (DECODE R4162), 27 May 1587
texts.summary: The writer (Guise?) tells Mercœur the levy of reiters is assured: by August two thousand Italian or Albanian lances and four thousand reiters; his secretary has gone to colonel Pfyffer with twelve thousand écus to treat for nine thousand Swiss; the heretics' army (eight thousand reiters, twelve thousand Swiss, lansquenets, four thousand arquebusiers for Châtillon) must be defeated, sparing nothing for the glory of God and the cause.

texts.label: f. 142 (DECODE R4165), 20 June 1587
texts.summary: After clear news of Lunebourg with nine thousand horse on the Rhine by 20 July, the cipher says the levy that was to be so far advanced is not, the thousand lances and four thousand reiters are "ung instable secours", hasty resolutions force the party to order its affairs less securely than its first designs, and within five or six days the writer hopes to settle the matter with [73], the forces going to find it at Meaux.

IC 0.0398 over 3,630 tokens and Sukhotin's vowel test: consistent with a homophonic alphabet of about 50 signs, not with a syllabary (the commonest sign carries 8.7% of the text).
Homophonic annealing with a 1530-1600 French LM (order 4/5, no spaces) and a unigram-frequency penalty, up to 20 restarts x 400k moves, whole text and page by page.

Control experiment: real French enciphered with a 50-sign homophonic key of the same shape, run through the same solver. It failed too, so the solver was the obstacle; a wrong Sukhotin vowel/consonant constraint and a temperature scale far too small for the log-probability deltas. With both fixed the control solves 100%, and 95.5% with 15% of its signs corrupted.
The corrected annealer on the real text produced French immediately; basin hopping and a word-segmentation objective recovered the whole alphabet.
The recovered key had no sign for m or b, impossible for French: the diagnostic that pointed at the transcription rather than the key.

Second, reading-guided transcription of ff. 263v and 264v against the key: the dot groups are m (controls 'et maintenant', 'l'amitie', 'Monsieur de'), phi is b against f = u ('de beau|caire', 'd'une bonne armee'), E3 is s against E = a, T is u against b = n, eq is f. 513 and 138 sign tokens changed.

Content controls: place-names and persons appear where the clear text leads to them - Beaucaire sur le Rosne, Besiers, Carcassonne, Languedoc, Montmorency, d'Espernon, the prince of Parme, Lisbone.

texts.label: R8505, "L'Estat du Roy de Navarre et de son party en France" (Harley MS 1582 ff. 263-264)
texts.summary: A French political memoir, written after 1580, surveying Henri de Navarre as a political asset for an outside reader: his two 'qualitez' (first prince of the blood, chief of the reformed churches), the places and garrisons he holds in Guyenne, Languedoc, Dauphiné and Provence, his following, his alliances and the marriage question; it belongs with Navarre's embassies to the Protestant powers in the mid-1580s. The cipher carries the sensitive clauses inline in the clear French (d'Espernon, Beaucaire sur le Rosne, Besiers, Carcassonne).

texts.label: Harley MS 286 f. 61, D'Ewes's log of his son's fits, 1635-36
texts.summary: Not a letter but a private record: Sir Simonds D'Ewes, in the private alphabet he invented at school, notes in Latin each convulsion fit of his infant son Clopton D'Ewes (b. texts.label: R8482-R8483, Lord Cobham to [Walsingham], Ostend, 22 Mar 1587/8 (ff. 70r-v)
texts.summary: Henry Brooke, Lord Cobham, one of Elizabeth's peace commissioners at Ostend in spring 1588, asks that ships be sent to attend on the coast, warns that the garrison is too weak and short of money and victuals, and reports Parma's new ditch from Ghent by Eeclo to Sluys, nearly navigable for his float-boats, and the threat to the town and haven. No sign-level transcription exists: the cipher runs were read word by word from crops of the DECODE images.

texts.label: R8484, intelligence from Middelburg enclosed (f. 71r)
texts.summary: An enclosed intelligence report in another hand: Grenier's intrigue in clear, then in cipher advice that the ships be well guarded with two or three pinnaces in the channel, and news that a Jesuit (surname read Bastune?) has been sent post into Italy. No sign-level transcription exists.

texts.label: R8485-R8487, Lord Cobham to [Walsingham], Ostend, 20 Mar 1587/8 (ff. 71v-72v)
texts.summary: Cobham reports new companies at Oudenburg and stone and fagots coming by water from Eeclo, suspects an attempt on Ostend and asks to be removed to a safer place; he would think himself unhappy to be a means to conclude an irreligious peace, and argues against handing the prisoners Pigot and Barney over to the States. No sign-level transcription exists.

texts.label: R7766, Robert Reade to his cousin, Paris, 19 Apr 1641 (Harley MS 7001 ff. 148-149)
texts.summary: Robert Reade, nephew and secretary of Secretary Sir Francis Windebank, who followed him into exile in Paris, writes to a cousin at court, probably Thomas Windebank. The first cipher passage weighs what to do if a proclamation goes out against Windebank: they have not enough against him to confiscate his fortune, his person would not be safe if he returned, and only His Majesty can prevent it; the second says Sir William St Ravy has done Mr Forster no good offices. Read with the Windebank cipher reconstruction DECODE R9115; 14 tokens are conjectures.

solution.what: Fetched HCPortal record 513 metadata and full-resolution image; scanned records 490-535 for siblings from Nr. 259 (none).
Transcribed the six cipher lines (169 signs) and the decipherer's Anmerkung from crops.
Anmerkung: key letters bcdefg written continuously over the cipher, plaintext at the table's left edge, pairs for the first word.
The pairs fit shifts +2..+7 for b..g in a 25-letter alphabet without j.
Continuous decryption: line 1 reads ('schiket lisching oder e?nen andern hierher'), later lines drift out of phase.
Per-line and per-word phase search: 'beantworte diese fragen', 'paul follen', 'america', 'fries oken', 'merkliche folgen' at shifted phases.
Beam decoder allowing phase slips, scored with the de-modern n-gram model.
'de 4ette' = de Wette: the digit 4 is w under g (21+7 = 28); the cipher columns run on past z into digits, which take key letters.
With digits counted, the phase is continuous except one omitted sign in 'wo nicht'; 9 words carry single-sign copy slips (g/q, r/v, u/n/w, one transposition).
HCPortal, web and GitHub search for a prior reading, Lisching, Snell and Wetzlar; only an unsuccessful attempt (NoAutopilot/cipher-lab) found.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R1126/R1127 metadata and images; Vestigia search found Fantini's whole file (V1846-V1852), all images fetched.
Sender identified as Benedetto Fantini (DECODE misreads 'Jantini'), Ferrarese agent in Ippolito d'Este's household; only nos. 5 and 6 contain cipher, and no decipherment is in the file.
Column transcription (upper sign / base stroke) of R1126 p. 1, 18 cipher lines, 581 columns.
Homophonic anneal (it-cinquecento 4-grams, unigram penalty) over p. 1 columns, with the frequent 7g/7y signs kept, merged, or treated as nulls: 6 restarts x 60k moves each.

Statistics: the three-column run 7 / g / m-with-b recurs 14 times and 7g or 7y occurs 45 times in 581 columns, too often for one letter per column; 7g and 7y behave like word signs. The unit of the cipher is unresolved.
Web search and the Bonzagni 1512 and Caprile 1519 Este-Hungary siblings for a printed decipherment or shared key: Bonzagni is a different alphabet, Caprile's 1519 key is itself not built.
Second independent readings of p. 1 and p. 2 (agreement 90% and 76%); all disagreements adjudicated on the images; combined 1,258 units.
Synthetic Italian homophonic text, 1,190 tokens/90 symbols: 98.7% recovered clean, 92% at 5% label noise, 27% at 10-15%.
Anneal on the adjudicated text under seven unit models (per-unit letter, 7-9 merged, bare 7 null, upper only, brackets as word codes, CV syllabary, Caprile/che pins); seeds disagree, no Italian.
Third reading of p. 2 L13-L25, every unit checked on the image: 11 changes, estimated residual error 2-3%.

Size-matched controls: 144 true signs fail even noise-free (42%); 90-100 signs with 3-5% noise succeed (92-95%). The real text filtered to 87 labels still does not converge, so it is not a simple one-letter-per-sign homophonic cipher.

Caprile R1133/7c shows bracket signs are whole words; under that model Fantini's letters fall into 189 runs of about 5 signs (903 tokens, 121 labels). A control of that shape at 3% noise recovers 7%: ciphertext-only is infeasible.
Rebuilt the Caprile 1519 key by seeded EM alignment of R1133 with its 1882 decipherment 7c: the alignment collapses (purity 0.33); the firm Caprile values pinned on Fantini give no Italian.

outcome.method_basis: Both cipher pages were transcribed three times and annealed under seven unit models; controls show a word-code cipher of this shape cannot be broken ciphertext-only, and no key or decipherment was found in ASMo, Vestigia or print.
outcome.notes: Attempted, closed unread for lack of key material. Both pages transcribed three ways (~2-5% residual error). The bracket signs are word codes (as in Caprile 1519), leaving letter runs of about 5 signs; a matched control recovers 7%. Needs a key or crib: the Caprile 1519 key, or an ASMo decipherment.

solution.what: Located f. 156 and its continuation on f. 157r-v through the Gallica IIIF manifest and downloaded high-resolution images.
Identified Giovan Gioacchino da Passano and compared Le Grand's printed diplomatic letter and Letters and Papers no. 6307; neither prints the account cipher.
Transcribed nine account entries on both sides of f. 157, including 402 proposed cipher signs; separated clear amounts and 'in summa'.
Measured 20 distinct proposed signs and index of coincidence 0.0819; checked repeats and periodic coincidence.
Tried one-to-one Italian permutation search, including a 40 by 80,000-step incremental search, period-specific u/v, French, Spanish, Latin, modern Italian, English, reversal and adjacent swaps.
Tried frequent signs as spaces and as nulls, homophonic mappings, and Italian dictionary segmentation.

A 402-sign artificial Italian monoalphabetic cryptogram of matching entry lengths recovered 20/20 assignments; with 10% and 20% random symbol corruption, 18/20 and 17/20 assignments remained recoverable.
A plain one-sign/one-letter substitution is inadequate for the copied account, or the provisional transcription has more systematic sign conflation than the controls' random errors.

Independently re-transcribed the account with dotted signs distinguished and straight 1 separated from curved 2: ciphertext_dotted.txt, 397 provisional signs, 28 types. Earlier transcription merged significant dots and inconsistently aliased 1 and 2.

Seeded JavaScript incremental homophonic annealing, shared it-cinquecento four-gram model, 100 restarts x 100000 iterations, frequency KL penalty. Dotted transcription yields connected Italian account entries, including in denari contanti, oro et argento, Winchester and St Albans. Unpenalized model degenerated to repeated i; retained as failed initial test.

Manual checks identify denari contanti, baghe, vasele d oro et d argento, supelectili de casa, Winchester, St Albans and York. The passage earlier treated as clear in summa is actually five cipher signs 1 m S m m = un ann followed by 7 = o. This restores un anno and adds five enciphered tokens.

Extended the computational key by recurring Italian words; 1d=b, n=m, T=s. Recovered the supposed clear in summa as five cipher signs un ann; restored un anno. Three rare signs left without invented expansions.

Checked all 16 physical cipher lines against the images, exposing 13 local emendations. Decoder emits 402 token rows: 395 assigned, 386 conservatively coherent. Right-margin Roman components sum to DCCL. No contemporary key or parallel plaintext.

Nearby cipher uses a different inventory; LP 6307 is 4 April, not March. Word/shelfmark searches found no parallel. Post-solution OVI lexical lookup confirms dese can mean ten but does not settle the numerical sentence. The historical copy explicitly omits a page and three lines.

Context readings for the quotation list: margin sums CL/L/LX/XX/CCL/CC/XX with a raised sign taken as thousands (foot total DCCL under M); [D] = [Cardinale] (four masculine-person places, 'al deto [D]' echoes the clear 'predetto Cardinale'); [Q] = [il Re] (receiver of the goods); [S2] left open. Grade I, bracketed, not key values; coverage unchanged.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 395 tokens, 25 types, it-cinquecento order 4: reading -2.338 per letter; random keys -4.658 (z 5.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.884 (mean -2.95, z 11.7); annealer on the real text -2.641. Verdict: pass.

system.summary: Two-figure letter-and-syllable cipher, one code per value (about 60 codes), written without separation, with the digits 5 and 8 as nulls and names in clear capitals.
system.sibling_key: Kauderbach's 1761 key, HStAD 10024 Loc. 08236/11 Bl. 5 (DECODE R936): same design and vocabulary, different numbers.
system.notes: Names are capitals with ./. in clear (S./., Q./., P./.), meanings differing from the 1761 table. 13 may be y and re.

prior_solution.where: DECODE notes that the Hague cabinet never solved them; no printed decipherment found.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: DECODE records fetched with the session cookie: 32 page images, 3 transcriptions (R1043, R1044, R2078).
Web search for a printed decipherment or edition of Kauderbach's despatches.
Digit counts, successor table, 2- and 3-figure phase IC on the DECODE transcriptions: no fixed period; long exact repeats show a fixed code.
Seven records transcribed from the images by sub-agents (one died on an oversized-image error and was re-run); R1954 in a letter-like hand only partly reliable.
Mixed 1/2/3-figure group rules by first digit scored by entropy; EM segmentation of 1-4-figure tokens.
Removing 5 and 8 as single-figure nulls restores a clean 2-figure phase (IC 0.027 vs 0.021; 4-figure 0.155/0.161 vs 0.103); Viterbi realignment gives a table of about 60 two-figure codes.

Homophonic letter solver (quadgram coordinate ascent, validated 98% on synthetic French through the same pipeline) in French, German, Dutch, Italian, word-reversed French, with nulls, syllable values or merged look-alike figures.
Pattern cribs for long repeats (guerre, Angleterre) seeded into the solver.

DECODE key listing searched; Kauderbach's 1761 key (R936) fetched: one code per letter or syllable, capitals for names, a declared null. Numbers do not fit; vocabulary adopted (m restored from the image).
Simulated annealing over one-to-one assignments of the codes onto the 1761 vocabulary, char-4-gram score; seeds 22 and 24 converged to the same key (-3.85/letter).
Key refined by reading and an extended vocabulary (in, ou, qu, st, par, pas, qui, pour, fai, ke, z; 01/12 swapped); ten letters read by two sub-agents, one per five letters.
Content checked against history: Holderness's warning and the 30,000-man augmentation (Jul 1755), Kniphausen at Compiegne, the Treaty of Versailles of 1 May 1756 with its neutrality clause.

Four slips of normalisation in the reading files and write-up, reported while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list, re-checked group by group in cipher/R*.txt with key.json and the machine decryptions, and corrected: R1043 'parce qu'on craint qu'il n'y ait des articles secrets qui aillent encore plus loin' (was 'croit qu'il y a ... qui vont') and 'l'on a fait aussi' (was 'dit'); R2080 'treize mille hommes' (29 03 14 77 16, confirmed on the image; was 'trente', so the augmentation of the verification step above is 13,000, not 30,000) and 'pour combatre' (66 = pour; was 'et combattre').

system.summary: Homophonic cipher: 1-40 and letter/graphic signs for single letters (some for letter pairs), 41-100 for consonant+vowel syllables in a regular reverse-alphabet table, a few nulls.

conditions.human_role: None beyond the goal statement.

solution.what: Fetched 9 DECODE records and 73 public images; no key record or transcription on DECODE.
Found Mírka's Crypto-World 11-12/2012 reprint: key rebuilt from R3811 p.1 interlinear, only R3811 read, key not printed.
Four agents transcribed all 73 images token by token (tr/), with the ~210 interlinear glosses on R3811 pp.1-2.
Free homophonic annealing (symbol -> letter/CV bigram/null) with a German 5-gram model on R3813.
Same with a letter-frequency (KL) penalty.
From the glosses: 41-100 are consonant+vowel signs, two consonants per ten (reverse alphabet), units o i e a; 1-40 and signs are single letters.
Structured annealer (one consonant per half, one value per single sign) seeded with 17 gloss values, on R3811-R3813, then all records.
Irregular fifth-place signs (pu lu mu hu ku du gu bu cu us ru) and two-letter single signs (te se si ve so ti tu) fixed from context and LM ranking.
All nine letters deciphered with key.json (read/*.txt); 98.3% of 22,913 cipher tokens given a value.

Checked second pass: agents compared every line of all 73 transcriptions with image crops, guided by a per-token decode; about 360 tokens corrected (c for #l-loop, 9 for #sect, 6/61 for phi, digit-group splits).
Bug fix: 56 cipher lines starting with a sign token had been skipped as comments by decode/parse; restored.
R3813 'x' is a separate crossed-f sign = ta (LM better on R3813, worse on R3812 if applied there); split out as #f-cross.
German 5-gram score per letter before/after the second pass: better on 8 of 9 letters (R4736 flat, more text restored).
alpha re-valued m -> sa (Salvius, caesaris, universal-); looped variant split out as #a-loop = m on 28 image-checked tokens; LM better on every letter vs baseline.
Clear text transcribed: R4645 Banér copies (to Lüneburg 10 Jan 1639; to Lower Saxon envoys 29 Jan 1639); R4734 endorsement shows the addressee is Count Schwarzenberg.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 22728 tokens, 133 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.378 per letter; random keys -4.857 (z 8.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.206 (mean -3.213, z 131.9); annealer on the real text -2.781. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): page transcriptions tr/IMG_<record>_*.txt and the machine decipherments read/<record>.txt (with the clear copy, endorsement and summary files where they exist); key key.json and KEY.md.

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the nine read/*.txt files read through. The deciphered runs are unspaced and garbled every few lines in eight letters (by-eye coherence 55-80%), so sentences that run through the cipher cannot be built: R3811-R3815, R4625, R4645, R4736 relabelled decoded, not read; R4734's short runs read (kept read, reviewed B). fraction_read 0.999 (tokens with a value) -> 0.021.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b06): key corrected for all nine letters after kwic checks over the whole corpus: 38 = d (was g: feindt, und, landt, wurdt), Δ = nu (was e: warnung, hoffnung, nun, Nuncio), #dot = su (was null: sufficient, subsidia, verfassung, suspiciones), #s-long = ti (was t: militaria, resolution, obligation; glossed ti on R3811 p. 1), m = a (was null; after 29: quartier, quam, quando). Two polyphonic readings entered as relabelled signs: 9v = vo (the same 9 shape; Volck, von, vor, voluimus, darvon) and pv = vi (the crossed long-s; Salvius, resolviren, proviant, privilegia), relabelled in tr/ only where the other value gives no word. KEY.md updated.

Re-read b06: every letter checked on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images (main checkout img/; crops in the session scratchpad only, research/reading_audit/b06_crop.py); about 330 label and clear-text fixes logged in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv (φ for 6, #f-cross for p after 27, 9v, pv, regrouped figures, struck tokens turned into notes, clear Kurrent re-read, R4625 dated Hamburg 10 Feb 1639 from its p. 6). The R3811 interlinear decipherment transcribed in read/R3811_interlinear.md (it also settles 4 2 = 42, 9 = #sect, 0 = φ).

Re-read b06: readings and English translations built for all eight letters (read/<rec>_reading.md, _en.md, _reread_log.md), aligned word by word with the decode (research/reading_audit/b06_align.py; R3811 also with the interlinear gloss), supplied letters bracketed. Clean-sentence share of the reading bodies (b06_body_score.py, the _check_reading.py logic): R3811 0.62, R3812 0.616, R3815 0.681, R4625 0.603, R4645 0.625, R4736 0.636 (read, grade B); R3813 0.531, R3814 0.524 (decoded, not read: Latin, names and period spellings the word list does not know, homophone splits of x and d, runs without a word).

Re-read r2c (REREAD_BRIEF): DECODE R3813 and R3814 re-fetched with the project cookie; besides the images both list two attachments not opened before, Jakub Mírka's key reconstruction as an Excel sheet and a one-page handwritten table (2022). A key, no plaintext. Neighbouring records R3809/R3810 (Florence) and R3816/R3817 (Heusner 1637, SP 106) unrelated; web search for an edition of Kurz's Hamburg letters found none.

Our key compared with Mírka's table sign by sign: structure identical (41-100 CV table, letter series sa..vu = a..r). Two values disagreed and were checked at every occurrence in the nine letters: k = to (was ti; all 17 uses: protectorium, electores, multorum, a proposito, bis dato, in puncto ...) and m = va (was a; negativam, riserva, avantagiosen, enervatis; after 29 = qu the v is not doubled: decode.py rule). Both adopted. 4 = x does not hold for the plain 4 (fails 3 times). 9v = vo (22 Oct, flagged for review) holds at all 48 uses and is Mírka's q.

Look-alike signs split on full-resolution crops (r2c_line.py): in R3813 the crossed sign is two shapes, the tall crossed f = ta and a low curled p-form = vi (Mírka's p): 20 tokens relabelled pv, 3 plain p likewise; the looped k-form = to had been read d (8) or α (1): relabelled k; in R3811 three x are the k-form (protectorium, Stockholmb); in R3812 (5) and R3815 (1) the p after Sal- is the curled p-form; the x places of the plain 4 are a crossed 4 (Mírka's X, glossed x on R3811 p. 1), new label #4-cross = x (7); R3814: 'aber wir' (#sect), 'quod' and 'vor oder' (9v). Logged in read/<rec>_corrections.tsv. Tried without result: R3814 'auf terte freltung', 'zeit wetlohren', 'denomina-d-4-e'.

R3813 and R3814 readings updated (about 35 words now carried, aligned word by word with b06_align.py, 0 words not carried) and sibling readings brought in line with k = to, pv and #4-cross. Body scores with conjectures as holes (v2_score.py): R3813 plain 0.537 -> 0.563, explicit holes 0.910 -> 0.932; R3814 0.508 / 0.952 -> 0.968; both read as sentences: marked read (grade B). Every letter now reads: fraction_read 0.575 -> 1.0, class read.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 9 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

texts.label: R3812, Hamburg, 3 Feb 1639
texts.summary: Kurz von Senftenau on the quartering of six imperial regiments and the Lower Saxon Kreistag: Banér's plundering will ruin the Stift Halberstadt, Duke Georg of Lüneburg will not resist; he sees no real Swedish or French wish for peace and great ill-feeling between Denmark and Sweden. Postscript on Arnim's visit after escaping Swedish captivity.

texts.label: R3811, Hamburg, 17 Jan 1639
texts.summary: Nothing can be done with Duke Georg; France, Sweden and Holland plan an embassy to the King of Denmark to prevent a congress in Sweden; Duke August of Saxe-Lauenburg is said to seek Danish protection; Arnim denies plotting against the Peace of Prague and Kurz advises a protectorium. The letter carries an interlinear decipherment (summarised by Mírka in 2012).

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 17 Jan 1639. Read and translated (read/R3811_reading.md, _en.md); clean-sentence share of the reading body 0.62 (49 of 79 sentences). texts.label: R3813, Hamburg, 27 Jan 1639
texts.summary: Twenty-page memorandum: the enemy advances unopposed towards Salzwedel; a Kreistag broken up by the enemy is better than one concluded with express neutrality; Kurz advises a defensive strategy, distrusts Salvius, weighs a secret particular treaty with Sweden through Brandenburg or Denmark, and says France wants Lorraine, Alsace and even the imperial crown.

reading_review.note: Hamburg, 27 Jan 1639. Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (r2c): reading body (header and Notes cut) 0.563 clean sentences on the word list, 0.932 on explicit holes with every [?word] and [word] counted as a hole (v2_score.py; 290 of 311 sentences), hole rate 0.036; German of 1639 with Latin, so the explicit-hole share is the bar, and the sentences hold through the twenty pages (Banér's crossing, Duke Georg's passivity, the defensive plan, quarters against money, Salvius, the Cologne congress, the protectorium). system.summary: Numerical homophonic substitution inserted in clear French: one-digit and two-figure units (vowels 1,3,5,9 and their teen forms, consonants two-figure groups), 6 = word space; no nomenclator.
system.notes: Key recovered by AngusRobinson (PR #20). Points follow the space sign 6. i/j/y and u/v merged; uu for w.

prior_solution.where: Cryptiana, DECODE and web searched 23 Sept and 7 Oct 2026; nothing found.

conditions.human_role: Identified manuscript and requested solving to completion. 7 Oct 2026: outside contributor AngusRobinson (GitHub PR #20) recovered the key and decipherment; Bourdeau asked Claude to review and verify the PR. Tools and model of the contributor unknown.

solution.what: Resumed existing local notes and IIIF scans; earlier Prague cipher transcription incomplete. Regenerated native-scale crops.
Inspected Breslau cipher at native scale; numeral order and digit grouping require renewed analysis. Earlier notes are unverified prior project work, not an independent decipherment.
Transcribed sixteen Prague recto insertions and May cipher into runs_draft.json; glyph and grouping uncertainties retained.
Tested 63 greedy one/two-digit prefix partitions. Unrestricted homophonic scoring collapsed to repeated letters; constrained swaps produced no coherent text. Testing point-delimited pairs next.
Swept 1566 retained forward/backward greedy prefix segmentations on the frozen initial draft; six pair variants and pointed-six null variants gave no coherent manuscript plaintext.
Expanded to 29 Prague insertions plus the two May spans; measured 834 and 77 draft digits. Rechecked f64 lower cipher against its repeated view on f65.
Imposed hypothetical mais...jamais, then ne/ni, in point-delimited pair parses of May. No coherent extension; all crib mappings rejected as unvalidated.
Constrained pair substitution solver recovered 538 of 538 synthetic plaintext letters. This verifies the restricted implementation, not the manuscript model. See control/result.tsv.
Read f63 reference to sending a copy of the cipher by one of two routes on 24 February to Sr Barquin (name provisional). Corrected par lune, previously misread as a place.
Located catalogue mirror for fr. 4695 no. 51, Labbe to Nevers, Prague 5 February 1577, Gallica btv1b90582923; plausible earlier correspondence, not inspected and not a demonstrated key enclosure.
New Gallica image/manifest requests failed by connection reset or timeout via Python, curl and browser; earlier-letter/enclosure trail remains externally blocked.
AngusRobinson (PR #20): guessed three similar figure strings as l'empereur / empereur, giving one- and two-figure units with homophones and 6 = word space.

texts.label: f. 124, to Charles IX, Warsaw, 26 April 1573 (no. 51)
texts.summary: Lanssac tells Charles IX that the obstacles in Thuringia, Meissen and the Mark of Brandenburg delayed him so that he reached Poland (Mezeritz) only on 25 February, and that without the escort of the King's pensioners Alexander von Miltitz and George Luelz he would at the least have been detained; the ciphered passages hide the dangers Frenchmen met in Germany. The rest, in clear, refers to his recueil on Polish affairs.

texts.label: ff. 154r-v, to the duc d'Anjou, Warsaw, 24 April 1573 (no. 60)
texts.summary: On the eve of the Polish election, Lanssac reports to Anjou that the Lithuanian chiefs have promised their vote to him, which with the party already won should put the crown on his head, unless the Grand Seigneur's recommendation of him, made with ruse through the voivode of Wallachia, brings some unexpected change.

texts.label: ff. 156-157, to Catherine de Médicis, Warsaw, 24 April 1573 (no. 61)
texts.summary: Lanssac tells Catherine that matters stand so that by next Monday she should be mother of the two greatest kings in the world, barring a change of minds, and fears that the Emperor might surprise them and that the King of Denmark, bending to his will, might give them much trouble on that side because of the strait, not half a league wide. The end of the letter (f. 157r) is in clear.

texts.label: ff. 160, 164, 174, to Charles IX and Anjou, 1 and 9 May 1573 (nos. 63, 65, 70)
texts.summary: f. 160: the Polish nation is as venal as its German neighbours. f. 164: the Emperor has spent more than 300,000 écus in the negotiation against 30,000 on the other side and achieves nothing but to trouble Anjou's design. f. 174 (Płock, 9 May), announcing the election: it succeeded against the will of the Grand Seigneur, the Emperor, the princes of the Empire, the King of Spain, the Muscovite and the King of Sweden.

system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.
system.sibling_key: Alonso Sanchez's 1522 Venice cipher and Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher, both reconstructed by Tomokiyo; same design, provably different values (xul = 'lo' here, 'despues' in Sanchez).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's 2025 article covers Sanchez (R9593-R9632) and Juan Manuel (R9499-R9529) only; Lope Hurtado is not mentioned and his records fall outside both ranges. A web search returns no decipherment.

conditions.human_role: redirected the session to this target; supplied the DECODE login cookie reused from an earlier target. Would need to fetch higher-resolution images from the RAH's own Biblioteca Digital, which blocks automated access, to lift the alphabet limit.

solution.what: Established in the sanchez1522 session that these nine records are not in Sanchez's cipher: his codes end strictly in b c d f g h l m n, Hurtado's take finals p and z.
Searched for a published decipherment of Hurtado's cipher. None: Tomokiyo's article covers Sanchez and Juan Manuel only and does not mention him; web search returns nothing. The key is unpublished.
Split the nine Lope Hurtado records out of sanchez1522 into their own target with images and DECODE metadata.
Found that R9644 carries both the ciphered letter (ff. 238-239) and a full contemporary clear version (f. 242), headed 'Claro' section by section and keyed to the cipher by marginal letters A, B, C.

Aligned the cipher against the clear on an exact-count run: 'ton tab xud xul y-m xon' against 'que nunca hombre lo fue mas', six tokens for six words in a sentence with no room for slippage, plus tu = no from 'no apretallo mucho'. Seven values confirmed; eleven more read as probable from the surrounding sentence where counts are not exact.

Cross-checked against the sibling keys: xul = 'lo' here but 'despues' in Sanchez, so the keys are provably distinct. None of the seven confirmed codes appears in Tomokiyo's 173-code Juan Manuel table either, which is consistent with a third key but not conclusive since that table is partial.

Second anchor on f. 238: 'zun top' immediately before the clear words 'descargo de los q', against plaintext 'da por descargo de lo que dexa'. Confirms top = por in an independent context and gives zun = da. Also shows long words spelled letter by letter between the codes (a ten-sign run where 'satisfecho' must be, an eight-sign run where 'servidor' must be). Nine values now confirmed, twelve probable, kept apart in a confidence column.

Checked R9650 f. 270 (the other Decrypted record): ton tab xud stand there in identical forms, and top again immediately precedes clear words in a slot reading 'por disimular en este caso' - a third independent context for top = por. tu and zun recur. So Hurtado used one key across these letters and values won on R9644 carry to the rest, which is what makes the six non-decrypted records reachable.

Found the start of the clear version on f. 241 ('Al Rey - de Lope Hurtado, de Roma, del primero de noviembre', then Claro, then lettered sections), so the clear runs ff. 241-242 and covers the cipher of ff. 238-239 from its start.

Aligned the stretch after the clear words 'si algo se le dixesse': cipher '<8-sign run> ton [b]z7 teg' against plaintext 'pensaria que era para'. New confirmed values era and para, plus the letter r attested twice (the r of the spelled pensaria, and zun+r = dar, which re-confirms zun = da). Thirteen confirmed, thirteen probable.

Retracted an earlier probable value: zar = 'Bari' was wrong. zar is frequent and falls here in the slot 'los criados de su Sa'; it is now carried as 'de' or 'su', still probable. The confirmed/probable split in key_codes.tsv is what caught this - no probable value had been used to derive anything.

A line of R9644 f. 238 aligned end to end with the plaintext, nothing left over: 'ta xil+s zun+z xur zun q x-i-r-i-a ton tu ton+ria ton xul' = 'no les dar nada y diria que no queria que lo'. Gives ta = no (a homophone of tu, both in the same line, so the cipher has homophones at code level), xil = le, q = y, and the ending -ria. Shows codes carrying syllables: xur+zun = na+da, ton+ria = que+ria, with zun the same 'da' confirmed earlier in 'da por'. Nineteen confirmed, thirteen probable.

ton+zun+ria-n = que+da+rian = 'quedarian' on R9644 f. 238 against the plaintext. Three codes chained into one word. zun = da now confirmed in three distinct roles: a whole word (da por), the second syllable of na-da, and the middle syllable of que-da-rian. The ending gives the letter 4 = n, matching the n of the spelled pensaria. Twenty-one confirmed, thirteen probable.

Exact-count run at the end of the paragraph: four cipher units for 'tiene perdida la esperança'. 'perdida' is spelled out, seven signs for seven letters, which hands over a first slice of the substitution alphabet: p, e, r, d (two different signs), i, a, and n. Cross-checks against the spelled 'pensaria' earlier and against r, already confirmed twice. Thirty-one confirmed, thirteen probable. One sign left unassigned: it reads t in 'tiene' but seemed s in 'pensaria', so one transcription is wrong and it is not guessed.

Pushed a profile.json with a non-schema field (system.homophones.note) which made _check_profile.py report INVALID; caught on the next check and fixed in the following commit. The homophone observation (two codes for 'no'; two signs for the letter d inside the spelled 'perdida') is kept in NOTES.md, where prose belongs, and recorded in the schema as max_per_consonant = 2.

'El camarero Pedro es el principal' in the clear gives the spelled name Pedro on the cipher side: five signs for five letters, p/e/d/r already confirmed, so m = o falls out. Alphabet so far: p, e, r, d (two signs), i, a, n, o. Thirty-three confirmed, fourteen probable.

Found that R9648 (Non-decrypted) carries the same matter as R9644's clear - 'pregunte a su S.' and 'le avia embiado la carta de v. Mt y q esperava saber lo de Yngalaterra' stand in the clear on its leaves, answering to section C of the R9644 plaintext. Hurtado sent his despatches in duplicate, so one clear version serves both, and R9644's plaintext cribs R9648 as well.

First previously-unread text read: R9648 f. 262, nine cipher tokens against nine plaintext words with nothing left over - 'y que el papa no esta en que venga' - and 'que nueva tenia de Francia' after the clear words 'pregunte a su S.'. The values q=y, ton=que and tu=no, won on R9644, reappear here correctly, which is the check that matters. Seven new values: taf=papa, y-of=esta, y-uc=en, te-r=nueva, tenia, y-on=Francia, and the spelled 'venga'; y-ub=el promoted from probable. Short, and leaning on the duplicate's plaintext rather than the key alone, so a foothold rather than a reading.

More of R9648 f. 262 reads: 'ton y-ub zed' before the clear 'le avia embiado la carta' = 'que el arcobispo', giving zed = arcobispo, a name-code for the archbishop of Bari. And a continuous run 'la paz por los infieles y por la necessidad', where la, por, los and y are all values won earlier and reappearing correctly, and tef = paz is new. Forty-six confirmed, eleven probable.

The alphabet decodes a word on its own. On R9648 f. 264, between the clear words 'antes de agora' and 'si se oviera hecho', the cipher gives 'tu su <run> <8-sign run> xur zun' = 'no se [h]uviera perdido nada'. The eight-sign run spells p-e-r-d-i-d-o, and six of those signs (e, r, d, i, d, o) were derived on R9644 from 'perdida', 'pensaria' and 'Pedro' - every one correct here in a word decoded without being looked for. xur+zun = na+da reappears intact. R9644 carries the same sentence in the clear, being the duplicate, so the reading is corroborated rather than unsupported; but the decoding was done from the key, not read off the crib.

THE VALIDATION THAT MATTERS. Everything so far leaned somewhere on R9644's plaintext, R9648 being its duplicate. R9656 (ff. 334-335, headed 'De Lope Hurtado de xx de noviembre') is a different despatch three weeks later with no clear version and no duplicate. The key reads there unaided: after the clear words 'las cartas traxo don Correo q vino con la valante', the cipher gives '|| tu n7 <2 runs> y-ub taf' = 'no ... EL PAPA', with y-ub = el and taf = papa both won on R9648 against R9644's crib. Elsewhere on the leaf ton, zar, y-of, sub and tu all fall in slots that make sense. The three unresolved units are left blank rather than guessed.

R9648 f. 264 after the clear 'A lo q he entendido': 'zil y-ub zed zar <spelled Cosenza>' against section B of the R9644 plaintext = 'con el arcobispo de Cosenza'. Gives zil = con, re-confirms zed = arcobispo in a second context, and promotes zar = de, now attested three times (de su Sa, de Francia, de Cosenza) - which matters because zar is one of the commonest groups on every leaf. Forty-nine confirmed, ten probable.

rab = vuestra magestad, from 'zar rab' falling exactly on 'de v. ma' in section C, and from rab being one of the commonest groups on every leaf - which is what 'vuestra magestad' should be in despatches to the Emperor. The spelled words either side check the alphabet again: 'honrrado' and 'approvechado' both end a-d-o, with n inside the first, every sign having come from R9644. Fifty confirmed, ten probable.

Attempted to extend the substitution alphabet from spelled words with known plaintext (Cosenza, venga, tiene, pensaria). Blocked: the transcriptions contradict each other - tiene wants one sign = t where pensaria wants it = s; venga wants a sign = v where perdida fixes it = i; Cosenza comes out eight signs for seven letters with two signs apparently doing double duty. At least one transcription in each pair is wrong, so those signs are left unassigned rather than picking whichever suits. Same wall as sanchez1522: the three-letter code groups read off the page easily, the spelled letter-signs need a picture-book built glyph by glyph against known plaintext.

Section A of R9644 (f. 237, marked A in the margin) aligned against its clear on f. 241. Six values already fixed - tu (no), xul (lo), ton (que), y-af (es), zil (con), rab (vuestra magestad) - all fall in their right places across one long sentence, the densest single check the key has had. New: su-su = 'su' and s-id = 'Sa' (Su Santidad, the Pope), from the pair standing at 'su Sa' in 'prevenga a su Sa'. Three more probable: obligado, haga, dezir. Fifty-two confirmed, twelve probable.

Paragraph 2 of R9644 f. 237 against its clear: 'porque su Sa tenia tanta passion que no conocia lo que don Joan'. Seven fixed values in a row (top, ton, s-id, ton, tu, zil, xul, ton), plus another instance of the stem-plus-ending pattern - zil (con) + spelled 'ocia' = 'conocia', the third construction zil has appeared in. Three new probables: tenia, tanta, don. Noted but not settled: s-id stood beside su-su (su) as 'su Sa' in section A but carries 'su Sa' alone here, so either it means Sa with su sometimes coded separately, or it means the whole title.

End of R9644 f. 237 against 'lo que le parece del duque ... lo que no quedo de don Joan segun dizen todos'. Gives y-o-b = duque (the Duke of Sessa, imperial ambassador at Rome); zar+one sign = del; ton+d+o = 'quedo', a code finished with two alphabet signs; and d-o-n spelled outright, which fixes a second sign for o beside m. That last matters beyond the word: this sign was one of those whose readings contradicted each other, and it turns out to be a homophone, so part of the earlier alphabet tangle was a missing homophone rather than a bad transcription. Fifty-five confirmed, thirteen probable.

Built decode.py, which applies only confirmed values (probables print in angle brackets, unknowns as ?tok) and reports coverage. Measured on two lines from records the key was not built on: R9650 f. 270 gives 8/13 = 62%, R9648 f. 262 gives 7/10 = 70%. So roughly two tokens in three resolve on sight in letters the crib does not cover. The misses are a few unmet nomenclator codes and the spelled runs, which need the alphabet. Good enough to follow the sense of a passage, not good enough to edit one.

Found that R9650 also has its own full clear version, on f. 272, headed 'Al Rey - De Lope Hurtado de ...' exactly as R9644's. So there are TWO complete cribs covering two different letters. R9650's brings vocabulary the first lacks - franceses, Italia, dinero, Leon, yglesia, Hieronymo Adorno, don Joan Manuel, visorey de Napoles, posta - which are exactly the content nouns the key is short of. It also gives the letters' subject independently of the cipher: the French determined to come into Italy and sending a great sum of money to Lyon, the Pope to do what he can, Adorno having intercepted letters, the archbishop of Bari the channel to the Emperor.

R9650 f. 269 (the cipher whose clear is f. 272) against 'que los franceses son determinados de venir en Italia, y enbian gran suma de dinero a Leon, y que es menester'. Eight placements of already-fixed values land correctly in one sentence of a letter the first crib does not cover - ton, zar three times, y-uc, q twice, y-af, xul. The slots give the content nouns the key was short of, recorded as probable since token counts are not exact: franceses, Italia, dinero, Leon, gran, suma. Sixty-one entries, fifty-five confirmed.

R9650 f. 269 against 'y que el papa haga lo que pudiere': six fixed values (q, ton, y-ub, taf, xul, ton) round a single unknown, which the sense fixes as haga - promoted from probable, having been in the same slot in R9644 section A ('no haga lo que es obligado'). A value turning up twice in the same construction across two different letters is not coincidence. zar rab = 'de v. ma' again at the end of the line. Fifty-six confirmed.

R9650 f. 269 against 'y por lo que deve, no se ponga en esto': seven fixed values in one short clause (q, top, xul, ton, zar, tu, su, y-uc). New probables from the gaps: deve, ponga, esto, and cartas from the phrase before. Sixty-five entries, fifty-six confirmed.

Consolidation audit of the key: cross-checked every value for two codes claiming the same plaintext. Four retractions, kept in the file as commented RETRACTED lines rather than deleted - zed='de' (superseded by zed=arcobispo, confirmed twice), the sign-pair='el' (early non-exact alignment; el is y-ub, confirmed three times), one 'tenia' (conflicts with the confirmed one; one transcription is wrong), and one 'nada' (a misreading of xur+zun). The only surviving multi-claims are genuine homophones, each confirmed in evidence: two codes for 'no', two signs for d, two signs for o.

Read R9644 and R9650 complete, from the clerks' own contemporary clear versions (ff. 241-242 and f. 272), transcribed from the images into read_r9644.md and read_r9650.md. R9648 is R9644's duplicate so the same clear reads it too. Three of the nine records now have their content read in full; the ciphered leaves of those letters are read in part against the same text.

R9652 read complete: it carries NO cipher. DECODE calls it 'Partially decrypted' but the leaf is written entirely in the clear and signed Lope Hurtado; the status appears to reflect faded show-through at the head. Content: the licenciado Bernardino, a 'gran bellaco' the Duke of Sessa wants arrested, and Adrian VI declining a night arrest in Rome while offering a formal suplicacion instead; plus the viceroy of Naples' despatch on the siege of Rhodes forwarded to the Emperor. That last ties this correspondence to Sanchez's R9653 of 20 Nov, which carries the Rhodes news from Venice - Rome and Venice reporting the same disaster in the same fortnight, in two different ciphers, bound in the same volume.

Measured the key on R9645, a record with no crib of any kind: 57% of tokens resolve with confirmed values only. It decodes to 'se si no con [...] con vuestra magestad, que no [...] en [...] esta[do] [...] de vuestra magestad' - the shape and subject of the sentence with the content words missing. That is the honest ceiling of the present key on an uncribbed letter: function words and names resolve, spelled content words do not.

CORRECTION. An 8x zoom on the spelled 'perdido' in R9648 f. 264 shows the word resolving into seven distinct glyphs, but with the signs in positions 2 and 6 - which must be e and d - looking near-identical. They had been read as different letters at the lower zoom the alphabet values were taken at. So the nine alphabet values were labelled 'confirmed' on weaker evidence than that word implies. All ten sign entries downgraded to probable, with the reason written into each row; decode.py now shows every alphabet value in angle brackets. The distinction the earlier audit should have drawn: code groups are written as ordinary latin trigrams, legible without paleographic judgement and cross-checking against each other, so the 47 of them stand; alphabet signs rest on discriminating cursive shapes at the limit of the scans and do not.

Re-measured coverage after the downgrade, with decode.py applying confirmed values only: R9650 f. 270 still 62%. The coverage figures were carried almost entirely by the code groups, so the downgrade does not move them - which is itself the evidence that the nomenclator and the alphabet are independent, and that the reading rests on the safe half.

Established what would actually finish this, and that it needs the human. DECODE serves these leaves at 3440x2465 for a TWO-PAGE opening - about 1700 px across a folio, enough for the latin trigrams and not enough to tell two similar cursive signs apart. That is the measured cause of the alphabet limit. The volume is in the Coleccion Salazar y Castro, which the RAH is digitising at bibliotecadigital.rah.es; those images would be far better than DECODE's derivative copies. But that site returns HTTP 403 to automated requests and puts a bot check in front of its search, so it needs Daniel to fetch, exactly as DECODE's image server needs his logged-in cookie. Searching there for 'Salazar y Castro, A-26' and pulling ff. 237-243, 260-272, 334-335 at full resolution would unblock the alphabet and with it the five uncribbed records.

Checked whether DECODE holds anything better, using the logged-in cookie. It does not. The full-size file filesrv returns IS the 3440x2465 two-page opening already fetched (1.45 MB); MASTER_, MS_, ORIG_ and .tif variants all come back as the server's 5,244-byte not-found placeholder. The Image Manager (/decrypt-web/ImagesList) answers 'You do not have permission to access' with this cookie - it is a viewer session, not an editor one, so its zoom view is unreachable too. The ceiling is DECODE's stored derivative copy, which confirms that lifting the alphabet limit needs the RAH's own digitisation rather than anything further from DECODE.

Walked f. 239, the third ciphered leaf, marked B/C/D in the margin. Section B against 'que sin el no hay nada, y con el' gives su-b-r = 'sin' (sub 'si' plus one sign) and xur+zun = nada again. Section C against 'da senal de paz ... el Rey de Francia ... por enbiar embaxador a su Sa ... pues queda de la guerra' gives tel = 'pues', confirmed by an exact slot and immediately followed by ton+zun = que+da = 'queda', which confirms both a further time; ta-r = Rey and y-ed = embaxador recorded as probable. Eighty entries, forty-nine confirmed code values.

CORRECTION to an overstatement. Measured R9656, the uncribbed control, at 42% - lower than R9645's 57% - and its output is fragments ('no ... el papa ... la ... que ... su el papa'), not substance. I had been describing the five uncribbed records as reading 'in substance'; measured, they do not. The honest ceiling on an uncribbed letter is roughly half the tokens, concentrated in function words and names, with the content words as the misses: enough to say what a passage is about when surrounding clear text helps, not enough to read one. R9648 and R9650 score higher partly because their cribs were walked. Corrected in NOTES.md, profile.json and the write-up.

Applied the 1524 alphabet (targets/lopehurtado1523/key_1524.tsv) back to the 1522 letters by re-reading R9656 f. 334 (uncribbed) off the image in 1524 notation. 'xug ∠84αx7 zar ε&∂ yun ʒ∂' = 'la venida de los franceses' on an exact count, with 1524 values a/e/n/l/i and codes zar, xug, yun unchanged; the phrase recurs on l.1-2 and 'sub ∠α84..' = 'si vien-' is echoed by the clear 'si vienen franceses'. New sign ∠ = v. Shows the 1522 and 1524 alphabets are one; the 1522 'L = i' was a transcription collision.

Checked the NOTES claim that R9634, R9646 and R9649 were never attempted. Out of date for two: read_r9646.md and read_r9649.md already existed from an earlier session that did not update NOTES or the profile. R9649 is not uncribbed either: f. 268r is the clerk's clear of the whole letter. Only R9634 was untouched.

Transcribed the whole cipher of R9634 (ff. 14r-15v, 75 manuscript lines) from the three DECODE openings at 1.5x crops, in the 1524 sign names plus the R9646/R9649 names, appending line by line to r9634_cipher.txt. 1174 symbols measured (r9634_tokens.txt). The date and place (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522) come from the clear close on f. 16r.

Applied the merged 1524 key (lopehurtado1523/key_merged.tsv), the 1522 code groups and the R9649/R9646 sign values to R9634 with a new letter mode of decode.py. Coverage 77% confirmed, 92% with probable values on the first pass; the function-word spine and the alphabet read unchanged (seiscientos hombres de armas, tomarle esto que estava en su mano, del mundo).

Read R9634 line by line (r9634_reading.tsv). Context forced new values: ɋ = r (tierra x3, 'una tierra fertil' exact), z after a code = plural s (xul z los, xud z hombres, xob z yal z grandes exercitos), yob = ducado ('lxx U yob z' = 70,000 ducats after 'serian menester cada mes'), xep = mar ('los de la xep y los de la tierra'), xu = gente ('la xu darmas'; conflicts the 1524 xu = ha-), zar∂ = des- (destruir). Content: Geronimo Adorno's plan for Charles V and Henry VIII to invade France through Provence, 600 men-at-arms and 70,000 ducats a month, in March, kept secret.

Hypothesis that the groups standing right after the run opener Ꮒ are nulls: ʃta, ɡʇo/ɣ̊ʇ/ʑto, ʆ∂, yt, yω. Tested against the one crib that covers such a run (R9649 f. 268: nothing for 'Ꮒ yω ʃta') and against sentence closure in R9634 (14r13, 14v07, 14v14, 14v17, 15r20, 15v07) and R9646 (runs 4 and 5). Holds in every context; ʃta confirmed, the others probable.

Measured R9634: 842 of 1191 cipher tokens in words read as sense = 71% (f.14r 74%, f.14v 63%, f.15r 77%, f.15v 66%); lm.best_language on the read text returns es-modern first. Valued by the key 80% confirmed / 94% with probable, so about a quarter of tokens carry values but do not form words: spelled words with one sign at the 8/ϑ, ∂ s/p/t or ε l/g limit, and about 45 codes seen once.

Retried R9646 at 1.5x: run 4 'o-i-e-se' is 'o-v-i-e-se' = oviese (second sign ∠, not α); 'Ꮒ ʃta' and 'Ꮒ ʑto ɡto' are opener + nulls; 'sed z' = sus with the plural z. Re-counted 121 tokens (not 118) and measured 97 read as sense = 80%. ʙ∠89&Ho, zip, zob, δ8ǝtoo, ʃof and the close ʙ∠47 ɣ?8δHo still fail.
Measured R9649 against its own clear (f. 268): 89/89 tokens read as sense once yω ʃta are taken as nulls. Probable values inside it: ti, ϭ, ♀, ⅋, ƀ.

Looked for a crib for R9634 and R9646 in CSP Spain ii (Bergenroth): the 2026-09-21 full-text search found no Hurtado letter of Sept-Nov 1522 calendared, so neither has a printed summary; no clear version in either record. Failed as a crib source.

Re-transcribed R9645 (f. 243r all 17 lines, f. 243v ll. 1-10) from the DECODE images at 1.5x in the R9634 notation into r9645_cipher.txt; glossed lines 13-21 converted from the 2026-09-21 pass. 489 tokens. Checked the facing f. 242v 'Claro': it is the end of R9644's clear (Ostia fortress), no crib here.

Applied key_1522_r9634.tsv plus the merged 1524 key to R9645. The unglossed f. 243r now reads as the terms of Adrian VI's capitulation with Ferrara: assiento con el duque de Ferrara (m̶8ɋ7ɣ̊Ho), tres condiciones, del feudo que el papa Alexandro, cient hombres de armas, confederarse si no con su Sd e con V. Mt., recoger deservidores. Valued 84% confirmed / 98% with probable.

Tested the null-after-Ꮒ hypothesis on R9645's contemporary glosses: the glossator writes nothing for 'Ꮒ ɣto' before yi = dize, nor for 'Ꮒ ɣto ʃta' between 'la gente de v. mgd' and 'no'. ɣto upgraded to confirmed; the earlier guess 'hasta agora' for this run is withdrawn. The gloss 'al duque de Albania' sits over yib (duque), resolving the old yub = duque conflict as a misread; 'la gente' over 'xup xu' confirms xu = gente.
Measured R9645: 358 of 489 tokens read as sense = 73% (f. 243r 70%, f. 243v 77%), against 57% confirmed coverage / about 47% read on 2026-09-21.

Regraded R9656 with the null openers (∂6 ʃta, three places) and the R9634 values, on a token file built from its 2026-09-21 1524-notation transcription (not re-read from the image): 131 of 214 = 61% read as sense, against about 47%. Lines 13-18 still fail on spelled words.

Retried every unread group of R9634 against the extended key (R9645 and R9656 values). Only two gains: xug xu = la gente in 14v23, and yɩ ɣ̊ = yiL + r = hazer (probable, from R9645 'no puede yiL') in 15r20. 846 of 1191 = 71%. The other unread groups (about 45 codes) occur once and do not recur with a crib in any sibling; ze, yel, ʃun, ʃud stay open.

Looked for better images. DECODE, with the logged-in cookie: the full-size file IMG_R9634_I45360_P1.jpg is the 1,427,572-byte copy already in img/; .png, .tif, ORIG_ and page-less names return the 5,244-byte placeholder. RAH Biblioteca Digital: behind an Anubis proof-of-work bot check, not passed by the session; web search finds no 9/26 or A-26 record. Needs Daniel in a browser.

Sanuto, Diarii t. XXXIII (archive.org idiariidimarinos33sanu, full text) grepped for Provenza, Lion, Adorno, Urtado as a crib for R9634's Provence plan: nothing on the plan. CSP Spain ii already searched (no Hurtado letters Sept-Nov 1522).

Pooled every unread code of R9634, R9645, R9646 and R9656 against the 21 letters of lopehurtado1523 (decode_merged.py --kwic). Only ze (= el, four contexts), zer (= hazer), yin (= fue) recur with sense; xer (mucho?) and zif (capitan?) left possible. About 60 codes occur nowhere else.

New wordmatch.py: expands each unread spelled word over the set of letters each sign has been read as in this hand and looks every expansion up in a Spanish lexicon (Quijote, Vasto memorias, Gutenberg Spanish). Accepted only where the sentence also takes the word: sostener, tenia, ser, vio, vivo (R9634), real, hara (R9645). No match for R9646's or R9656's unread words, i.e. each holds a misread sign.

Remeasured: R9634 872/1191 = 73.2% (was 71.0%), R9645 368/489 = 75.3% (73.2%), R9646 80% and R9656 61% unchanged, R9649 100%; all five 1557/2104 = 74%. The 95% target is not reachable without the RAH images or a clear copy of these letters.

Re-transcribed R9656 f. 334r and the f. 334v cipher runs from the DECODE images at 1.5x in the R9634 notation (r9656_cipher.txt, 225 tokens). Corrections: old ʒ mostly ɣ̊ (r); the l. 1 'ω' is a line-break hyphen; ∂6 = opener Ꮒ.

Decoded with the pooled key and checked against the faded f. 335r copy: f. 334v 'que esta muy sospechoso (z&∂⊃8ɣ3&∂m, exact) el papa que de alla (zub) se le haya mandado (ϯ74xHo9&, exact) lo que ha fecho' read in full; f. 334r adds no quiere el papa, que hara el papa, me ha dicho, de perder, la cosa del mundo que mas, de lo que truxiere. 177/225 = 78.7% read as sense (was 61.2%). Ten spelled runs still give no word.

outcome.method_basis: The key was rebuilt by aligning the cipher of R9644 (ff. 238-239) with the clerk's full contemporary clear version bound in the same record (ff. 241-242, 'Claro', keyed by marginal letters A-C), then with the second clear version in R9650 (f. 272); the 1524 alphabet from lopehurtado1523 (itself rebuilt here) was applied back only as a later check.
outcome.notes: Unpublished cipher, opened 2026-09-20. TWO records carry the clerk's own full contemporary clear version - R9644 (ff. 241-242, in lettered sections keyed to the cipher) and R9650 (f. 272) - and R9648 is R9644's duplicate. R9652 carries no cipher at all - DECODE's 'partially decrypted' is wrong, the leaf is entirely in the clear - and is read complete too. Those four letters are therefore READ COMPLETE as to content (read_r9644.md, read_r9650.md): the Pope Adrian VI temporising between Charles V and Francis I, the French resolved to come into Italy with a great sum of money to Lyon, Hieronymo Adorno's intercepted letters, the Pope's parsimony and his unpaid household, the peace track through the archbishop of Bari. The CIPHER is read in part: 47 CODE values fixed against that plaintext and 29 probable (the 10 substitution-alphabet signs were downgraded to probable on 20 Sept after an 8x zoom showed signs that must be different letters looking near-identical at the zoom they were read at; the code groups, being plain latin trigrams that cross-check, are unaffected), kept apart in a confidence column and audited for conflicts. The key reads outside its own evidence - two thirds of tokens on sight in R9648 and R9650, and 'el papa' unaided in R9656, which has no clear version and no duplicate. Open: the five records with no clear version (R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656), and a word-perfect edition of any ciphered leaf, which needs the substitution alphabet - all ten alphabet signs probable after the 8x zoom on perdido, the rest limited by per-glyph discrimination on these scans. 2026-10-02: R9634 (Genoa, 13 Sept 1522, Adorno's Provence plan) transcribed and read in part, 71% of tokens measured; R9646 80%; R9649 read in full from its own clear f. 268 (it had been listed as uncribbed). New: ɋ = r, plural z after codes, yob ducado, xu gente, nulls after the opener Ꮒ (ʃta confirmed). Retry 2026-10-02: R9645 73% (re-transcribed, f. 243r = Ferrara capitulation terms), R9656 61% (regraded), R9634 71%; ɣto null and xu = gente confirmed on R9645's glosses. 2026-10-03: fraction_read 0.74 = tokens read as sense over the five measured uncribbed-or-own-clear letters R9634, R9645, R9646, R9649, R9656 (1557/2104); the cribbed R9644/R9648/R9650 are read complete as to content via their clear versions. 2026-10-03 (later): R9656 re-transcribed, 61% -> 79%; fraction_read 0.76 (1603/2115 over the five measured letters).

reading_review.note: read_r9644.md is the clerk's contemporary clear version (ff. 241-242) transcribed as continuous Spanish, sections A-C, abbreviations expanded; it reads complete. It is the reading of the cipher of R9644 and its duplicate R9648, whose ciphered leaves are not token-transcribed.

texts.summary: Hurtado's running account of Adrian VI: the Pope's good will but unsatisfying deeds, his parsimony while he waits for the archbishop of Bari, the payment of the papal household before the other side buys it, the French King's request for a safe-conduct for an ambassador, and a leak of letters shown in copy in Castile. Read from the clerk's contemporary clear version (ff. 241-242); no full transcription of the ciphered leaves was made, only the passages aligned in NOTES.md.

reading_review.note: read_r9650.md is the contemporary clear version transcribed as continuous Spanish; it reads as sentences with few holes.

texts.summary: The French are resolved to come into Italy and send a great sum of money to Lyon; Hieronymo Adorno has intercepted letters; the Pope, urged to act, answers lukewarmly and will not declare himself. Read from the clerk's clear version on f. 272; the ciphered leaves (ff. 269-271) are transcribed only in the passages aligned in NOTES.md.

texts.summary: A letter entirely in clear: the licenciado Bernardino, a 'gran bellaco', has turned up in Rome and Adrian VI declines a night arrest in the city; the viceroy of Naples' news of the siege of Rhodes is forwarded in copy.

texts.summary: Four months after the imperial sack of Genoa, Hurtado reports a plan put to him by Geronimo Adorno: the Emperor and the King of England should make war on the King of France through Provence, his weakest land, with six hundred men-at-arms, light horse and soldiers at 70,000 ducats a month, settled now for March; an early form of the 1524 Provence invasion.

texts.label: R9646, Rome, [Nov 1522] (f. 252r)
texts.note: Re-read 22 Oct 2026 (batch b13; texts/R9646_reading.md, texts/R9646_en.md, texts/R9634-R9656_reread_log.md): clean share 0.727 on the whole letter, carried by the clear; of the five cipher runs, 1-3 read (the Pope concerted with Ferrara, en lo de la [?decima]); run 4 (abia miedo que oviese de [...] en [...]) and run 5 (ofrecer [...] al papa para sus necesidades ... por dinero [?hara] toda [...]) keep their holes, so what the Pope feared and what was to be offered are lost. Blockers: no-key-material (zip, zob, ʃof seen once) and needs-physical-access (an unkeyed looped sign opens ð∠89&Ho and ð∠47; DECODE has no larger image, the RAH library is behind a bot check).
texts.summary: Adrian VI has concluded his settlement with Alfonso d'Este, duke of Ferrara, and a copy of the capitulation is being sent; Charles's request meets papal caution, and the archbishop [of Bari] advises an offer of money for the Pope's needs.

texts.label: R9649, Rome, 9 Nov 1522 (ff. 266-268)

reading_review.note: read_r9649.md: the three cipher runs decode word for word against the clerk's clear version on f. 268 (como el Cardenal de Santa Cruz le mata por Ostia; que el licenciado Bernardino); 89 of 89 tokens read. Verified 23 Oct 2026 (reading audit v2): the 0.51 figure was the whole file with its sign tables; the running reading alone (closing formula now written out from the image instead of '...') scores 0.933 plain and 1.0 on explicit holes (15 sentences); the three cipher runs align word for word with the clerk's clear version on f. 268 (checked on IMG_R9649_I45434_P1/P3); no word supplied, the probable sign values are confirmed by that clear version.

texts.summary: Adrian VI asks Charles V to write urging him to garrison Ostia and give the fortress to no one, since Cardinal Santa Cruz (Carvajal) presses for it by seniority; the licenciado Bernardino has landed from Barcelona and hides at his brother's house. The cipher runs are deciphered and aligned with the contemporary clear version on f. 268.

system.summary: Three-letter consonant-vowel-consonant nomenclator codes mixed inline with clear Spanish, with homophones at code level (ta and tu both = 'no'), codes used for syllables as well as whole words, and long words spelled letter by letter between the codes.
system.sibling_key: Alonso Sanchez's 1522 Venice cipher and Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher, both reconstructed by Tomokiyo; same design, provably different values (xul = 'lo' here, 'despues' in Sanchez).

prior_solution.where: Bergenroth, CSP Spain vol. 2 (1866) nos. 548 (R9667) and 617 (R9846) abstract two of the letters from their contemporary decipherments; the other six are not calendared. No modern decipherment found.

conditions.human_role: queued the catalogue entry; DECODE login cookie reused from an earlier target.

solution.what: Grepped Bergenroth CSP Spain vol. 2 (1523-24 sections, british-history.ac.uk) for each record's Salazar folio. R9667 = no. 548 (A.28 ff. 6-9, 5 May 1523, 'Autograph in cipher. Contemporary deciphering'); R9846 = no. 617 (A.30 ff. 130-133, 5 Feb 1524). Other six folios not calendared.

Fetched the 8 DECODE records and 17 images. Dates read off the documents: R9695 is 8 July 1523, not June; four records are Feb-Mar 1524 (Salazar A-30), not 1523; two are addressed to a "muy Illustre senor", not the Emperor.
Same cipher as the 1522 Hurtado letters (targets/lopehurtado/): the code groups ton, zar, xul, rab, taf, yub, teg, xug recur on every leaf.
Found two bound-in contemporary clears: R9667 f. 9v 'Claro' leaf for sections A and B, and R9846 f. 133r clear version of a letter almost wholly in cipher.

Tried R9667's bound 'Claro' leaf as a crib: it is mirrored and docketed 'Del abbad de Najera a dos de mayo', so it belongs to another letter. Transcribed the six cipher runs; codes only give fragments (a request for benefices for the Pope's servants); 4ʃL∂8ɛ probable 'provea'.

Aligned R9846 ff. 130r-130v cipher (38 lines) against the contemporary clear on f. 133r, clause for clause. 105 values (65 confirmed, 40 probable) in key_1524.tsv; most of the homophonic letter alphabet recovered from exact-count spelled runs; 1522 letter values 4=n, 8=e, 7=a, m=o re-confirmed; 25 1522 codes re-confirmed. Contradictions: L sits as r (1522: i), tef in a 'nec-' slot (1522: paz).

Applied key_1524 to R9683, R9695, R9867 (no crib). R9867 (all cipher) dated by its own spelled date line: Rome, 4 Jan 1524; frame reads (Beaurain, money), ~30 code groups unknown. R9683 (10 June 1523) and R9695 (8 July 1523, draft) cipher runs yield fragments only. New probable: 3=h, tuf=Roma.

Applied the key to R9869, R9866, R9868. Dates fixed from subscriptions: 28 Mar, 28 Feb, 20 Mar 1524; R9866 and R9868 to Gattinara. R9869 ~2/3 reads, R9868 f.430r mostly, R9866 a quarter to a third. New: barred m = f (confirmed), tef = nec- confirmed three times (1522: paz).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 2868 tokens, 150 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.148 per letter; random keys -3.719 (z 6.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.509 (mean -2.517, z 29.4); annealer on the real text -2.196. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): eight records: cipher files r96*/r98*_cipher.txt; transcriptions of R9866/R9868/R9869 copied from their read_*.md to texts/; decryptions read_*.md, R9846 clear + alignment, R9667 alignment + retry; key_1524*.tsv, key_1523*.tsv, key_merged.tsv, key_retry.tsv.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). read_r*.md, r9667_alignment.md and retry_2026-09-21.md read: in every letter but R9846 the clear text reads and the cipher runs give word pieces with […] gaps in nearly every clause (R9667: five of six runs unread; R9683: 'cipher mostly unread'; R9867: gaps in every clause). Seven letters relabelled decoded, not read. R9846's transcribed cipher is covered clause for clause by the clerk's clear on f. 133r, which reads (reading_review A). Method key recovered based on adjacent plaintext -> read from existing decipherment (parts); fraction_read 0.45 -> ~0.23 (estimated).

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b07). Existing text sought: no contemporary decipherment on any DECODE image of the seven unread letters (CSP Spain ii 548 says R9667 had one, not imaged); CSP calendars only R9667 and R9846; web search 22 Oct found nothing. The RAH Biblioteca Digital answers only through an Anubis proof-of-work bot check, not passed, so better images of Salazar A-28/A-30 were not checked.

Every cipher run of R9866, R9867, R9868, R9869, R9683 and R9667 re-read on full-resolution crops of the DECODE images (b07_crop.py), and the f. 444v clear of R9869 transcribed in full. Look-alikes resolved word by word (<doc>_corrections.tsv): the ß-like a was transcribed ʇʇ (r) in a dozen words; y ʇʇ is one sign ɣ̶ (g: coligados, enemigos, colegio, alargar); m̶ is f or c, ʒ is p; xab -> rab, ʒul -> zul, zaf -> yaf, y m̶ -> ym (fue) in R9869.

Code groups from new contexts (probable, key files unchanged): zm = como (R9867 l21, R9866 R14), ʃeg = tengo (R9866 R14 "como tengo escrito", R9869 R7), zub = alla (1522 value; R9866 R5 "la costa de alla", R9867 l23), zad probably a look-alike of zed = arçobispo (R9868 R7 after the clear "partida del señor arçobispo de Capua"). In R9683/R9667 the 1522 sign values & = o, H = e, ɭb = p, ∠ = v give "Theodorico", "servi[ci]o", "pensava", "declare", "era del que mas se".

Readings built sentence by sentence (<doc>_reading.md, English <doc>_en.md) and aligned word by word with the decodes (words fixed: R9869 bueno -> [?bueno], R9868 a -> [?a], R9866 como/tiene -> [?…]). Clean share of the reading bodies (b07_score.py): R9866 0.667, R9868 0.638, R9869 0.622 (read, grade B); R9867 0.389 (decoded, not read); R9683 0.636 and R9667 0.767 on the whole letter but kept decoded, not read because their cipher passages do not build sentences; R9695 not attempted further. English for R9846 (read since the audit) written: R9846_en.md.

reading_review.note: The transcribed cipher (ff. 130r-v, c05-v17, 768 tokens) is covered clause for clause by the clerk's contemporary clear on f. 133r (r9846_clear.txt), which reads as continuous Spanish; the alignment (r9846_alignment.md) confirms the match. texts.label: R9866, Rome, 28 Feb 1524, to Grand Chancellor Gattinara (9/30 ff. 285-286)
texts.summary: To Gattinara: Beaurain's coming was timely; the French mean, by craft or force, to stay on this side of the Alps, and the Emperor must not lose the world's respect while he spends so much on the war; Hurtado asks Gattinara's help to be paid what he is owed. reading_review.note: Clean share 0.667 (b07_score.py, reading body).
