title: Charles III of Lorraine to the comte de Vaudémont, Nancy, 18 June 1592, BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (DECODE R9449)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3621 no. 97, fol. 109 (Gallica btv1b52524472n, canvas 227; DECODE R9449)

plaintext.source: A contemporary 'Coppie' with the cipher left in; DECODE R9449 non-decrypted; no. 22 in the same volume is a plaintext decipherment of other (January) letters, with no cipher, so no crib.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF, per-line crops at about 1.5x native (lc/), after shear deskew -0.031
transcription.notes: _check_profile.py --measure --drop-first gives 1,153 tokens / 94 distinct because it counts the 34 inline clear words in [[ ]] and 10 punctuation marks; excluding those gives 1,109 cipher tokens (1,071 letter symbols in 44 forms + 38 nomenclator figures in 14 values), as NOTES states. About a quarter of glyph identifications are still wrong (merge-control calibration), so the transcription is the limit.

system.summary: Reciprocal letter-pair substitution written in ordinary cursive letterforms (a/i b/p c/f d/q e/t g/u l/y m/z n/s o/r h/x), two dots under a letter for a doubled letter, a null (looped ae), a few special signs, and figures for syllables and words (31 = ma, 139 = vous, 145 = me, 141 = qu'il); λ, γ, U, π, m̄ are nulls.

diacritics.note: Crossbar, overbar and dots on a letterform make a distinct cipher symbol.

system.sibling_key: Four 1592 key sheets in the Nevers key book fr. 3995 (ff. 32, 83-84, 98, 103) examined and eliminated; no Lorraine key on DECODE, Cryptiana or in print. None used.
system.notes: Re-read 22 Sept 2026 (ct/no97_reread.txt, ct/no97_reading2.md): the 18 Sept key's values paired reciprocally, and the pair key with the c/e and b/h splits reads the letter. Special signs λ, m̄, U, E, π, γ, ꝗ, figure-4 mostly unresolved.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved.htm, entry 'Duke of Lorraine (1592)', marked Solved: 'I solved this in 2025', quoting only the opening ("J'ay este infiniment mal satisfait du peu d'execution ...."); no key or text published. Present in the 6 Sept 2026 snapshot (targets/napoleon/unsolved.htm), before the 18 Sept attempt. DECODE R9449 still 'Non-decrypted'; no key anywhere.

conditions.human_role: Outside contribution: the work was done and committed by GitHub user aryasn2026 (git author of all three commits) and merged as pull request #4 after review (docs/lorraine1592.html). What the contributor did beyond running the model is not recorded. The NOTES ask the user to verify the DECODE queries, the Charles II/III identification and every transcription.

solution.what: Verify step: looked for the ciphered originals of the January intercepts in fr. 3621; no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment only, no cipher in the volume to pair it with.
Key sought in DECODE (8 records for fr. 3621), Cryptiana, HistoCrypt, BnF notices, Lepage 1864: none published; other Lorraine keys are different systems.
Four 1592 key sheets in fr. 3995 whose DECODE profile matched (ff. 32, 83-84, 98, 103) fetched and eliminated on their own evidence.
Shear-deskew line finder segments 20 lines / 1,114 glyphs; clear text of nos. 22 and 97 transcribed; unsupervised shape clustering of the glyphs.
Homophonic annealer (solve.py) against a Montaigne 4-gram model on the clustered glyphs: -2.78/char against -1.85 for real French.
Glyphs recognised as ordinary cursive letterforms and transcribed by eye from 42 half-line crops: 1,071 letter symbols in 44 forms and 38 figures (ct/no97_eye.txt).
Old annealer on a control with a known key recovers only 37-56% (true key -1.62 vs found -2.64): the search, not the model, had failed.
Steepest-ascent iterated local search (search.py) recovers known keys at 98.7-99.6%; free nulls and degenerate all-e keys identified as traps and blocked.
Search on the manuscript: key stable across seeds and under a locked crib, -2.10/char; words produced unprompted (munitions, prisonniers, secours, quartiers, conserver la plaine).
Eight-symbol group reading 'chasteau' at lines 15 and 19, with Chasteauvillain twice in the clear on the page; one symbol short (chasteauilains), so eight letters secure and six probable.
Null test: same pipeline on five shuffled ciphertexts gives 0-3 distinct French words of 6+ letters (mean 1.2) against 33 for the manuscript.
Noise and systematic-merge controls: the -2.10 score matches 6-12 merged glyph pairs, i.e. about 65-75% of letters correct; the transcription limits the reading.

The 18 Sept key's values pair reciprocally (a/i, o/r, d/q, n/s); tested as an 11-pair reciprocal alphabet a/i b/p c/f d/q e/t g/u l/y m/z n/s o/r h/x with the transcription's c split into e (t) and c (f), B into b (p) and h (x), dots = doubled letter, ae = null: lowercase-only decode turns into French (infiniment mal satisfait du peu d'execution; conserver la plaine).

Native IIIF image of f227 sheared -0.031, 21 line bands cut into 5 crops each at 2.3x; every cipher line re-read against the pair key, glyph choices (e/c, b/h, dotted forms) decided with the key in hand; word-graded transcription ct/no97_reread.txt (1,105 tokens).
Nomenclator figures from context: 31 = ma (com-31-nder, de-31-nde, 31 resolution), 139 = vous (chemins, 139 tiendres), 145 = me (affin que 141 ne 145 delaissent); the other 11 figures unassigned.
fr. 3621 notice searched for sibling Lorraine/Vaudemont cipher pieces: none (ciphered pieces are Birago 31/36, Potier 79, Dinteville 114/116).

measure_reread.py: 790/1,105 cipher tokens in words graded H/C = 0.715 (letters 0.721, figures 21/38); the 18 Sept key+tokens give the same words for 449/1,105 = 0.406; 4 emendations (two omitted v in Chasteau(v)ilain, q(u)e, promesses).

Review of Tomokiyo's unsolved list against the repo: his entry marks R9449 solved by him in 2025 and quotes the opening; the entry predates this project's attempt (6 Sept snapshot). The opening he quotes matches our reading's first line word for word (ct/no97_reading2.md L00). Prior claim missed by the 18 Sept search, which looked only for a published key.
Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): Lasry notes Tomokiyo had already solved it (2025); not a first break, dropped from the ciphertext-only list for Klaus Schmeh; marked independent re-solution.

Checked whether measure_reread.py counts sense: it counts hand grades H/C and only checks them against the key decode. New measure_sense.py tests every H/C word against an attested French lexicon (shared lang corpora fr-henri4, fr-1520s-diplomatic, fr-gutenberg) and the fr-1600-letters LM: 692/1,105 = 0.626 attested on the 22 Sept file (0.70 once single/double consonants are folded); the gap is spelling variants plus a few fragments.

Full-resolution IIIF f227 re-fetched, sheared -0.031, lines re-cropped and unread stretches re-read at 2x: L18 'l'effect du dict Chasteau(v)ilain', L12-13 'induiront et resolument', L04 'le mander' (not demander), L01 final gamma, L02 'pioniers' without the inserted c.
Figure 141 pooled over its three occurrences: 141+m(z) 'qu'ilz avoient fait', 141+J(s) 'qu'ils connoissent', 'affin qu'ils ne me delaissent': 141 = qu'il.

λ, γ, U, π, m̄ as nulls: of 37 occurrences all but two stand between complete words and the sentence reads without them (faire U passer, faire γ æ passer, fauldra λπ le remettre, satisfait m̄ du peu).

Joint coordinate-ascent solve of 17 special signs (single letters, nulls or common words) under fr-1600-letters on the whole text: the optimum changes with the per-char length penalty (1.6/2.0/2.4) and fills the text with 'pour'/'de'; per-sign lexicon test non-discriminating.
Context values ŧ/m̄/α + 'ien' = bien/rien/combien, E = la, 98 = ville: each fits some occurrences but not all, or other words fit equally; not counted.

measure_reread.py on the 5 Oct file: 861/1,102 = 0.781; fragments quelq, auld+is, promes fail the lexicon check and were downgraded to M: final 844/1,102 = 0.766 (letters 0.771, figures 24/38); measure_sense.py 787/1,102 = 0.714.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 823 tokens, 68 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -1.635 per letter; random keys -4.932 (z 6.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.752 (mean -2.841, z 27.0); annealer on the real text -2.321. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): eye transcription ct/no97_eye.txt and the graded re-read ct/no97_reread.txt (5 Oct, reading of record), the running text ct/no97_reading2.md and the clear text; the pair key copied from no97_reading2.md §1 and NOTES §10 to texts/key.md.

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). ct/no97_reading2.md §2 and ct/no97_reread.txt read: about one sign in four is unread and nearly every line carries a [?] gap or an unvalued figure; fragments parse ('infiniment mal satisfait du peu d'execution', 'pour y commander et conserver la plaine'), sentences do not (docs/_check_reading.py: 37 of 96 sentences clean in the running text, 0 of 20 in the graded file; only the clear text reads). Relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method key recovered from ciphertext-only -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read 0.766 -> 0.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, b29): DECODE R9449 (one image, no attachment) and R9444 (no. 22, plaintext decipherment of the January letters) re-opened; Tomokiyo's unsolved page re-checked (opening only, unchanged); DECODE record list and ciphertext metadata searched for Lorraine/Vaudémont/Nancy keys: none; BnF key records of 1580-1600 listed and fr. 3623 no. 23 (R9453, Bienvenut to Nevers 1590) viewed: not this system.

The 5 Oct graded re-read rendered as running text (ct/no97_partial_reading.md) with the clear lines; standalone crossed t adopted as a null (8 of 8 occurrences between complete words); G = que and j = null tested and not adopted. Score 0.069 -> 0.154 clean sentences; stays decoded, not read.

Method restored: key obtained by recovering the reciprocal letter-pair key from the ciphertext alone (key recovered from ciphertext-only); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

texts.label: fr. 3621 no. 97, Nancy, 18 June 1592
texts.summary: A contemporary copy of Charles III of Lorraine's letter to his son the comte de Vaudémont, with clear French and cipher alternating on the same lines. The Duke is infinitely ill satisfied with the little execution of the promises of pioneers and munitions made to him, urges his son to press the attempt on Chasteauvillain, and writes of putting someone there to command and hold the plain and of bringing his army back to quarters. The volume is the duc de Nevers's intercept and correspondence file for 1591-92.

One sign in five is still open (special signs, ten figures, garbled runs) and most sentences have two or more holes. Blocker: no-key-material: DECODE R9449 has one image and no attachment, Tomokiyo has published only the opening, and no key with this reciprocal pair system was found on DECODE (list and ciphertext metadata searched; BnF keys of 1580-1600 listed, fr. 3623 no. 23 viewed) or in fr. 3995.

texts.summary: Henri IV to Maisse, his ambassador at Venice: Cardinal de Gondi has passed near Venice and the marquis de Pisany follows him to the Pope for the Catholic royalists, so Maisse must stay at his post; Lambert returns to the Levant with the despatch for Brèves, which Maisse may amend; the King approves Maisse's warnings to the English ambassador and Brèves; the King of Spain's ambition; Lesdiguières's war in Piedmont and the help the Italian friends should give; the Pope's resolutions are awaited. The whole cipher passage is transcribed group by group and aligned with the contemporary Brienne 13 copy (97.6% letter agreement).

texts.label: f. 373, 7 Nov 1592 (figures of the whole cipher transcribed and aligned with the Brienne 13 fol. 104v-106v clear copy)
texts.summary: Henri IV acknowledges Maisse's letter of 4 October and will wait for the outcome of the Gondi and Pisany mission; urges the Venetian friends to help him with money and to work on the Pope, since only his person can preserve the Crown; approves Maisse's handling of the third-party (tiers parti) rumour; the duc de Retz has left without funding the Swiss, the League expects reinforcements while Parma is ill; Lesdiguières must be supported in Piedmont; Brèves has the Levant charge and Maisse is asked to stay at Venice a little longer. A clear postscript announces Joyeuse's defeat and death before Villemur.

system.summary: The numerical letters use German homophonic substitution and a nomenclator, while the separate ten-line alphabetic block uses repeating shifts 4,5,3,6,2 over abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz with unresolved exceptional code groups.
system.sibling_key: none: 176 HCPortal key records of the Marburg key volumes checked; the Sixtinus key (HCPortal key 5, Dec 1635) has the same layout but a different table
system.notes: Numerical system: 89 two-digit groups, about 20 digraph signs, about 45 codes (151 tokens), a few name signs; numerical assignments are not alphabetically ordered. Alphabetic system: a=0, subtract shifts 4,5,3,6,2 modulo 24 continuously across lines, starting at phase 0. 43, 45 and LL advance zero modulo five in the selected treatment; this establishes neither expansion length nor referent. Annotation [E?]: Sixt: / cla: remains tentative and unexpanded.

This records the contributor stage, not a changed account of the earlier numerical attack.

solution.what: Fetched the ten HCPortal records and 18 original scans of HStAM 4 h 1411 through api.hcportal.eu.
Harvested all 176 HCPortal cipher-key records of the Marburg key volumes with their users; no Malsburg key. Keys 5 (Sixtinus 1635), 30, 38 and 49 compared with f. 3.
f. 3 transcribed by hand from 2x line crops (455 groups).
Homophonic annealing of f. 3 alone against de-1640s, with and without a letter-frequency penalty.
Remaining pages transcribed by two agents in the same format (about 9,000 more groups); ff. 30-31 found to duplicate ff. 28-29.
Annealing ff. 3+12+18 (1,575 groups): all four restarts converged on the same key and German text (das ich auch noch nit weiss ... garnisonen ... contributiones vom platten lande).
Letter signs valued from context: N/D ch, Y/G ei, Z/O st, W/P ss, L/A tt, R/C/E/M mm, X/j/J sch, H ll, S/F au, T/B ff, Q ai; single figures are numerals.
Digit table re-annealed and polished over all pages with the signs fixed: 23, 40, 75 corrected; rare groups 14, 17, 20, 33, 85 assigned.
Dictionary-segmentation measure; the same measure on shuffled keys gives 50-58%.
236 unread groups re-checked against the scans: 24 misreads and 2 doubled groups corrected, 210 confirmed as written.
Codes valued from context: 128 Cöln, 130 Hamburg, 188 die Staaten, 253 Regiment, 273 Compagnien (grade I).
f. 12 letter-cipher block: many-to-one and null-allowing annealing in German, Latin, French, Italian and Dutch; periodic IC for periods 1-15; Caesar shifts; HCPortal letter keys 2 and 105.
Web search for an edition of the Malsburg letters (Rommel, LAGIS); none found.
Reading measured: 9,338 of 9,736 cipher tokens in words (95.9%); 193 code/sign tokens open; 97.9% of the non-code text.

Integrated Larry Beck with ChatGPT's separate alphabetic investigation, preserving Bourdeau's original numerical work and provisional alphabetic input. The supplied revised edition and audit were inspected; this is an integration date, not a claimed first-discovery date.

Compared the preserved ten original lines with the selected image-reading branch and uncertainty apparatus. Legacy 531 raw letters include eight editorial-label letters, giving 523 ordinary cipher positions; the selected branch has 510. Separate model reading passes and six binary source choices remain explicitly qualified.

Reproduced the contributed decryption with alphabet abcdefghiklmnopqrstuwxyz, repeating subtraction 4,5,3,6,2, phase 0 and continuous line handling. Special labels are outside the stream. Re-encryption is only a consistency check; the public verifier does not independently authenticate source readings or historical identities.

Integrated the ten-line literal output separately from editorial German and English. Retained tqouppen, itzigdn, the er ... wurden anomaly, blot and source alternatives. Conditional opening and possible proposed-letter scope prevent treating dismissal, payment or troop movements as accomplished facts. No coherent-text percentage is asserted.

Integrated inspected documentary findings and their limits: Geyso p.99 n.2 paraphrases an uninspected Malsburg letter of 16 November 1636 concerning Melander and authority; retention letters complicate an actual-dismissal hypothesis. Koblenz 47/4400 is a catalogue lead for cipher codes, not an inspected matching key. No values for 43, 45 or LL established.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 9506 tokens, 119 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.066 per letter; random keys -5.639 (z 15.0); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.662 (mean -3.692, z 52.7); annealer on the real text -2.423. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per-record transcriptions ct/hcp*.txt and the folio files f0*.txt; decryption reading_segmented.txt (measured text, one block per folio) and work/reading_auto.txt for the address leaves; the alphabetic block from Larry Beck's alphabetic/ package; keys key.txt, codes.txt and the alphabetic key in alphabetic_reading.md.

title: Ferdinand I to Johann Malvezzi, Augsburg, 23 January 1548 (DECODE R366)

documents.shelfmark: Budapest, Hadtorteneti Intezet es Muzeum, Hadtortenelmi Leveltar, 1548/3 (DECODE R366)

plaintext.source: No decipherment in the manuscript and none found on the web (September 2026). Malvezzi's correspondence of 1548-1552 is printed in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (Munich 1995), which is not freely available online and was not consulted; the letter's content is probably in print there from the Vienna registry copy.

transcription.source: DECODE images IMG_R366_I3424-I3431, fetched with a saved DECODE session cookie
transcription.notes: Read directly from the images against the key. First pass 21 Sept (read_A.md, read_B.md); second pass 5 Oct 2026 re-transcribed every open stretch from full-resolution crops; reading_full.txt holds the full plaintext of the ciphered passages (514 plaintext words, nulls removed). No separate symbol transcription file. Cipher runs on pp. 1, 4, 5, 6, 7.

system.summary: Monoalphabetic homophonic cipher in graphic signs (alchemical and planetary signs, Greek and Latin letters with other values), two or three signs per common letter, numbers for doubled letters, and a short code list of syllables for the principals.
system.sibling_key: DECODE R367 (same shelfmark) and R386 (NSZL Quart. Lat. 2254. 15)
system.notes: The circle-on-a-stem family of signs is ambiguous between u, e/ae and (with a cross) t; resolved by Latin context. Some signs serve more than one letter in practice. Nomenclator: about 20 code syllables (ki=Rustanus, ka/ke=Passa, le=Charles V, Bi=king of France, Nas/Ras/ye=the Sultan, zes=Queen Isabella, zos=Frater George, Cad=Constantinople, Eb=orator), plus 50=bellum, 51=pax. Nulls are whole Latin-looking words inside the cipher (etiam, idcirco, atque, cum, Porro, Dar, Der, spo, spu) and the loose letters b, d, n, z and a Greek pi.

prior_solution.where: No decipherment on DECODE or the web. Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 (Munich 1995) prints the Ferdinand-Malvezzi correspondence of early 1548 (Ferdinand's instructions for Malvezzi, 24 Jan 1548, reportedly no. 62; Ferdinand to Justus de Argento, Augsburg 13 Feb 1548, no. 68, pp. 213-15, per Tracy 2021), so this 23 Jan 1548 letter is probably printed there around nos. 62-67 (c. pp. 190-212); number unconfirmed, edition not online, not consulted (checked 2026-09-21).

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, and set the target with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
tools: PIL (cropping and zooming the page images)

solution.what: Fetched the eight R366 images and the record metadata from DECODE with a saved cookie.

Web searches for a published decipherment of the letter and for the Ferdinand-Malvezzi ciphers. No decipherment found; identified Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 as the edition that probably prints the letter, not freely available online.
Searched the DECODE record list around R366 and found the key records R367 (same shelfmark) and R386, with transcriptions DOC_R367 and DOC_R386.
Calibrated the sign values on p. 1 against the key images (sermone, tecum, quod, propter, tractatum, nobiscum, constituendae, autor).
Read the cipher runs page by page from zoomed crops, two subagents in parallel on pp. 1/4/7 and pp. 5/6. p. 4 read almost in full, pp. 5-6 read, pp. 1 and 7 read in part.

Looked for the letter in Austro-Turcica 1541-1552 via web search, the H-Net review and footnotes in Tracy, 'The Logic of Kleinkrieg' (AHY 2021) and Gürkan/Levantine Heritage papers. The edition is not online (no Google Books/HathiTrust full view found). Established only its neighbours: instructions for Malvezzi 24 Jan 1548 (reportedly no. 62), Ferdinand to Justus de Argento 13 Feb 1548 = no. 68, pp. 213-15. The 23 Jan letter's own number and text could not be seen, so the reading is neither confirmed nor corrected.

Checked the old 0.83 measure: a mark count over read_A/read_B (word counted read unless marked [?]); it did not test Latin sense and left out p. 1 cipher lines 1-8. Wrote reading_full.txt and measure_sense.py (shared 'la' model: word-form test plus 9-word window above the 2nd percentile of corpus windows; shuffled-letter control).
Re-transcribed from full-resolution crops all of p. 1's cipher (ll. 1-10), p. 4 l. 1, the sese/ulciscantur lines and the last line, p. 5 open words, p. 6 l. 14 and ll. 15-26, and all of p. 7.

Added the hand's variant sign values from the read pages: looped g-sign = d, stemmed circle with looped foot = q (before u) / r, footed Pi = g, P with small circle below = o, pointed cap = l. With them p. 7 and the p. 6 foot read straight through (magistrum horologiorum; de gentibus nostris in confiniis; captives freed by the Sultan).

Corrected 9 writer's slips forced by context (pacr->pacis, Turcrum, uiciscantur->ulciscantur, comutum->computum, factorum->facturum, expona->exponas, manutenea->manutenendam, faciam->faciamus, ordinaria). Left unread: the banker's surname after Gulielmo (signs give Semaslia, person not identified), one two-sign group before nominatione on p. 6, two lone v signs (probably uel).

measure_sense.py: p1 41/41, p4 114/114, p5 156/158, p6 134/136, p7 64/65; overall 509/514 = 0.990 (0.973 without the 9 slip-corrected words). Control with letters shuffled within words: 19/514 = 0.037 (code words only).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): first-pass glyph-and-Latin line readings read_A.md / read_B.md as the transcription, reading_full.txt (second pass, 5 Oct) as the decryption; the key is DECODE R367 (k367.txt), not recovered here, so no key_file.

outcome.method_basis: The key is DECODE R367, a reconstruction filed at the same shelfmark (Military History Archive 1548/3), with a second copy R386; its sign values were calibrated on p. 1 and the cipher runs read from zoomed crops of R366.
outcome.notes: The substance is recovered in full: Ruestem Pasha's standing after the treaty; the French work to break the Habsburg-Ottoman peace because they dare not attack Charles V directly; Malvezzi's pay (2,800 + 1,500 ducats by Justus de Argento, a 3,000-ducat credit repayable at Venice); a master clockmaker to be brought by the secretary; what to answer about the frontier garrisons; and reciprocity for captives freed by the Sultan. Open: a banker's surname, one two-sign group, two lone v signs.

texts.label: R366, Augsburg, 23 Jan 1548, ciphered passages pp. 1, 4-7
texts.summary: Ferdinand I writes to his envoy at the Porte, Johann Malvezzi, in reply to four of his letters; the clear text is the routine complaint about border raids, and the cipher carries the delicate matters. Rüstem Pasha has drawn great hatred on himself as author and defender of the Habsburg-Ottoman peace; the French are working to wreck that peace because, not daring to attack Charles V with their own forces, they want the Sultan's resources turned against him; and Malvezzi is to receive 1,500 ducats a year and 4,300 ducats at once through the secretary Justus de Argento.

solution.what: Fetched R4500 with the session cookie; one page, German clear letter with 14 cipher lines, interlinear gloss on lines 1-4.
First token transcription from line crops; misread the gloss/cipher alignment.
Many-to-one annealing on de-1500s without word spaces: letter-frequency noise only.
EM alignment of gloss 'das kann dieses orths selber observiren' to cipher line 3; inconsistent mappings.
Downloaded all 126 records of the volume (R4452-R4577); compared sign alphabets R4467, R4491, R4520, R4525.
Re-transcribed all 14 lines from mid-resolution views keeping word spaces.
Annealing with word spaces, '12' as one unit, seeded und/under; produced 'entschuldigt', 'damit ich', 'underthenigst'.
Fixed 5=a, q=m, D=l, 2=s, X=b by context; then M=w, 8=o from the gloss.
Gloss phrases 'zumahl nicht', 'etwas tentiret werden', 'dieses orths halber', 'dagegen' come out of lines 3-5 with the rebuilt key.
Read lines 3-14; lines 1-2 do not decode as transcribed.
Second pass on lines 1-2: restored dropped initial signs; line 2 reads, line 1 opens 'die landts...'.

Correction reported while quotations were pulled for Lasry's list, checked on the scan at 3x: the first three signs of line 9 (F 6 12), marked unread as blotted, are clear and give 'ser' with the key unchanged, so 'die|ser ue st ung' = 'dieser Vestung' (9 = u/v) replaces the conjecture 'dieser [sachen]'; in line 11 the signs hidden by '...' after 'nochmals' give 's a l er' with a doubling bar on the triangle, so 'nochmals allerunderthenigst und underthenigst'. 14 of 538 signs unread (was 17).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 524 tokens, 21 types, de-1640s order 4: reading -2.212 per letter; random keys -5.481 (z 5.6); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.479 (mean -3.55, z 31.6); annealer on the real text -2.179. Verdict: pass.

Context: the truce of Majano expired 16 July 1435 and was extended; run 2 before 'es continuada daci a Tots Sants' = 'la treua [ab Castella]' as the leading crib.
Prior literature checked for a reading of the letter: nothing in print.
DECODE ACA keys: R10182 (1413) a jargon code; R10183, the 1437 Montcada-Amat alphabet, a different alphabet from the letter's.
Reg. 3226 (264 images) swept in full for sibling cipher: none.
Reg. 3224 (286 images) swept in full: no cipher.
Reg. 2693 (392 images) swept: no cipher signs or key, but 'Fuit expedita in cifra' entries including Alfonso to the queen, Gaeta 27 July 1435, 'In ciffra': a king-queen cipher in use that week.
Reg. 3113 (472 images) swept: no cipher. Cartas Reales Alfonso IV on PARES: no ciphered 1435 king-queen originals.

Printed 1429 Castile-war key (Cortes & Pons 1986) obtained and compared: alphabet does not carry over; nomenclator signs seem to match (regne d'Arago, Catalunya, rei de Castella, Navarra) as a hypothesis only.

Annealing, one sign = one letter, Catalan quadgram model, with and without the 1429 look-alike values and cribs (la treua, treua, tregua, castella, M z = es): every crib heavily penalised, output gibberish.

Matched control (control.py, control_out.txt): 60+60 synthetic Catalan texts in f. 59r's exact layout (runs of 11/14/17 signs, 39 letters + 3 word signs, 18+3 = 21 distinct), monoalphabetic and 1429-style homophonic keys, solve.anneal() unchanged (20 seeds x 200k). Recovered (>= 80% letters) 0/60 and 0/60; median accuracy 0.08 / 0.13; solver optimum above the true key in 120/120. A true 5-letter crib is penalised by median 42-46 (>= 35 in 79/120), as much as the target's cribs, so the crib penalties are not evidence against a monoalphabetic cipher.

outcome.method_basis: The 42-sign runs on reg. 3225 f. 59r fit neither the 1437 Montcada-Amat key (R10183) nor the 1429 Castile-war alphabet (Cortes and Pons 1986), and a matched control shows ciphertext-only solving fails at this length.
outcome.fraction_read_source: cipher.txt: 42 signs, none given a value (the nomenclator matches are a hypothesis)

gaps.detail: Matched control: the annealer recovers 0/120 synthetic texts of this exact layout and sign inventory, monoalphabetic or homophonic.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with a numeric nomenclator of common words and names (12 il, 13 qui, 14 que, 35 parce que, 76 le roi de Navarre).
system.doubled_letters: special sign for some (yy = ss, T= = m/mm)
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's published partial tables for Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1; used as the starting key and corrected on the leaves.
system.notes: 87 entries in key.json, 42 of them code groups (19 marked unidentified '+', 4 names '*'). Several signs are confusable by shape (i/n/s, s/i, e/u at 0.91-0.93 correlation), so at the level of reading the cipher behaves as polyphonic and the language model chooses. A three-cipher hypothesis was made and retracted: all nine leaves tested answer to Cipher-1. Split on 14 Oct 2026 (one key per entry): Matignon's Cipher-3 leaves (fr. 15572 f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179) are the entry matignon1586c3. f. 79r, once taken for a crib of 'Cipher-2', is Cipher-1 (the solved key reads it); the genuine Cipher-2 leaves fr. 15572 ff. 218-219 are not part of any entry (not attempted).

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana: partial key tables for Cipher-1 and short openings of ff. 143, 150, 154 and 'f. 111'; contemporary decipherments of sibling leaves (f. 14v in f. 15r, f. 18 in f. 19, ff. 78-79 in the margin). Contemporary clear copies of ff. 143, 149v-150 and 154r-v bound as ff. 155-157 of the same volume, overlooked here until Michael Brackx found them (issue #70, 21 Oct 2026). No printed decipherment found (17 Sept 2026).

solution.what: Checked Tomokiyo's list: ff. 110, 123-124, 143, 150, 154, 173, 196, 201 undeciphered in Cipher-1, with partial tables and short openings; deciphered siblings ff. 14/15, 18-21/19, 78-79, 91-92. No printed decipherment found.
Mapped folios to Gallica canvases (double-page openings, drifting offset, two foliations).
Re-derived the Cipher-1 key from Tomokiyo's table, checked against the f. 14v/f. 15r crib and the f. 143 cipher; added values not in his table.
f. 143 recto, 21 lines, in three passes (three, five, eight tiles a line); uniform line grid found to corrupt the second half and replaced.
f. 143r decoded with the key and the LM beam decoder: about two thirds read, agreeing with Tomokiyo's opening and running past it.
Word-aware decoder (wdec.py) tried against the character decoder on f. 143: no gain; residue is transcription.
ff. 196 and 201 identified as one despatch enciphered twice, with clear head and foot cribs.
f. 18 cipher / f. 19 clear decipherment pair found and verified (14 = que, 52 = plustost); labelled glyph exemplars mined from it.
Confusable figures measured at 0.91-0.93 correlation: not separable by shape, reading is polyphonic.
readleaf.py (segment, match exemplars, beam-decode) recovers about 70% of plaintext characters on the crib leaf; exemplars do not transfer to f. 143's hand.
Figure-unit arithmetic proposed code 82 = le Prince de Conde; later retracted (line 8 'z' was the page edge).
Those leaves decoded in stretches: pay crisis of April 1586, lenders refusing, siege report naming 'le mareschal de Matignon', Mayenne's plan for Gascony.
ff. 196 and 201 aligned: 57% identical figures, 8 runs of 8+; shuffled control 12%, no runs.
Claimed ff. 123-124 and f. 110 were two further ciphers, from figure-frequency profiles; a 'rouergue' pattern on f. 79r gave five values for 'Cipher-2'.
Solved key vs scrambled keys: ff. 123-124 -2.35 vs -2.50..-2.53 per figure; f. 110 +2.07 gap. Three-cipher claim and the f. 79r values retracted.
f. 78v margin decipherment: cribem.py seeded with the solved key reaches alignment 106 vs 3-41 for scrambles; the key recovers the margin text.
ff. 123-124 (4,278 figures) transcribed and decoded: f. 124r reads well, f. 124v in fragments, f. 123r badly.
f. 110: 1,699 figures transcribed at three and five columns; magnification not the limit.
f. 110: automated glyph segmentation and clustering (fails its control on f. 154), seeded solve (moves 23 of 27 labels off the key), cold solve (-2.27 per figure, no continuous French).

Coverage measured instead of estimated: measure.py decodes every transcription with key.json and the 6-gram model, counts a token read only if keyed and inside a >=3-word, >=10-letter lexical run, and runs a 3-seed scrambled-key control per leaf. Result 4,325/12,994 transcribed tokens (0.33), 0.28 of the whole target with untranscribed lines counted (0.22 chance-corrected); f. 110 scores at its scrambled floor. Also found: f. 196 has 31 cipher lines (26 transcribed), f. 177 has 29 (24 transcribed), and the 'f. 178v fourth hand' page is the f. 179 Cipher-3 slip bound upside down.

Split from the former combined target under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): the two Cipher-3 leaves (f. 276, fr. 15571 f. 179; alejandrozarco, PR #25) became matignon1586c3 with their steps and credit; George Lasry's f. 43 credit (a leaf outside this target) removed. (the f. 143 cipher, with 49 = comme), 'soubz vostre bon plaisir toutesfois' and 'Et aussi qu'il n'y avoit plus de hasard' legible; f. 155v ends 'Mr du Mayne de ... avril 1586' and begins 'Comme il estoit bien besoing ...' system.summary: Matignon's Cipher-3 (Tomokiyo's partial table): a homophonic substitution of graphic signs and figures for French letters, with word signs (60 faire, a beta-like sign de, 20 la, 18 le, p-with-stroke pour, C with n que, ∴ qui, ### et) and a null (plain v).

system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from matignon1586 under the one-key rule: that entry joined these two Cipher-3 leaves with the Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1 despatches. The two leaves share names (Iehan Durant, La Rousière) and belong together; deciphered siblings in the same key: f. 189 (in f. 190), ff. 277-278 (in ff. 279-280), f. 282 (margin). From 21 Oct 2026 the entry also holds fr. 15573 ff. 379-381 (Burford, issue #44), same key; he took six values from a further deciphered Cipher-3 letter, fr. 15570 ff. 271-273 (1585): long zigzag = ss, circled 9 = par, d = vostre, barred double o = le roy de Navarre (doubtful), 13 = faict (doubtful), 6 = s (doubtful).

texts.label: fr. 15572 f. 276, 1586 (alejandrozarco, PR #25)
texts.summary: A Poitou intelligence note on the Catholic factions round La Roussière, Henri III's governor of Fontenay(-le-Comte): La Guiolle unsure of Le Puy, La Saussaie, the priory promised to Aubois, the sieurs de la Fontaine, la Chaie and Mirebeau; 'Le Pui est ennuyé de la guerre'. Writer and recipient are not named. The transcriptions are the two independent sign-by-sign reads (one letter per sign).

texts.label: fr. 15571 f. 179, 1586 (alejandrozarco, PR #25)
texts.summary: Frontin is to come to terms with La Rousière's children; the writer is resolved to attack Pons, 'il se poura prendre en ung mois'; sickness among the foot; 'employer Lansac en ... l'armée de mer'. The siege and the sickness fit, without being established, the plague in Mayenne's and Matignon's army round Castillon (Aug-Sept 1586); Tomokiyo's interlinear decipherment was the check.

texts.label: fr. 15573 ff. 379r-381v, autumn 1586 (Brett Burford, issue #44)
texts.summary: A six-page despatch wholly in cipher, addressed to the King and probably from Matignon: a military report on the Guyenne campaign, the river trade on the Garonne between Toulouse and Bordeaux from which the Huguenots draw dues, Caumont and the Mas de Verdun, Castillon, the Isle and the Dordogne, the King of Navarre, 'your sister' at Agen, the artillery from Navarrenx, Marmande and fifteen to sixteen thousand crowns. system.summary: Each plaintext letter is a group of two to four signs (letters, figures and invented signs), with figure groups for letters and syllables (14 = p, 20 = la, 18 = le/de, 30 = m), signs for common words (qui, par, faire, sieur, Monsieur) and nulls between groups.
system.doubled_letters: own groups for ff, ll, ss, mm, pp/rr
system.sibling_key: none known; Tomokiyo (cryptiana, henryiii page, 'Matignon's Tuple Cipher') knows only this letter in it
system.notes: Polyphony here is partly a transcription matter: several labels (E2 c/e, M30 m/n/mm/nn, QUI qui/que, N18 le/de, DA de/d) carry two or more values and the decoder chose per place. A different cipher from Matignon's Cipher-3 (matignon1586c3) and from the Mayenne-Forget Cipher-1 (matignon1586).

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear decipherment over most groups on the leaves themselves; Tomokiyo describes the cipher and the letter but gives neither key nor reading; no edition found.

texts.label: R1156, Pozsony, 1 June 1482
texts.summary: King Matthias Corvinus to Duke Ercole I of Ferrara, his brother-in-law, five weeks after Venice opened the War of Ferrara: he and Queen Beatrix had resolved to send 500 horse, among them 100 hussars, but found no safe road; his captain Balázs Magyar goes to Croatia towards the Venetian border to gather troops. Printed by Fraknói (1895, no. 131); re-read here from the glyphs, correcting four passages of the print.

system.summary: Mayenne-Forget's Cipher-2 (Tomokiyo's reconstruction): homophonic substitution of invented signs and figures for French letters, with signs for syllables and common words (de, la, que, qui, est, et, pour, plus, monsieur, 23 apres, 24 peu, 31 pas, 17 tant) and a slash as word divider.
system.sibling_key: Tomokiyo's reconstruction of Mayenne-Forget's Cipher-2 (cryptiana henryiii_MayenneForget2.png), with values Burford aligned on letters in the same cipher deciphered at the time: fr. 15573 ff. 103v-104r (Mayenne to the King, Libourne, Sept 1586), 7v-8r, 32r-33r, 97r, 149r-150r.
system.notes: One key across the three documents: ff. 218-219 were read with Tomokiyo's table (Harumi-Matsuba checked ten values against Burford's key after the fact), f. 120 with Burford's key, f. 385 is Burford's own. Not Cipher-1 (matignon1586) or Cipher-3 (matignon1586c3): different sign inventory (barred # signs, ∴, // dividers). Code numbers do not carry across the three ciphers. Two sign readings conflict between the contributors: barred h is armée in Harumi's key, while Burford splits it into hb = tout and Qh = armée; the χ° sign is q in the table but pour in the calibration letter.

title: Pseudo-Elias of Cortona, Lumen luminum, cipher recipes and zodiac table, North Italy c. 1525 (Beinecke Mellon MS 29; DECODE R2877)

documents.shelfmark: Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Mellon MS 29, ff. 1v-2v and front pastedown; DECODE R2877

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the manuscript (the later pastedown copy is unglossed), in the Beinecke catalogue, in Rec 2014 or in Galiano's articles.

transcription.source: Yale Digital Collections IIIF, canvases 17388795-17388799 (full resolution crops)
transcription.notes: Sol recipe list (f. 1v), Luna recipe list (f. 2r) and 12-entry zodiac table (f. 2v); q/g distinction uncertain (Rec 2014 reads g where this transcription has q in two entries). Scribal signs kept as 3 (ʒ), 7 (et-sign), 9 (con-sign), B (ß). The pastedown copy is recorded but not counted. 'in' and 'cioe' are clear words inside the f. 2r list and are included in the count.

system.summary: Letter strings with a few scribal signs, standing for the substances behind twelve zodiac cover names and for two recipe lists; not simple substitution, possibly polyalphabetic, a whole-name code, or invented pseudo-text.
system.sibling_key: none known

prior_solution.where: DECODE R2877 Non-decrypted; Rec 2014 (Societas Magica Newsletter 31, n. 8) calls it a code and does not solve it

conditions.human_role: Selected the target from the catalogue and set the goal; no other input.

solution.what: Downloaded all 69 Yale IIIF images of Mellon MS 29 and full-resolution crops of the cipher lines; checked DECODE R2877 (same images, no transcription, no key).
Beinecke catalogue description, Rec 2014 (Societas Magica Newsletter 31), Galiano's articles on Elias' alchemical codices, general web search for the Italian prologue.
Located the cipher (ff. 1v, 2r, 2v and the pastedown copy; ff. 3r-37v checked, clear) and transcribed the 234-letter corpus with its scribal signs.

IC 0.075 in both sections (language-like), but the zodiac table and the recipe lists have different letter profiles (q 17% vs <2%, h 3% vs 10%); Sukhotin puts q as the main vowel in one and r in the other.
One-to-one monoalphabetic annealing against Italian and Latin, with and without word division, q/g split and merged, sections together and apart: best -4.0 per char (gibberish).
A synthetic 206-letter Italian ingredient list under a random key is recovered by the same solver at -2.6 per char, so a simple substitution of Italian would have been found.
Homophonic (many-to-one) annealing; Caesar and Trithemius progressive shifts per entry over five alphabets; Vigenere periods 2-7 restarting or running; reversed words; alternate-letter nulls.

Alberti cipher disk (lowercase ring with k, y, h, &; capitals R and V inside the runs as index letters): Alberti's published ring per segment, then an unknown ring with 19 per-segment offsets annealed jointly.
Word-pattern solver over ~170 Italian substance, number and weight words: no consistent key; Virgo 'pqyqpqsqst' and the 'qrqr'/'lrqrlr' shapes fit no substance name.

Rylands Latin MS 65 (Lang's survey of alchemical cipher MSS; contains the Latin Lumen luminum and Elias's Vademecum) scanned in full: no Italian prologue or clear recipes; its f. 1v 'Tabula alphabetorum Raymundi' is a letter-per-substance Lullian alphabet, which does not make the Mellon strings read.

outcome.method_basis: The 234-letter cipher of Beinecke Mellon MS 29 (ff. 1v-2v) was transcribed and tested under simple systems with Italian and Latin models; nothing reads, and no key, clear copy or printed decipherment exists.

title: Mémoire en chiffre du XIIe décembre 1560: anonymous report from the Agenais to Montmorency, BnF fr. 3157 no. 67

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3157 no. 67, ff. 152r-156v (Gallica btv1b90598645 views 153-158)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaves, the dorse or the neighbouring items; only the heading 'Du xiie decembre 1560' is in clear.

transcription.source: Gallica IIIF full resolution, half-width 3-line crops
transcription.notes: Tokens are cipher words (the manuscript divides words with '/'); 9,497 signs in all. First pass by three agents, then a key-guided correction pass by four agents against the images (corrections_<fol>.tsv, about 300 x->r fixes).

system.summary: Homophonic substitution in a cursive pseudo-script with word division, two-stroke units (zo=u, pp=m, s3=r, lz=d) and four whole-word codes (pour, roy, et, sieur).
system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: Main trap: the rounder r-form (n) versus x (e). Polyphonic delta (u/v, b, g) and double dagger (i, a). No name codes; all persons and places spelt out.

prior_solution.where: G. Lasry solved it independently in 2023 (improved Feb 2026), unpublished (private communication, 25 Sept 2026). No DECODE record, not on Tomokiyo or Lasry (GL.htm) lists, no edition found by web search. Brunet 2019 on Clairac not reachable.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: posed the catalogue entry with /goal. No target-specific intervention.
tools: decrypt.py (key.txt with units and word codes)

solution.what: Located item 67 in fr. 3157: the BnF notice's folio numbers precede the item numbers, so the cipher is ff. 152r-156v (not f. 158). Fetched the ten pages from Gallica IIIF.
Checked the dorse and the neighbouring Villars letters for a decipherment or key: none.
Looked at Lasry's GL.htm tables for Henri II / Charles IX as the brief asked: different symbol sets.
Three agents transcribed the ten pages into ASCII sign codes (one stopped after three pages by a tool block; a fresh agent did 153v-154r).
One-sign-per-letter homophonic annealing with word spaces: gibberish (-4.2/char).
z followed by o in 262 of 283 cases: 'zo' taken as one unit; most frequent words Tzox, Wx, Wxm, hx.
Seeded Tzox=que, Wx/Wxm=le/les, hx=de; annealer read 'les derniers advertissemens', 'les affaires de pardeça'.
Aligned decrypted words with the French they must be: entendu (r=n, io=u), avoir, ordinairement (s3=r), souloit (nn=s); reran the annealer with these units (-3.2/char).
Standalone groups read from context as codes: Z=pour, 4=roy, c+/i+/e+=et, F/g=sieur.
Key-guided correction pass by four agents against the images, changing a sign only where the image supports it: about 300 x->r fixes, the looped sign y (=i) identified, missing signs restored.
Line-by-line reading with marked emendations; lz=d found during it (despuis, disans, d'environ); 16 of 1,715 cipher words left unread.
Web search for an edition or decipherment (names, places, shelfmark): none; Brunet 2019 on Clairac not reachable.

Merged with a parallel project pass on the same item (main 13e0f27b2): its margin (153r.14, 'assemblez en la chambre du conseil') and dorse ('Advertissemens') readings decoded with key.txt and confirmed; added to the reading.
Lasry review (email 25 Sept 2026): Lasry wrote that he had independently solved it in 2023 (improved Feb 2026) but never published it; kept in the ciphertext-only list with that note.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 7830 tokens, 50 types, fr-1530-despatches order 4: reading -2.264 per letter; random keys -5.162 (z 4.1); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.007 (mean -3.029, z 43.3); annealer on the real text -2.657. Verdict: weak.

system.summary: A numerical cipher of 77 distinct figures (12-157), written with the writer's word division, among clear Polish and Latin words; its design is not established.
system.notes: Dots join the figures of a word, gaps separate words, '=' joins a word across a line end (r7524-words.txt). One-figure words 12, 38, 56, 133; repeated words (22.118.82.36.31.81 x4) suggest a letter cipher with homophones, untested. Not Potocka's alphabet.

solution.what: Acquired cached DECODE metadata and full-resolution images for R7524 together with the nine Potocka letters (R7525-R7536) addressed to the same recipient.

Visual inspection: R7524 catalogue language is Polish and its figures run to 157, unlike the short French passages of the Potocka letters; a single solver across all the letters to Dunin is not justified.
R7524 transcribed from the images: 232 cipher figures with clear Polish and Latin anchors (r7524-cipher.txt).

Mniszech R7524 tested with Polish quintgram homophonic annealing, a tentative hetmanow crib, a tentative null 33/ch=130 and a unigram-regularized search (solve_mniszech*.py). No coherent decipherment; these are hypotheses, not recovered values.
Searches for Mniszech/Dunin cipher, the shelfmark and cipher terms found biographical and archive catalogue context but no decipherment.
Inspected the three cipher-key records in the local DECODE Sanguszko catalogue: R7515 numeric alphabet (a=5/10/15, two series) and R7460/R7461 (graphic signs). None fits R7524.
A 232-token synthetic Polish homophonic control with 75 observed symbols recovered only 49 positions (21.1%). Mniszech search failures are inconclusive, not evidence of impossibility.

R7524 re-read at full resolution from IMG_R7524_I33989_P1/P3: all 232 figures confirmed; the writer's word division (dots within words, gaps between, '=' at line breaks) recorded for the first time in r7524-words.txt (53 cipher words, single-figure words 12, 38, 56, 133; doubled 19.19 and 28.28). The clear word filed as 'Starosty horodly' is 'spraktykowawszy'.

R7524 word-boundary homophonic annealing (solve_r7524_words.py) with pl-modern and with a period model built from Pasek's memoirs (Wikisource) + Gutenberg Polish; also with cribs hetmanow and 15.20=ie.
R7524 dictionary-word annealing (solve_r7524_dict.py; 49k-word Pasek+Gutenberg list, char-model fallback): 34-36 of 53 words land in the dictionary but restarts disagree completely; no stable key.
Tested whether R7524's numbering is Barbara Potocka's table (base 14-39, homophone = 2x base; targets/potocka1714/key-potocka.json) shifted (-40..40) or scaled (x1-x4): nothing fits.

Entry split from potocka1714 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026). Compared r7524-words.txt with the flat files: they differ at figures 46 and 201 (36 vs 30); the P1 image shows 36 at figure 46. No new attack.

outcome.method_basis: Homophonic annealing (flat, word-boundary, dictionary-word, with cribs) on modern and period Polish models gave no stable key, and a matched 232-token synthetic control was recovered only to 21.1%, so the failure is inconclusive.
outcome.fraction_read_source: targets/mniszech1714/r7524-words.txt: 232 cipher figures, none with a value.

texts.label: R18, Francia 22/1, 10 Aug [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: On publishing the Council of Trent: strong resistance everywhere over Gallican liberties. In Paris Morosini lobbied the Sorbonne and the royal council, and told Henri III that a Most Christian king should accept the council without conditions. The King answered that the clergy, above all the Archbishop of Lyon, were the ones opposing it.

texts.label: R28, Francia 22/7, [early] Oct [1588] (duplicate)
texts.summary: While walking in the palace garden with the King, the Queen Mother and the Cardinals of Bourbon and Vendôme, Morosini learned that the King would send Signor Girolamo Gondi to Rome about pulling Marshal Montmorency away from the Huguenots. Vendôme reports that Cardinal Joyeuse worked against the Count of Soissons in Rome.

texts.label: R43, Francia 22/22, Blois, 23 Dec [1588]
texts.summary: Guise is killed with daggers in the King's chamber on the King's order, after warnings that he meant harm to the King. The Cardinal of Guise, the Prince de Joinville, the Dukes of Nemours and Elbeuf, the Archbishop of Lyon, the prévôt des marchands and a Paris president are arrested, and the Cardinal de Bourbon is put under guard. The Queen Mother is left speechless, the city is locked down, Morosini seeks an audience in vain, and the Cardinal of Guise is feared dead too.

texts.label: R53, Francia 22/32, image 499v, [Moulins, early May 1589; decipherment f. 500r]
texts.summary: Navarre, by what the vice-legate of Avignon's secretary said, arrived at Tours on Thursday and lodged at Plessis with a large company; he went to see the King, gave him the shirt at his rising and the napkin at table, and dined with him: a mixing of heretics and Catholics at court, hateful to honest men. Contributor, 容密: 90 first-sheet groups too few; on about 590 groups, four per-place digit substitutions annealed into readable text.

Contributor, 容密: 借甸 (3949) for 借款 (2949) exactly when the hundreds gave no carry revealed an additive; exact key (tables + 0901 with carries) computed on N02, N08, N11, N12; rule 90 = 00 added from the groups beginning 90.
Contributor, 辰密: 共密 and 容密 keys failed; permuted-page + permuted tens/units model annealed on N13, N16, N26 (201 groups); exact assignment stuck in false optima.
Contributor, 辰密: the page table found follows the countdown of numbers without a zero, then imposed; 劈 for 力 and 滠 for 灰, both from groups ending 9, gave the rule units 9 = 10.

Contributor: 容密 key from four telegrams reads the other ten unrefitted; 辰密 N05 (not in the search, no prefix) reads through; N16 ends 灰 matching its date; V4B, V4D, V4E never used to find the keys read unchanged; names fit June 1916 office-holders.

Project: his verify.py rerun with python -I: 32/32 published raw texts reproduced; scores 共密 3.492, 容密 3.179, 辰密 3.773 against maxima of 200 random keys (-1.450, -1.665, -1.588) and 200 digit shuffles (-1.224, -1.455, -1.177).

Project: his search_gongmi.py recovers K = 9000 and φ exactly from scratch (3.492; shuffled nulls -1.10, -1.07, -1.09); search_rongmi.py gives K = 0900 with hundreds and tens exact, units equivalent up to the carry, thousands off on 7/8/9 (2.608 vs 3.179 for the published key; nulls -1.10, -1.19).

Project: own decoder written from the stated keys (decode.py, Unihan kTaiwanTelegraph table from targets/sunyatsen/tw.csv) applied to his re-read digits: 2472/2472 groups and 32/32 telegrams identical to his raw texts (共密 555/555, 容密 1306/1306, 辰密 239/239).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): cipher groups ct_gongmi/rongmi/chenmi.txt; decode.py run over groups.tsv and saved per code as texts/<code>_decryption.md; Dudout's keys copied from NOTES to texts/key.md; his annotated texts and translations linked on his Wenmi pages

Brice Dudout's Wenmi pages en/gongmi.html and en/rongmi.html fetched 23 Oct 2026: per telegram a raw decoding, a proposed reading ({x} = probable reading, 〔x〕 = kept unresolved) and an English translation, with a digit table group by group. b21_wenmi.py: each proposed reading cut into units and aligned with our decoder's output on the page digits; every plain character equals the figure's own value (0 mismatches in gongmi; rongmi 1, the 偽/僞 table variant of one code); each {x} tested for a one-digit variant of its group: gongmi 21 of 24 are one-digit alternates, rongmi 40 of 55 (the rest supplied from context and bracketed). texts/gongmi_align.tsv, rongmi_align.tsv.

One-digit variants listed for every group kept unresolved (〔x〕). Adopted: N24 group 22, 2530 滠 -> 2520 灰 (tens 三 for 二), '灰日唐宅開會' = 'on the 10th a meeting at Tang's house', after '佳日' (9th) in the same sentence; sense-only, flagged for review. solution.what: Fetched DECODE records R85-R90, their transcriptions and key files, and two page images, with the repository cookie.
Found Lasry's reconstructed key on every record, byte-identical to the key on R93-R102 (alessandrino1568); no plaintext attached.
Identified sender, recipient and year from the archive description on the records (ff. 146-338 = Alessandrino to the nuncio, 1567) and the clear openings on ff. 163r, 299r.
Tried archive.org and HathiTrust for Serrano 1914; not on archive.org, HathiTrust 403.
Ran the alessandrino1568 decoder unchanged on the six transcriptions.

All six read as continuous Italian: Philip II's journey to Flanders and a papal interview, Borromeo's Milan jurisdiction, the archbishop of Cologne, the second French civil war; R88/R89 are two copies of one letter and R90 repeats its close.

Historical consistency: Morvilliers, l'Aubespine, Montmorency, Conde and Coligny in arms date R88-R90 to Oct-Nov 1567; Cologne (von Wied, unconfirmed) and the Milan dispute fit 1567; the two copies R88/R89 agree.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): DECODE transcriptions (RebAn 2016) per record; decryptions = the word-split DECODE bodies from decode_updates/decryptions copied into texts/, plus decrypt_raw.txt, all with Lasry's key as filed (decode/DOC_R85_D3265_3265.txt etc.).

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/R85-R90_decryption.txt and decrypt_raw.txt read: Italian fragments between garbled strings in nearly every line in all six letters (R85, R87, R89 closely), e.g. 'pur tu giudica che saria bene che re inuita sectabolo oposi satisfatione del mondosi'; docs/_check_reading.py 21-40% of sentences clean in the word-split files. Re-read under REREAD_BRIEF (batch b09): the 10 DECODE cipher images of R85-R90 and their 29 cleartext images (folios around each cipher) fetched with the DECODE session cookie (research/reading_audit/b09_fetch.py), kept out of the repository.

Contemporary texts looked for among the cleartext images: R87's decipherment is f. 251r (top lines lost, stops at "resistere"); R90's second sentence is in clear on f. 302r (end of the 4 Nov 1567 letter with R88); R88, R89, R90 are three cipher copies of one text. No decipherment for R85, R86, R88, R89 (clear covering letters only). Serrano 1914 not reached (HathiTrust 403).

Decipherment f. 251r and clear passage f. 302r transcribed from the images (texts/R87_decifrato_f251r.txt, R90_clear_f302r.txt). Cipher transcriptions checked on the images at every break: twelve labels corrected (texts/R85-R90_corrections.tsv; corrected files for R85, R86, R87), e.g. R86 row 1 2020 -> 1010 (N.S.) and 4 0 2 0 9 -> 4 0 1 0 9 0 (a V.S.), R85 row 2 four spurious figures removed.

Decipherment of R87 aligned with the figures (reread_b09_align.py, edit-distance DP over the two-letter figure sets) and R88/R89/R90 aligned with each other and with f. 302r. Code values fixed: 8010 = [la] Regina [di Francia] (Lasry "Re di Francia"), 4010 = S.M. (Lasry "Sua Santità"), 1020 essere, 1040 lettera, 8030 religione, 8070 ugonotta, 8080 heretici, 8090 havere, 3040 Fiandra; 3 0^. 9 = qua; "colospo" = colloquio (colo + 509 qui + o); 209 = "chi" as a syllable (richiesti). The decipherer misread in four places, where the figures are followed.

All six read word by word on the figures from a first draft by the extended beam decoder (reread_b09_decode.py --rows), every word aligned with its figures (research/reading_audit/b09_align.py: R85 169/190, R86 155/164, R87 437/448, R88 326/361, R89 336/349, R90 45/48 words carried); words not carried bracketed. Failed or open: R85 codes 3050 and 3020 (this use), a blotted group and a ticked run; R86 code 2020; R88 group 7 3 8. State decoded, not read -> read for all six; class not read -> read, method not solved -> read with known key.

texts.label: R86, Spagna 1 item 2, f. 236r [1567]

system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and a few syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 4, and the single digit 3 as a null.
system.sibling_key: None needed: the same key serves Spagna 364C (items 1-32) and 364D (items 1-24), 1717-1720.
system.notes: Nomenclator runs: 4001-4078 particles and endings; 4079-4296 nouns and names A-R; 4401-4479 S-V; 4485-4531 calendar and day numbers; 4532-4543 and 4552-4563 two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre month runs; 4535-4619 a second alphabetical run A-T; scattered blocks at 4681, 4706, 4870+. Lasry's filed key gives 268 of the 399 four-digit groups used in the corpus; 61 more were recovered in this session, leaving 135 distinct groups (3.4% of nomenclator tokens) without a value. The digit 3 is a null, except when it falls among the three digits following a 4 prefix, where it belongs to the nomenclator group.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's reconstructed key and segmented decipherment of the whole S364 corpus, both filed as attachments on every one of DECODE R154-R177; key dated 24 October 2020

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE session cookie used to download the record attachments.

solution.what: Fetched the 24 DECODE record pages R154-R177 with the project cookie and downloaded all 72 attached documents.

Checked the attachments before attacking anything: each record carries the per-item transcription, a reconstructed key signed George Lasry, 24 October 2020, and a 783 KB file holding his segmented decipherment of Spagna 364C/1-32 and 364D/1-24.

Confirmed all 24 of the 364D items are present in that decipherment and measured its coverage: 34,243 cipher tokens, 33,408 valued, 97.6% read. The catalogue's 'noted, a transcription job' rating and DECODE's 'partially decrypted' status both understated it.
Compared the filed key against the corpus: 268 four-digit entries against 399 four-digit groups in use, leaving 189 groups without a value in 715 tokens, 11.0% of all nomenclator usage.

The key is alphabetical in runs, so every unvalued group has a bracket from its nearest valued neighbours; combined with contexts from the 84,961-token corpus this should fix most of them without cryptanalysis.

Recovered 61 groups, each on at least two independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket too (promozione, aggiustamento, giurisdizione, vascelli, Vicere, tribunale, corriere, cifra, negoziato and the rest). Resolved the calendar block as two parallel Gennaio-Dicembre runs at 4532-4543 and 4552-4563.

4538=Luglio, derived from the month run's offset, is independently confirmed by 'delli 12 Luglio passato, qual appunto fu il giorno della promozione del Sig. Card.' - Alberoni was created cardinal on 12 July 1717.

Re-measured with the recovered groups applied: unknown nomenclator usage falls from 11.0% to 3.4% of nomenclator tokens corpus-wide (715 to 221), and over 364D alone from 8.0% to 3.4%; whole-text reading of 364D rises from 97.56% to 97.89%.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per item, the DECODE transcription (decode/keep/DOC_R*.txt, EHum / KaJo 2016-17) and George Lasry's segmented decipherment of 2020 cut from the corpus dump (lasry/364D-*.txt; whole corpus decode/keep/lasry_decipherment_S364.txt); key: Lasry's filed key plus the groups recovered here (key_extra.txt, key_table.md). No decryption re-applying the extended key exists as a file

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): the five flagged despatches read on Lasry's decode rows, joined into running text. R154 (D) and R173 (C) have holes in most or half their sentences: relabelled decoded, not read. R166, R168 and R170 build Italian sentences with scattered open groups: overturned to B. Class already solved kept; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889 (groups in documents that read).

Re-read brief b22: every file on DECODE R154 and R173 fetched with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/b17_fetch.py): transcriptions, Lasry's key and corpus file (already held) and the 7 + 2 page images (only R154 p. 1 had been saved). The images carry a complete contemporary interlinear decipherment over every cipher line of both despatches; DECODE's PLAINTEXT rows had copied it with most words as '?', which is why NOTES called it thin.

Interlinear decipherments transcribed line by line from 1800-px strips (b22_crop.py): lasry/R154_decifrato.txt (135 lines, ff. 12r-15r), lasry/R173_decifrato.txt (34 lines, ff. 344r-v). Figure corrections against DECODE's transcription in lasry/R154-R173_corrections.tsv (4594 -> 4597 Prima; 4570 -> 4576 twice; 4470 -> 4479; one f. 13r cipher line missing from DECODE, figures read from the image; a false code 4839).

Key changes from the decipherments, each checked at every place in the S364 corpus (ctx.py over seq.json), key_b22.tsv: adopted 78 = dal (Lasry del; 5/5 in R154, corpus contexts 'fin dall'anno', 'rilasciato dal Re', 'di levare dal concordato'), 4029 = però (Lasry quale; 37 places), 4009 = essendo (Lasry ere|esse; 16), 4160 = esercit (Lasry Capitol; 3), 4545 = cotest (2), 4434 = Em.za (13); 4545 and 4434 added to key_extra.txt. For review: 4201 = Stà Sua (sense, 3 places). Not adopted: 00 (46 places, contexts too garbled), 4168 (2 places, no common value); 4516 kept as 16 (the decipherer's d.o read as a slip for 4576).

Group-by-group alignment of Lasry's decode rows with the decipherments (research/reading_audit/b22_nunzio_align.py; lasry/R154_align.tsv, R173_align.tsv, R154_words.tsv, R173_words.tsv): R154 3,428 of 4,030 letters carried by the figures' own values or codes, 93 on a look-alike figure, 255 on groups DECODE marks unread, 163 where the group gives other letters (mostly code 4261 rendered 'il Papa'/'Sua Santità'); R173 1,005 of 1,172, 19 look-alike, 79 unread, 46 other.

Readings lasry/R154_reading.md and R173_reading.md built on the decipherments, decipherer's spelling kept, abbreviations expanded; translations R154_en.md, R173_en.md. b17_score.py on the reading bodies: R154 0.986 (68/69), R173 0.917 (22/24); explicit holes only 1.0 and 1.0 (before: Lasry's rows joined 0.381 and 0.358). Both read; with them all 24 despatches of 364D read.

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): the 22 despatches other than R154/R173 had no reading file; the sweep had scored the DECODE figure tables (plain 0.0-0.33). Readings lasry/R155-R177_reading.md written: Lasry's decode rows with key_extra.txt and the b22 changes, word-divided by hand beside DECODE's PLAINTEXT rows (copies of the contemporary interlinear decipherment); helpers research/reading_audit/v5b_nunzio_rows.py, v5b_nunzio_side.py. Found: R163 = second copy of R162+R161, R168 = duplicate of R166, R176 = second copy of R173 (+ f. 360r), R174/R175 = closes of passages whole in R177/R176; Lasry's 'stessi' group stands for 'volte' (4 places), 'tanto' for 'Armata' (2), 4113 'Card.le' for 'conte-', 4482 for 'caduto'; not adopted. All 22 score plain 0.68-1.0 except R175 (16 words, 0.5); R170 keeps [...] gaps where ~19 figure lines are missing from DECODE's transcription.

Verification 5: R170 (364D/17) and R172 (364D/19) had [...] gaps where DECODE's figure transcription misses lines (about 22 of 112 and 5 of 50) and its PLAINTEXT rows are garbled. The DECODE images were fetched with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/b17_fetch.py) and the contemporary interlinear decipherment read on 1700-px strips (b22_crop.py) and transcribed (lasry/R170_decifrato.txt, R172_decifrato.txt). Readings rewritten from it: R170 0.69 -> 0.964 plain, R172 0.684 -> 1.0. R163 (364D/10) and R177 (364D/24) were checked on their images too: no interlinear on either leaf, so their readings stay on the figures (R163: two open codes and one garbled run; R177: one unread run before 'mani').
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 24 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's reconstructed S364 key (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of the whole corpus were attached to every DECODE record R154-R177 before the attempt; the project measured that reading and recovered 61 more nomenclator groups from alphabetical brackets and context.
outcome.notes: Solved by George Lasry in October 2020 and already read on the DECODE records when this session began; nothing about the system was open. What is new here is the measurement of that reading and 61 additional nomenclator values that extend his key. Verification detail: coverage measured token by token off Lasry's aligned decipherment; each recovered group rests on two or more independent contexts and usually the alphabetical bracket; 4538=Luglio matches the known date of Alberoni's promotion, 12 July 1717. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R154 and R173 decoded, not read; R166, R168, R170 overturned to B; fraction_read 0.9789 -> 0.889. Class already solved kept (Lasry's decryption, 2020). 23 Oct 2026, re-read (b22): R154 and R173 read from the complete contemporary interlinear decipherments on the DECODE images, aligned with the figures; six key values corrected or added (key_b22.tsv); all 24 despatches read.

credits.note: solved and read the S364 corpus in 2020: reconstructed key and segmented decipherment on DECODE R154-R177; measured and extended by 61 nomenclator groups here

texts.label: R154, Spagna 364D/1, Roma 11 Genn. 1718
texts.summary: Clement XI's Secretariat of State to the nuncio in Madrid at the opening of the War of the Quadruple Alliance. The recurring business is the promotion of Cardinal Alberoni and the settlement of the pending disputes between Rome and Spain: the nuncio's jurisdiction, the abolition of the Nunziatura in Naples, the expulsion of the nuncio, the Spanish ships bound for the Levant, the Emperor, the Turk and the peace treaty.

reading_review.note: Read 23 Oct 2026 (b22): the complete contemporary interlinear decipherment over ff. 12r-15r, visible on the seven DECODE images (only page 1 had been saved; NOTES had judged the gloss 'thin and unreliable' from DECODE's PLAINTEXT rows, most words '?'), transcribed (lasry/R154_decifrato.txt) and aligned group by group with Lasry's decode rows plus six key changes adopted at every corpus place (key_b22.tsv: 78 dal, 4029 però, 4009 essendo, 4160 esercit, 4545 cotest, 4434 Em.za). 3,428 of 4,030 letters carried by the figures' own values or codes; 93 letters (2.3%) rest on a look-alike figure (4570 -> 4576 dett-, 4470 -> 4479 ...); one cipher line of f. 13r missing from DECODE's transcription read from the image. No word supplied. b17_score on the reading body 0.986 (68/69), explicit holes 1.0; Lasry's rows joined 0.381.

system.summary: Undivided digit stream: two-digit homophones for letters and syllables, four-digit nomenclator groups prefixed 1, and the digit 7 as a null.
system.sibling_key: unknown
system.notes: Lasry's filed key (ASV - S423) values only the two-digit elements; none of the 166 four-digit groups in the corpus (708 tokens). The nomenclator is not alphabetical as far as the recovered values show.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's reconstructed key ASV - S423 and segmented decipherment of Spagna 423/1-11, attached to every one of DECODE R179-R188; key dated 24 October 2020

conditions.human_role: Supplied the DECODE session cookie; set the target by /goal.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R179-R188 record pages and all attachments (per-item transcriptions, key, corpus decipherment, page images).
Checked attachments first, following the Spagna 364D precedent: Lasry's key ASV - S423 (24 Oct 2020) and his segmented decipherment of all 11 items are on every record.
Parsed the aligned decipherment (9,001 tokens incl. nulls): the key values no four-digit group; 166 distinct groups, 708 tokens, unread. Text read 90.6%.
Tried the 364D alphabetical-bracket method; the 1736 nomenclator is not alphabetical (1222 -mente, 1245 -zione, 1882 Spagna, 1935 V.S.), so values must come from context alone.
Assigned 46 groups from context, accepting a value only where every occurrence reads (N.S., V.S., S. Sede, Corte, Spagna, Napoli, Brevi, Sig. Card., -mente, -zione, tutt-, molt-, altr- ...).
Re-measured: 424 of 708 nomenclator tokens valued; whole text 90.6% -> 95.3% read. Content consistent with the 1736 Spanish recruiting riots in Rome (Acquaviva, Montemar, Molina).

Catalogue entry 250 (DECODE R26, 7 Jan 1736) identified as item 423/1 of this volume, filed apart from R179-R188; already covered by Lasry's decipherment and reading.txt. Entry closed, no new reading.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per item, the digit stream (lasry/423-*.txt) and, for items 2-11, the DECODE transcription (decode/keep/DOC_R*.txt); the decryption is reading.txt (Lasry's decipherment with the nomenclator values recovered here), split per item into texts/reading_423-*.txt, plus Lasry's 2020 decipherment of the whole corpus; key: Lasry's filed key and key_extra.txt

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): the eleven running texts read through. Open nomenclator groups (about one per eight to ten words) and ??? runs stand in almost every sentence of ten letters, relabelled decoded, not read; the short 423/3 builds its sentence (reviewed B). Class already solved -> read in part; fraction_read 0.953 (tokens valued) -> 0.016.

Re-read (REREAD_BRIEF, batch b04): the 26 DECODE page images of R26 and R179-R188 fetched with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/b04_fetch.py; scratchpad only, not in the repository) and R26's transcription DOC_R26_D1635 (NiLan 2017) saved to decode/keep/. The pages carry no interlinear or margin decipherment; the clear text in the margins of some images is the facing leaf of other letters. A web search found no edition of the 1736 ciphers to Guiccioli; the minutes would be in the Madrid nunciature archive (not digitised).

The DECODE transcriptions re-segmented with Lasry's rules (7 null outside groups, 1xxx nomenclator, else pairs; b04_seg.py) instead of Lasry's segmented file, which leaves out whole runs (423/5: 137 of 177 non-null tokens; about 20% in all). Fifteen unclear or struck figures resolved on the images and by sense (texts/423_b04_corrections.tsv); per-letter decodes in texts/423-<n>_decode_b04.txt.

Key corrected and extended from the documents (texts/b04_key_additions.txt): two-digit 25 = che (Lasry ";"), 30 = ta (not to), 69 = z (not t), 93 = nel (not quel); nomenclator 1234 = qual (was Ministr/Nunzi), 1205 = com (was che), 1241 = tant (was molt), 1210 = esser (was restar), each tested on every occurrence; 34 new firm values (medesim, cont, aver, fatt, Mons., ben, letter, part, issim, interess, relazion, pubblic, spagnuol, dett, parlar, Regn, volt, tre, due, ordinari, riguard, tropp, ragion, present, qualch, manier, liber, aggrav, ordin, avvis, procur, scriv, molt, Nunzi) and about 30 probable ones printed [?x].

Readings built sentence by sentence for 423/2, 423/4-11 (texts/423-<n>_reading.md, English _en.md) and aligned word by word with the decode (b04_align.py): every unbracketed word is carried by figures or a nomenclator value; supplied words bracketed. _check_reading.py on the bodies (abbreviations de-dotted): clean-sentence share 0.47-0.71 (the strict count treats every [?x] probable value as a hole).

423/1 (R26, 14 July 1736) read through on NiLan's weaker transcription (texts/423-1_reading.md, _en.md): the sentences of the riots, the Ostia and Trastevere enlistments, Acquaviva and Montemar build, but about a dozen runs do not decode (clean share 0.31); not re-transcribed from the images in this session.

Opened every attachment of DECODE R26 and R179-R188 at full resolution with the project cookie (research/reading_audit/r2d_fetch_docs.py): the png documents labelled 'cleartext' are not the cipher pages but neighbouring folios, and among them are contemporary clear copies ('Copia') of the ciphered letters 423/1 (ff. 284r-286r), 423/4 (f. 301r), 423/5 (f. 375r), 423/6 (f. 386r), 423/9 (ff. 416r-v), 423/10 (ff. 493r-494r) and 423/11 (ff. 509r-v). The 22 Oct re-read had opened only the IMG page images.

Transcribed the copies of 423/1, 5, 9, 11 (texts/423-<n>_copy.txt) and aligned each token by token with the re-segmented decode (research/reading_audit/r2d_align.py, texts/423-<n>_r2d_align.tsv); six figures of NiLan's R26 transcription corrected on the cipher images where the copy disagreed (texts/423_b04_corrections.tsv, item 1); 423/9 'io te danno', 423/11 'le la mede' and 'ben ..giata' found to be cipherer's slips on the images.

Key corrected and extended from the copies, each value checked at every occurrence (texts/b04_key_additions.txt, r2d block; research/reading_audit/r2d_kwic.py): 26 = del (not a) and 80 = dal (not nel); twelve earlier nomenclator values replaced (1219 ora, 1239 quell, 1608 necessari, 1229 perche, 1231 pero, 1818 ragguagli, 1699 pregiudizi, 1865 sodisfazion, 1218 avut, 1223 mentre, 1260 Ambasciator, 1368 congiuntur); about 55 groups valued (1513 Governator, 1544 Inquisitor, 1449 ecclesiastic, 1389 costi, day groups 1952 = 7, 1953 = 8, 1957 = 12, 1964 = 19 ...). Open groups: about 60 distinct on 22 Oct -> 12 now (12 distinct: three in 423/1, carried by the copy; four in 423/2, four in 423/7, one in 423/8).

texts.label: Philip II to the nuncio Ormanetto, 1573, ASV Spagna 7 ff. 303r-304r (DECODE R116)
texts.summary: A copy of Philip II's letter to the nuncio with two cipher passages. system.doubled_letters: separate codes (bb cc dd ff gg ll mm nn pp rr ss tt zz)
