solution.what: BNE and DECODE image routes tried by script; Cloudflare Turnstile and DECODE login block them.
Catalogue, people, Venetian zifra granda syllabary (Bonavoglia) recorded as a candidate key.
Daniel downloaded the viewer images.
All seven cipher pages transcribed at first pass, 1,528 tokens; clear passages read.
Figure distribution rules out N.11 and matches the 1577-78 Zifra Prima type.
Letter and letter-plus-wildcard annealers on matched synthetic nomenclators recover 0-9 % of letters.
Same annealers on the target give vowel or syllable soup, no separation from shuffles.
DECODE cookie: full-size R2252 images (same BNE scans, ~1.4x the viewer pixels) and keys R1788/R1789/R1790 plus siblings R1843/R1870 fetched; no DOC transcriptions on any.

Zifra Prima per trazer (R1789) transcribed (527 codes) and applied: 94.8% of tokens are defined codes but the decode is not Italian; d83 (commonest token) undefined. Sibling key with same code space, different allocation.
R1790 (c/f/m/r bases, Golfo/Zara cipher), R1870 (Duodo 1595, zifra-granda family) and R1843 (Lippomano 1590) checked: different base sets, not this key.
Zifra Prima with base letters permuted and per-base offsets (coordinate ascent, it-cinquecento LM): only nomenclator-word strings, no text.
CSP Venice viii April 1589 (BHO) checked for a calendar of the 27 April Senate letter: none.

First-pass digit statistics show systematic misreading (7 read as 2, 8 as 0, 3/5/8 confused); with those re-readings the Zifra Prima decodes frequent tokens to the commonest units and passages read as Italian; syllable-usage correlation p=0.0008 vs structured null.
Zifra Prima (R1789) confirmed as this letter's key, unchanged so far: e.g. f.35r ll.16-17 'alcun soccorso per proveder ... al pericolo di quella corona'.

beam.py: per-token Viterbi over digit-confusion variants with the Zifra Prima, it-cinquecento 5-gram with optional word spaces, EM-estimated confusion costs; machine draft Italian in long stretches (draft_beam_v1.txt).
Hand reading begun line by line from candidates + DECODE line crops (rd_f35r.txt; two helper agents on ff.35v-36v and ff.37r-38r); c86 = o and d83 = a found from context (keys/ottobon_overrides.tsv).

Hand reading complete for all 7 pages (rd_*.txt): 721 of 1,566 tokens read as Italian (46%, measure_rd.py); ff.37r-38r 56-72%, f.35r 63%, ff.35v-36v 12-17% (digits unresolvable at the available resolution).
Corpus for the LM: Alberi, Relazioni degli ambasciatori veneti (9 vols, archive.org djvu text) added to the it-cinquecento sources with the shared lang engine (build_venlm.py; 47 M chars).

dec.py: noisy-channel decoder (digit/base confusion model and code prior estimated from the 721 hand-read tokens, Venetian 5-gram LM, vectorised Viterbi beam over whole pieces, skip option, per-token margins). Leave-one-page-out calibration against the hand reading: 644/721 = 89.3% agreement by value vs 65.9% identity baseline and 73.8% at beam.py's weights.

Synthetic test (dec.py sim: hand-read runs re-corrupted by sampling the channel, 627 tokens): 82.6% recovered at 55% identity, 61% at 40%; word-lexicon bonus and self-training EM gave no gain; margin calibration: margin >= 2 agrees 97-100% with the hand reading.
Free decoding of ff.35v-36v gives Italian fragments but no continuous sense (dec_out/, view.py); the decoder alone does not read those pages.

Print search (CSP Venice viii, Hubner Sixte-Quint ii-iii, Desjardins v, Morosini Historia Veneta, De Thou): no verbatim text of the letter or of the Senate's answer; Hubner iii no. 36 (Doge to Badoer 13 May 1589) and ii p. 236 (29 April) give parallel wording only. De Maisse's letter-book with the answers is BL Add MS 30635-30637 (not digitised).

fit.py/refit.py: crib fit of proposed Italian line texts (hand reading, decoder drafts, context) onto the first-pass tokens; a token is read only outside gaps with channel log-prob >= -5; 74 lines re-read (texts_reread.txt).

fitcontrol.py: each text fitted onto wrong lines (15 shifts): 10% of tokens fit by chance at threshold -5 (22% at -8, 5% at -3) vs 80% on the true lines; 5 lines with weak evidence (true <= control max + 2) demoted to low.

Re-measured (measure_rd.py): 981 of 1,565 tokens read (62.7%), from 721 (46.0%); f.38r 84%, f.37v 79%, f.37r 70%, f.35r 68%, f.35v 48%, f.36r 35%, f.36v 29%. New: f.35v ll.7-9 'collegarsi et stringersi maggiormente in qualche unione di lega'; f.37r ll.15-17 'quanto alle richieste fateci da Vostra [...] in nome di quel Serenissimo Re' (second piece = the answer to the French ambassador).
Siblings checked on DECODE (R2248-R2262, Mss/994 items 1-15): no other Venetian cipher and no decipherment; ff.38v-63v in R2252 are address and blank leaves.

Venetian LM registered in lang/ as it-venezia (source it-relazioni, double weight); dec.py now loads it. Leave-one-page-out calibration against the 981 re-read tokens (ALPHA 0.4, BETA 0.4, CLEN 0.3): 870/981 = 88.7% with the registered model and with the old local table alike. Note: these reference tokens include the crib-fit re-reading, so the figure is not independent of the decoder's channel model; the independent figure is the 89.3% against the 721 hand-read tokens.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): first-pass transcriptions ct_f35r-ct_f38r, page readings rd_f35r-rd_f38r and the joined Italian reading.txt, in two entries for the two pieces; key keys/zifra_prima_R1789.tsv with keys/ottobon_overrides.tsv

system.summary: Two-digit homophonic substitution with syllable and common-word groups, three-digit nomenclator groups (200-999) for names and titles, and the digits 1 and 8 as nulls/word separators, written as a contiguous digit stream; the same key as Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), broken by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach in 2018.

diacritics.note: None recorded by the DECODE transcribers, and none seen on DECODE's 1491x2066 scan of p. 5.

system.notes: 112,805 digits over the 28 ciphertexts. Digit frequencies are uneven (0 = 16.1%, 4 = 4.8%) and adjacent digits carry ~0.18 bits of mutual information, so the stream is structured. No phase preference was found for two-digit codes (IC 0.01462 at phase 0 vs 0.01466 at phase 1; even- and odd-position digit distributions agree to 0.2%) or for three-digit codes - though that phase test is inconclusive on its own, since ~1.7% digit slips randomise the phase; the calibrated corpus search is the sound version of the claim. distinct_symbols is the digit alphabet, not the key's code groups, which are unknown. A run-length control puts the longest consistent two-digit alignment to the known plaintext at 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39, where a synthetic two-digit cipher at the same transcription noise gives 207 - so the stream is not a two-digit substitution of that plaintext. CORRECTION 21 Sept 2026: the variable-length diagnosis was right, the rest of the system was not identified here. The key (sibling, 6956) mixes two-digit homophones, three-digit nomenclator groups and one-digit nulls 1/8, which is why every fixed-width test failed and why the repeat spectrum showed deterministic variable-length groups. distinct_symbols stays the digit alphabet; the key has ~127 known entries.
system.sibling_key: Barb.lat. 6956 (1628), key recovered by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach, March 2018, filed on DECODE R215 (DOC_R215_D1506/D1507/D1508). George Lasry identified years ago that 6960 uses the same key; DECODE was never updated. Applied here 21 Sept 2026: it reads 6960.

prior_solution.where: Contents: Kiewning 1897 (Nuntiatur des Pallotto, Bd. 2), from the Roman decipherments. Key: Biermann and Bosbach 2018 for the sibling Barb.lat. 6956, on DECODE R215; George Lasry had found that 6960 uses the same key (told to the project 21 Sept 2026).

conditions.human_role: set the target; on 21 Sept 2026 relayed George Lasry's note that 6960 uses the 6956 key of Biermann and Bosbach
tools: banded DP crib aligner (align2.py, align3.py, align4.py, soft.py, walk.py, syll.py)
space-free Italian 5-gram model built here from lang/corpora it-renaissance + it-gutenberg (12.0M chars, it_clean5.npy)

solution.what: Found the manuscript free on DigiVatLib (Barb.lat. 6960, 194 canvases) and fetched the IIIF manifest; that service maximum is 748x1088 px per page, an old bitonal microfilm scan. DECODE's own scans of the same leaves, found later, are four times larger.
Mapped DECODE R286-R313 to DigiVatLib page ranges from each record's additional_information; established that the volume interleaves cipher sheets with clear register pages.
Searched for a printed decipherment; found Kiewning 1897 (Nuntiatur des Pallotto, Bd. 2: 1629) in full text on archive.org, which prints some forty of Pallotto's 1629 despatches marked 'dechiffr.'.

Matched R286 (pp. 5-6, headed 'Di Vienna 4 di Agosto') to Kiewning Nr. 153, and checked that the clear pages 3-4 and 7-9 run continuously through the cipher sheet with the edition's wording; separately matched p. 13 verbatim to Nr. 153 Beilage II.
Downloaded DECODE's 2019-20 digit transcriptions of all 28 ciphertexts (DOC_R*.txt) with the stored session cookie.

Aligned the opening of R286 against the known opening of Nr. 153 as two-digit codes: 27 letters align exactly (HORICEVUTALARISPOSTADATAMII) with two repeat confirmations, 38=T and 23=I. Read at the time as roughly a 1-in-180 coincidence; the later run-length control shows 27 is BELOW the chance baseline of 36-39 for this material, so it is not evidence.

Ran banded DP EM aligners over the whole of R286 against a hand-corrected 3,359-letter crib of Nr. 153, with two-digit codes plus one-/three-digit resync operations for transcription slips; best code-to-letter consistency about 55%, against a 20% naive baseline.
Tested for a fixed code width: index of coincidence and positional digit distributions by phase for two- and three-digit codes across all 28 ciphertexts. No phase preference at all.
Fixed-multiset simulated annealing over the 100 two-digit codes on 5,000 codes, scored by a space-free Italian 5-gram model built here; -3.54 log-prob per character against -1.5 for real Italian.
Tested a syllabic two-digit nomenclator by aligning codes to plaintext spans of one to four letters; every well-attested code collapsed to a single letter, so no syllable table.

Held-out test: learned a two-digit table on the first 55% of R286 against the crib, froze it, and aligned the remainder. Confirmations per letter 0.355 against a mean of 0.359 over eight controls that shuffle the letters among the same codes; DP score -3266 against -3313. The same test for a 2-digit-plus-nulls model gives 0.440 against 0.431. No separation: the earlier 55% consistency was the aligner fitting the crib, not a key.

Positive control: enciphered the same crib with a random two-digit homophonic key, damaged the digit stream with single-digit insertions and deletions, and ran the identical learner. True key recovered 100/100 at 0% digit error, 87/100 at 0.5%, 7/100 at 1.7%, 19/100 at 4%. The method is sound; it needs a transcription better than about 0.5% digit error.

Found that DECODE serves its own scans of these leaves at 1491x2066 (IMG_R286_I2489_P1.png, IMG_R286_I2490_P2.png), four times the pixel area of DigiVatLib's 748x1088. Re-read p. 5 line 1 on it: it differs from DECODE's transcription in two digits of 74, both substitutions, no length difference - correcting an earlier claim of about six differences including a length change, which was a misreading of the low-resolution image.

Run-length test. Long consistent runs cannot be faked: inside a window a repeated code must carry the same letter. Scanning every (digit offset, crib offset) pair, the longest consistent two-digit run between R286 and the plaintext of Nr. 153 is 39 letters; controls that shuffle the crib letters give 39, 39, 36, 38, 36 and reversing the cipher gives 39. A synthetic two-digit cipher over the same text at 1.7% digit noise gives 207, and a clean one 2705. The same method recovers 81/100 key codes from the noisy synthetic text where the DP learner managed 7. The real material sits exactly on its chance baseline: there is no alignment signal, so transcription noise is not a sufficient explanation, and R286 is not a two-digit homophonic encipherment of Nr. 153. This also retires the 27-letter opening match, which is below the 36-39 chance baseline.

Corpus search (hunt.py). For a substitution, equal codes force equal letters, so each cipher window's repeated-code pairs require the plaintext to repeat at those offsets; checked exactly over all 1,161,303 letters of Kiewning with one bitmask per gap. Calibrated by planting the true plaintext: a synthetic cipher hits its true position in 253/254 windows when clean and 16/254 at 1.7% digit noise, with zero false positives. Applied to R286, R292, R306 and R311 at widths 2, 3 and 4: zero genuine hits (the four apparent width-3 hits all land in the edition's index of Roman numerals). A real fixed-width encipherment of printed text should have given of the order of eight hits on R286 alone, so p ~ e^-8. The ciphertexts are not fixed-width substitutions of anything printed in the volume.

Repeat spectrum over all 112,805 digits against an iid control with the same digit frequencies: repeated substrings of length 8 number 28,519 against 91, length 10 number 12,109 against 1, and there are 39 repeated 24-digit strings where chance gives none. A well-made homophonic cipher cannot produce this, so the system uses deterministic code groups - a code or nomenclator in which a word or syllable is always written the same way. BPE segmentation gives 266 token types over 44,816 tokens, mean 2.5 digits, lengths 1-7: syllable-scale and not fixed width. This is the one positive structural finding.

Polyphonic one-digit-per-letter: the repeat spectra of R286 and the crib match at about 1:1 (3,570 digits, 3,359 letters), so tested the reverse constraint that equal letters force equal digits. Longest consistent letter-to-digit run 17 letters against shuffled controls of 18, 19, 18. Also tested BPE tokens as word codes by whether a repeated token lands on the same plaintext word: 16 of 74 token types against controls of 13, 12, 13. Both chance.

Found a far better crib source in DECODE's own transcriptions, which I had only skimmed: ~640 <CLEARTEXT> annotations across the 28 files and <PLAINTEXT> lines in five of them (R286, R305, R308, R309, R313), DECODE's mark for a decipherment written on the document. Most of these despatches are mixed letters - short ciphered runs embedded in clear Italian - not wholly enciphered texts, which is why a Kiewning-based crib could never have matched them. R308 reads 'Non sono [41 digits] circa il particolare de [...]' with the gloss 'restati piu contenti della risolutione' written above the figures; verified against DECODE's 1523x2088 scan.

Solved the R308 crib exhaustively (41 digits, 34 letters) under every simple model: fixed widths 1-3; deterministic letter code with groups of 1-2 and 1-3 digits (exact enumeration via the length identity, exact.py); 2-digit groups against syllables of 1-3 letters, both with the two-way deterministic constraint (4.0M nodes) and allowing homophones (7.3M nodes). Zero solutions in every case. So either the gloss does not align exactly to that digit run, or the system is more complex than any of these.

Content of the despatches recovered from Kiewning's printed contemporary decipherment, not from the cipher: Pallotto's mediation between the Emperor and the French envoy Sabran over the Mantuan succession, Casale, Susa and the Grisons passes, Aug-Nov 1629.

George Lasry reported (via Daniel) that Barb.lat. 6960 uses the same key as Barb.lat. 6956, broken by Norbert Biermann and Thomas Bosbach. Their keys and a sample decryption were found as files on DECODE R215 (D1505 decryption, D1506 Biermann key, D1507 Bosbach key, D1508 merged key, March 2018): two-digit homophones, three-digit nomenclator, nulls 1 and 8.

Applied the merged 6956 key to DECODE's transcriptions of all 28 6960 ciphertexts by DP segmentation (nulls 1/8, two-digit codes, three-digit groups). R286 opens 'ho riceuto la risposta datami in scritto', Kiewning Nr. 153 verbatim; running Italian throughout. About 2,000 nomenclator groups resolve from the key; about 1,750 three-digit groups are not in it and stay open. Output in key6956/decrypt_6960.txt, unedited.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): per record, DECODE's digit transcription (decode/R*.txt) and the unedited automatic decryption with the 6956 key (key6956/decrypt_6960.txt, split per record into texts/R*_decrypt.txt), with Kiewning's 1897 edition of the contemporary decipherments (ed/pallotto_bd2_1629.txt; crib153.txt for R286); about 1,750 three-digit groups are not in the key, so the automatic decryptions are partial

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). texts/R*_decrypt.txt read (R286, R294, R306 closely): unedited DP segmentation with garbled strings and [nnn] groups in most clauses (docs/_check_reading.py: 2-24% of sentences clean). The 27 sheets R287-R313 relabelled decoded, not read. R286 reads from Kiewning Nr. 153 (crib153.txt, 57 of 58 sentences clean; reading_review A). Class already solved kept (printed 1897); method read with known key -> read from existing decipherment (parts); fraction_read 0.95 -> 0.030.

Reread batch b01 (REREAD_BRIEF): new decoder (reread_b01_decode.py: nulls 1/8 never inside a group, segmentation by an Italian 5-gram model, DECODE's uncertain digits and its 0-for-8 misreading as alternatives); every sheet matched to its Kiewning number by 9-letter hits and aligned chunk by chunk with the print (reread_b01_match2.py, reread_b01_align.py); about 125 nomenclator groups missing from the 6956 key learnt from the alignments and contexts, 776 = tutto and 567 = occasione corrected (reread_b01/extra_groups.json). Unknown groups in the decodes fell from about 5,000 to about 800 (125 groups in extra_groups.json).

Reread batch b01: the 27 sheets R287-R313 read one by one (R290 by the coordinator, the rest by six reader agents of the same model), each with reading, English translation, log and DECODE digit corrections (texts/R*_reading.md, _en.md, _reread_log.md, _corrections.tsv); clear text re-read on the DECODE scans (DECODE's clear-text transcriptions are mostly unusable). 21 sheets build sentences (clean share 0.64-0.94), 6 stay read in part (0.53-0.67): R291, R300, R301, R302, R304, R313. Sheets found to be parts of one despatch: R292-R294 (Nr. 160), R297+R299 (Nr. 164), R302+R303 (Nr. 167), R306+R307 (Nr. 176), R311+R312 (Nr. 184); DECODE dates corrected (the volume runs 4 Aug-29 Sept 1629, not to November).

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): '## Reading' headings added to texts/R294, R295, R299, R303, R308_reading.md (bodies plain 0.806-1.0). Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 22 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

outcome.method_basis: The 6956 key of Biermann and Bosbach (DECODE R215), extended in this batch with about 125 nomenclator groups learnt from the Roman decipherments Kiewning printed in 1897, decodes the sheets; where Kiewning prints a sheet verbatim the reading follows the print, elsewhere it is read from the figures checked on the DECODE scans.
outcome.notes: Contents in print since 1897 (Kiewning). The key was not recovered by this project: every attack here failed. It is the key of the sibling volume Barb.lat. 6956, broken by Biermann and Bosbach in 2018 and on DECODE R215; George Lasry had identified that it also serves 6960. Applied 21 Sept 2026, it reads all 28 ciphertexts except ~1,750 three-digit nomenclator groups absent from the key. The earlier finding of deterministic variable-length groups stands and is explained by the key (2-digit + 3-digit + 1-digit nulls). The catalogue said 'what the cipher hides is not known'; it is known, and has been in print since 1897, from the Roman office's own decipherments. The cipher itself was not broken here and no partial key is claimed: a held-out test shows the table learned from R286 predicts unseen text no better than a shuffled control (0.355 vs 0.359), so the 55% consistency of the first pass was overfitting. A positive control on synthetic ciphertext recovers a random key 100/100 from a clean transcription, 87/100 at 0.5% digit error and 7/100 at 1.7%, so the method is sound and the limit is the transcription. Two explanations remain open and cannot be separated from this material: length errors in the transcription, or the cipher not being a fixed-width substitution of this plaintext. The run-length control then settled that: the longest consistent two-digit run is 39 letters against a chance baseline of 36-39 (synthetic at the same noise: 207), so there is no alignment signal and noise is not a sufficient explanation. R286 is not a two-digit homophonic encipherment of Kiewning's Nr. 153. Open: whether the code width differs, whether the sheet encodes another despatch or a materially different wording, or whether the system is nomenclator-heavy or variable-length. A corpus search over all 1,161,303 letters of the edition then closed the first two: at widths 2, 3 and 4 no window of R286, R292, R306 or R311 enciphers any text printed in the volume, against a calibrated expectation of ~8 zero-false-positive hits on R286 alone. What survives is either a variable-length nomenclator, or text that is not in print because Kiewning gives it only as German regest.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE metadata R7927-R7930 and the images of R7927, R7928 and R7930 with the saved cookie; R7929 has no images.
R7930 turned out to be only the cover of a Palm-Visconti letter plus a 1-500 French/Italian nomenclator worksheet; the letter itself is not imaged. R7928 is a Windischgraetz-Starhemberg key fragment.
Transcribed the 14 cipher passages of R7927 with their clear context and the interlinear glosses.
Applied the R7928 letter key: it contradicts the glosses (40=r vs long s, 23=u vs n).
Simulated annealing on letter values with de-modern 5-grams, codes drawn from a word/syllable list, gloss values pinned; 6+6+6 restarts.
Web search for a printed decipherment of Palm's 1727 intercepts.
Longer annealing (12 restarts x 250k moves) with six gloss pins: scores scattered -1985 to -2022, no two runs agree.

Synthetic German homophonic text of the same length and symbol count (162 tokens, 47 values), true values of the 6 commonest symbols pinned: solver recovered 81/162 and 71/162 tokens (two seeds), unreadable.

outcome.method_basis: R7927's 14 cipher passages were transcribed with their few contemporary glosses, but ciphertext-only annealing failed and a same-size control showed the text is too short; the R7928 key fragment contradicts the glosses.
outcome.notes: Closed as infeasible ciphertext-only: a same-size control with correct pins reaches only 44-50% token accuracy. Needs Palm's key or the Deciphering Branch clear copy.

title: Janos Papai (Belgrade) to Ferenc Rakoczi II, 6 March 1710: six passages in a graphic-sign alphabet (DECODE R731)

documents.shelfmark: MNL OL G15 Caps. H Fasc. 226, pp. 31-33 (DECODE R731)

plaintext.source: none

transcription.source: DECODE camera images IMG_R731_I4153-4155 (2448x3264), zoomed 1.8-1.9x; R731_signs.txt
transcription.notes: Six graphic-sign passages: 316 signs of 14 types plus 55 dot clusters kept as one token each (counted per character, since the file writes one character per sign and --measure splits on spaces). Tentative: the low swash may be a pen link and the dot clusters may be vowel marks.

system.summary: A graphic-sign alphabet of perhaps 25 signs (d-like, pi, m-like, q, division sign, =, '11', with colons and dot clusters) in six short passages inside a clear Hungarian letter.

diacritics.note: dots above and below the bars may be vowel marks; collapsed into one token in the transcription

system.sibling_key: none: R580/R581/R452 (Papai's numeric envoy key) carry no graphic alphabet; the corner sign line on R581 is cipher, not an alphabet
system.notes: distinct_symbols = 14 sign types plus the dot-cluster token in R731_signs.txt. Not the numeric R580 nomenclator of papai1706.

conditions.human_role: Posed the target; supplied the DECODE session cookie earlier.

Validated swap-annealing solver (solve731.py) on Papai's own text enciphered at random, same line lengths: recovered exactly (-8.96/4-gram vs -8.87 real).
Annealed R731 as transcribed, without dots, without swash strokes, reversed: best -10.1/4-gram, no Hungarian.

title: A. Pelissier to Pierre Jeannin, Burgos, 13 September 1592 (BnF fr. 3982 no. 22)

documents.shelfmark: BnF fr. 3982 no. 22, ff. 46r-50r (Gallica btv1b9060543f, canvases 100-108)

plaintext.source: Scattered interlinear glosses by a contemporary decipherer; Tomokiyo calls the letter 'only partially deciphered'

transcription.source: Gallica full-resolution scans
transcription.notes: Sum over the nine page files t46r-t50r.txt, each measured with --drop-first --skip '^\[\[' (clear passages dropped); NOTES give about 18,400 signs in 377 runs. Look-alike glyph families merged in passes 1-2 were split in pass 3 after calibration.

system.summary: Homophonic alphabet of 2-7 signs per letter (symbols and some two-digit numbers), a few doubled-letter signs, vv = et, nulls, and rare three-digit code groups for names.

diacritics.note: Hooks, flourishes, tails and bars separate look-alike signs (s6 = c vs 56 = y; hooked tau = p; barred 8 = q).

system.sibling_key: Pelissier's nos. 45/46 (Madrid, 27 Oct 1592) with clear decipherment on f. 115; Tomokiyo's key reconstructed from them, used
system.notes: Code groups seen: 315 = the Béarnais (firm), 310 = probably Savoy, 441 = probably France (context only, once each).

prior_solution.where: Contemporary interlinear glosses on the letter; key published by Tomokiyo (cryptiana league.htm); no published decipherment of no. 22

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's key image and web search: no published decipherment of no. 22.
377 cipher runs transcribed sign by sign (pass 1, agents).
Re-deriving the key by letter-frequency hill-climbing on the noisy transcription collapsed to an all-e attractor.
Tomokiyo's key applied with a quadgram beam search over each sign's candidate letters; glosses agree.
Pass 2 re-reading: 89% of cipher words.
Calibration: nos. 45/46 aligned sign by sign with the f. 115 clear text (1,764 signs), splitting merged glyph families.
Open-letter diagnostic decode showed the merged tokens directly, matching the calibration.
Pass 3 re-read all nine pages with the split tokens: 94% of cipher words.

Pass 4 (PASS4.md): gap-by-gap high-zoom re-read of ff. 46v, 47r, 47v, 49r. 18 [?] closed from the signs (46v 40->30, 47r 38->34, 47v 42->40, 49r 42->39; one empty gap withdrawn), one unsupported reading withdrawn. (first round).

Pass 4 completed: every [?] on all nine pages re-cropped and re-read, one image agent at a time (46r 11->8, 46v 40->30, 47r 38->34, 47v 42->36, 48r 21->11, 48v 17->11, 49r 42->21, 49v 27->17, 50r 20->15). New readings include une guerre, las de tant souffrir, seroit ueritablement fascheux, uenu a Chalons, Mouson place forte, grandes iournees, debiliter egalement, brider par le traicte, n'estoit, sceust; several empty gaps (no signs) withdrawn. Measured 3,934 words, 183 [?] = 0.953 (177 (?) words counted read; 0.909 if those are counted unread).

Recurring groups z 6 z, 26 I, z 5 8, z 6 1 tested at every occurrence: z 6 z and 26 I also occur as ordinary letters (z+6 = p: "pour l'opposer", "se pourroit", "importunites"); at the name-like places the context allows Mayenne or the King, so no single value is forced. None counted.

solution.what: Fetched R2242 record and four images with the session cookie.
DECODE note points to R1892; same vertical digit pairs, so tried the R1892 key.
One ciphered word in the clear page 2: 24 43 25 55 15 15 65 = famille.
Two subagents transcribed p1 (4 lines), p3 (17 lines), p4 (8 lines + P.S.).
Page 1 clear Dutch under the cipher agrees with the R1892-key decrypt and fixes ~12 word signs.
p3-p4 decrypted with the R1892 key: alliance, scattered troops, Basel ratification, ambassadors to Paris, Robespierrism.

Word signs in p3-p4 read from context and re-checked on the photographs: script L = uit, flagged D-shape = van, phi = Frankrijk (I); perp = om (M, also fits R1892 p2); the ratification passage and the Robespierismus sentence now read without gaps except the sign '&'. Dating consequence: the treaty 'with France' puts p3-p4 after 16 May 1795.
DECODE images not in the checkout; a cookie download returned a 5 kB placeholder; the 21 Sept rotated full-resolution copies were recovered from the old worktree .worktrees/r2242 and copied to img/.
p3 l1 re-transcribed at full resolution: every pair confirmed ('braaden wat zeid men [van] onse alliansie met').

p4 l8 re-transcribed: 32->22 ('woort'), final 42->52 ('broer', a 4 overwritten by 5); 13 32 11 'ynt' is as written, read 'antwoort' as the writer's 1-for-4 slip (M). Also p4 l6 43->34 ('is het'), p1 l4 11->55 ('dienst'), p3 l2 margin 'offeciers', five doubtful pairs given their probable values.

Word signs from context, pooled with R1892: Lambda = dat (M, three R1892 contexts agree), slashed/crossed Lambda = dat, infinity = daar (M, 'daar ... van voorstellen'), < = naar, check-over-bar = zonder (M), crossed e = zijn (M), X = weinig, crossed x = al, & = Engeland, + = mogelyk, crossed diamond = voor, Y-crossbar = ik, crossed Y = dez-.

Colenbrander, Gedenkstukken I-II full text (resources.huygens.knaw.nl retroboeken) searched for Grasveld, Sitter, Blaauw, Robespierismus, gebraaden, persisteeren, saamenhang, gedimitteerde, verstrooid, Banquier, rassemblement, ratificatie; GS II pp. 834-841 read. The letter is not printed.

The interlinear insertion 'sitteren [inverted D] grasveld' = '[de] Sitter en [van] Grasveld', the extraordinary envoys to Paris (GS I p. 655), and 'Meier en Blaauw' = the negotiators Blauw and Meyer (GS I no. 507): fixes the inverted D = van and dates p3-p4 to late May-June 1795.

Remaining single signs tried and not adopted: plain Delta (Staaten / zyde each fit one context), T-bar and S-stroke ('goeds', 'kan'), psi and H-loop on p4 l8, %, C-hook, crossed o, V-with-cross, H-with-P, dagger, square/vertical brackets, x mark, Delta-with-tail, P.S. signs.

Measured with apply.py --measure and measure_sense.py (nl-modern, 13-char window > -4.3, calibrated on p1 and letter-shuffled controls): tokens given a value 95.2% -> 97.9% (1,015/1,037); tokens read as sense 86.0% -> 94.6% (981/1,037).

Sense measure made strict and fairer (measure_sense.py): STRICT=1 counts I-grade sign values as unread; a token also passes inside an attested 6+-letter word (lang/ nl corpus + Gedenkstukken I-II OCR, fetch_gedenkstukken.py); y scored as ij for Dutch. Letter-shuffled control passes 8.4% (max 12.2%), unchanged by the word check.

Grades re-examined under a forced-context rule (M = several contexts agree or grammar admits one word): script L uit, phi Frankrijk, crossed Y dez-, slashed/crossed Lambda dat, Y-crossbar ik, crossed x al, < naar upgraded to M; X weinig, & Engeland, + mogelyk, crossed diamond voor stay I and count unread.
Every token failing the sense test checked on the image: p3 l6 31->34 (saamenhang); p4 l3 'persisteern' confirmed as the writer's (t e e r n).

Read as sense, strict: 941/1,037 = 90.7% (HEAD transcription, 30 Sept signs) -> 940 (2 Oct, LM only) -> 953 (+word check) -> 979 (+forced upgrades) -> 994/1,037 = 95.9% (+y as ij). With I values: 1,000/1,037 = 96.4%.
Gaps re-sorted: signs occurring twice (Delta, %, crossed diamond) stay open-codes; the nineteen true singletons are blocked by no-key-material (one context cannot fix a word sign).

Outside contribution reviewed (PR #31, WAINUT): seven proposed sign values from shape matches with R1892/R2242 and context (crossed o = zijn, dagger = al, P.S. S = maar, crossed o-slash = voor, H with P/loop = verwacht, psi = over, plain delta = kan). Not measured; the R1892 control (leave-one-out 1-8 tokens, LM rank first at 5 of 47) shows measure_sense.py cannot confirm such values. Kept as proposals; key and outcome unchanged.

Located f. 19v in the Alvin scans (attachment 42; attachment 40 is f. 18v) and downloaded the full TIFF.
Transcribed the four ciphered lines letter by letter (125 letters, 19 words with two line-end hyphens).
Applied the inverse shift, first word by word under the Latin model: k and x were misjudged because the model folds k into c, and prp came out as oro.
Fixed k=i and x=u (neither is a consonant in the text) and chose b/f/p by beam search over the whole colophon: the output matches the catalogue's reading word for word, prp = pro in context.

Prompted by the stop hook, checked all 175 Alvin images of C 513 for DECODE's 'six symbols in a note'. Back pastedown: clear pen trials only. Front: a pasted Old Swedish note to Anders Larsson ending in six signs.
Transcribed the slip's clear Old Swedish text (herbs and cinnamon bark sent for Anders Larsson's chest) and the six signs ÿ ɑ M ÿ u ꝺ.
Applied the colophon's vowel shift to the six signs: none of b f k p x occurs, so it does not fit.
Tried all 23 alphabet shifts on five readings of the signs (yamyud, yamymd, yanyud, yamynd, iamiud) and plain abbreviation (initials, closing formula): nothing.

reading.md: 232/264 cipher signs read as sense (87.9%).

A1 'instantia [y S] de ven[i]re': the cipher has no separate 'a' after instantia; y S conjectured 'me' (grade I, from the clear lead-in 'caso acaduto mi'), printed '[a m]e'. A2 'o[y] le mie': every single-letter value for y tried by hand, none gives Italian; left open. Counts unchanged.

Re-transcription of the open stretches from Gallica natives (fr. 3070 = btv1b9059934c view 127; fr. 3082 view 65) at full resolution. B3 sign d is a cursive theta (i), so 'volse r[c d 9]a' = 'r?i?a', which the corpus fills only as 'ruina' (123 vs next 14): c=u, 9=n by the word. A1/A2 y confirmed one sign; A6 X found straight-stroked, unlike A2's cursive x; B4 sign after xi has a back-loop. 'piu volse' has one u sign for both words.

The old 87.9% was a hand count by phrase (e.g. 7 signs for A2's one open sign y). New measure.py counts per sign, a sign read only inside a corpus word (it-cinquecento corpora, >=3 hits) or a listed spelling: 245/264 = 92.8% (A 134/149 = 89.9%, B 111/115 = 96.5%). Below 95%: A6 (12 signs) is the block.

texts.label: A. BnF fr. 3070 f. 81r, Venice, 10 Jan 1530
texts.summary: Guido Rangone to Anne de Montmorency: in cipher, that Venice pressed him to enter its service, then sent word to 'Signor Cesare' (Cesare Fregoso, Rangone's new brother-in-law) and made him great offers while Rangone was slighted. The clear rest is news of Venice (the Duke of Urbino, the Turkish envoy, Milan, the Swiss, Genoa's galleys). Section A of reading.md; cipher lines A1-A6 of cipher.txt.

reading_review.note: reading.md read through: A1-A5a build Italian sentences (he presses [me] to come into their service; he has sent to tell it to Signor Cesare and to make him great offers) with one-sign holes; only the last clause A6 ('la [?]icon puorano a tenderui', 12 of 149 signs) does not read. The low automatic score counts the clear passages and the editorial notes. Audit grade C refined: the cipher insertions are short but read.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 91.5% of the words of fr3070_f81_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

texts.label: R4233, fr. 3053 f. 6 ff., Rome, 26 Jan 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
texts.summary: The cardinal de Mâcon to Montmorency: pourparlers on marriages for Pier Luigi Farnese's children, the imperial ambassador and Venice; if the French cardinals were in Rome they could steer a conclave, the pope being 'septuagenaire et plus'. He reports the mission of cardinal Verulano's secretary to Switzerland and suspects 'quelque dessaing sur le duché de Millan'. Pass 5 (shape-true re-transcription, signs and reading line by line) supersedes the earlier R4233.md.

texts.label: R4234, fr. 3053 ff. 16r-18v, Rome, Feb 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
texts.summary: Soundings on a settlement, the bishop of Lodi's view that the King should never consent, cardinal Pisani's report, the marriages of Pier Luigi Farnese's children and the match with Cosimo de' Medici, and the arming of Pier Luigi's army (Stefano Colonna for the foot, Giovanni Battista Savelli for the horse). Pass 5 supersedes the earlier pass files, also listed.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. The pass-5 running reading of ff. 16r-17v builds long French sentences (the soldiers raised for Parma and Piacenza, the Milan plan, Contarini); the [?] holes are scattered, densest on f. 16v, and f. 18r's elisions are in the clear passages, not the cipher.

texts.label: R4235, fr. 3053 f. 21 ff., Rome, 15 Feb 1536 o.s. (= 1537)
texts.summary: 'J'ay sceu de bon lieu que le dict pape vouloit entretenir le Roy de mariage', to use the King's good words with the Emperor; Mâcon begs Montmorency to tell no one but the King and to keep the envoys' charge secret, above all from the bishop of Verona (Giberti). The three contemporary marginal decipherments agree with the reading word for word.

texts.label: R4238, fr. 3053 ff. 32v-33r, Rome, [xiii?] Sept 1536
texts.summary: The bearer is sent by the Sienese exiles to press the King to an enterprise against Siena, which Mâcon sees no prospect in; a German at Rome claiming to be of Ferdinand's chamber offers to enter the King's service and gives him letters for a lansquenet captain with count Wilhelm von Fürstenberg.

texts.label: R4239, fr. 3053 ff. 35r-38v, Rome, 6 Apr 1537
texts.summary: The marriage of Ottavio Farnese to the Emperor's daughter Margaret, the intrigues of the exile cardinals Salviati and Ridolfi after Alessandro de' Medici's murder, and a bid for Pier Luigi Farnese: against the Imperialists' offer of Novara, Mâcon counters with 'quelque honneste estat en France'. Ff. 37r-v are a contemporary clear copy of letter 2 (pass5/R4239_f37_clear.md).

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. Letter 2 (f. 36r-v) and the second paragraph of letter 1 (Ridolfi, the duke of Urbino) read in whole sentences; the first paragraph of letter 1 is summarised with elisions and f. 38r ll. 5-14 are read only in part (listed as gaps).

texts.label: R4240, fr. 3053 f. 40r-v, Orvieto, 2 Sept 1536
texts.summary: The general council: Vergerio carried word to the Germans that they might come and speak as the Holy Spirit inspired them; the pope, judging this 'la totale ruine de l'Eglise', has sent an auditor to summon them on the old custom instead, and the Germans say pope, cardinals and bishops must first be reformed.

texts.label: R4247 letter 1, fr. 3053 f. 77r-v, Orvieto, [early Sept] 1536
texts.summary: Andrea Doria and Milan: Mâcon infers from Doria's letter to the conte dell'Anguillara a secret treaty between the pope and the Emperor and puts it to Paul III; then cardinal Filonardi's man sounds him on Milan passing to Pier Luigi Farnese's son or the young Sforza, and Mâcon answers that the King will never consent, Milan 'estant leur vray heritage'.

texts.label: R4247 letter 2, fr. 3053 f. 78v, Orvieto, 1 Sept 1536
texts.summary: The second letter of the record, signed by Mâcon at Orvieto on 1 September 1536; it ends 'il seroit icy fort difficille de recouvrer gens de cheval ne artillerie; bien trouverroit on tant de gens de pied, et bons, qu'on vouldroit, et beaucoup de gentilz homes forussiz'.

texts.label: BnF fr. 3071 no. 4, ff. 9-10 and slip f. 9bis, Rome, 11 Apr 1537
texts.summary: Mâcon to Montmorency, 11 April 1537: the Farnese marriage offer (Vittoria Farnese to Cosimo de' Medici) and Paul III's threat, relayed through Latino Giovenale, to declare for the Emperor if it is refused; Pier Luigi Farnese and Novara; the King's Turkish alliance 'se verifie clerement'. title: Roosevelt cryptogram, 1935, numeric block (Schmeh Top 50 no. 17)

documents.shelfmark: Secret Service sheet received 24 Apr 1935, reproduced in The Friedman Legacy (NSA 1992) fig. 2, p. 8

plaintext.source: Friedman read only the letter part ('Did you ever bite a lemon?'); nothing for the digits.

transcription.source: Internet Archive 300 ppi scan of The Friedman Legacy, checked against the Cipherbrain image
transcription.notes: --measure gives 57 tokens / 52 distinct, counting the zero groups and the final dash as tokens; the numbers proper are 52 (1..52, each once). The third line of cipher.txt does not match the sequence quoted in NOTES.

system.summary: A permutation of 1-52, each once, with four groups of zeros; statistics fit a list written by hand.
system.sibling_key: none
system.notes: Tick-joined pairs are exactly 10-52, single digits exactly 1-9; rising-sequence and rank-correlation tests favour hand enumeration over a shuffled deck.

prior_solution.where: Ernst 2017 (Cipherbrain comments) argued the block is a doodle; no reading exists

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: structure.py (permutation statistics, shuffles, GSR riffle model)
solve_ordered.py (annealer over ordered keys, Copenhagen 5-gram English LM)

solution.what: Digits read from the 300 ppi scan; tick-joined pairs taken as one number.
Block shown to be a permutation of 1-52; rank correlation, consecutive runs and rising sequences against shuffles and riffle models.
Ordered-key homophonic controls on 52-letter English passages recovered 7 of 8 at 88-100 %.
Six ordered-key readings of the block (sequence and inverse, both alphabets, zero groups as breaks) give no English.

outcome.method_basis: The digit block was shown to be a permutation of 1-52 with zero-group separators, confirming Ernst's 2017 doodle argument; no message.
outcome.notes: Ernst's 2017 doodle claim confirmed; no message.

credits.note: argued the digit block is a doodle (tick-joined pairs give 10-52 once each), confirmed here
credits.source: Cipherbrain comments to Schmeh's Top 50 no. 17 post (Dec 2017)

credits.note: extended Ernst's argument to the full permutation 1..52; his number list matches the reading
credits.source: Cipherbrain comments to Schmeh's Top 50 no. 17 post

title: The Rosamonde telegrams: Sun Yat-sen and Soong Ching-ling, 1915–1916

documents.shelfmark: Diplomatic Archives of the MOFA of Japan, 1.6.1.4-2-1-2 vol. 1, JACAR B03050087600 (8 Jan - 11 Mar 1915)

plaintext.source: Japanese copies of the telegrams with no translation; per the contributor no decipherment exists in the volume or in the literature he checked.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout's edition (bdudout.github.io/wenmi/en/rosamonde.html): forms transcribed from the JACAR scans by Claude and, blind, by Brice Dudout (89% of letters identical in the initial sample).
transcription.notes: Eleven telegrams (17, 20, 21, 23, 25, 26 Feb; 3, 6, 7, 9, 11 Mar 1915). The project transcribed two of them (20 and 26 Feb, images 45 and 52) from the scans in the contributor's repository: 15 ten-letter words, measured in ciphertext_checked.txt together with 7 July. The contributor's full transcription is not in his public repository, so the set's length is not measured here.

documents.shelfmark: Diplomatic Archives of the MOFA of Japan, 1.6.1.4-2-1-2 vol. 1, JACAR B03050087700 (Mar 1915 - Feb 1916)

plaintext.source: No decipherment with the copies.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout's edition, as above.
transcription.notes: Four telegrams (12, 15 Mar; 10 Jun; 7 Jul 1915). The project transcribed 7 July (image 50): 5 words, 50 letters.

documents.shelfmark: Diplomatic Archives of the MOFA of Japan, 1.6.1.4-2-1-2 vol. 3, JACAR B03050089000 (29 Apr - 22 May 1916)

plaintext.source: No decipherment with the copies.

transcription.source: Brice Dudout's edition; per his page the 1916 forms were transcribed blind before the key was found.
transcription.notes: Seven telegrams (1, 4, 8, 10, 11, 12, 13 May 1916). Not checked against the scans here.

system.summary: English telegraphic text, unspaced and cut into ten-letter words, enciphered by a reciprocal letter substitution (twelve swapped pairs, d and p unchanged).
system.notes: Key a-u b-g c-s e-o f-j h-y i-r k-z l-t m-w n-v q-x, d and p fixed; the same key from Feb 1915 to May 1916. Names, numbers, reply addresses and a few words (happy, Inuzuka, iron, trunk) stay in clear. The last word of a message is cut at ten letters (husba[nd]); the 7 July message ends in a stray p. The 1915 forms twice write qq where pp is expected (6 Mar). The project's 200-letter sample has 23 distinct letters (measured).

prior_solution.where: Per the contributor, not in Bourdeau's sunintercepts work on the 1916 intercepts, Yang Tianshi 2001, Zhu Jiulin 2016, or Chang & Halliday 1986; other works not yet checked.

conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout found the telegrams in the JACAR volumes and directed the work; Claude transcribed the forms, Brice re-transcribed them blind, and the key was recovered by simulated annealing with an English quadgram model (contributor's account). The project only re-deciphered three telegrams from the scans.
models: Claude Opus 5.5 (Brice Dudout's sessions; he says he mainly uses Opus 5.5)

solution.what: Contributor found a family of ten-letter word telegrams (Tokyo to 'Laisaosang' and 'Rosamonde', Shanghai) among the Chinese-code telegrams in JACAR B03050087600 and B03050087700, and more in the May 1916 volume B03050089000.

Forms transcribed from the 200-dpi JACAR scans twice, by Claude and by Brice Dudout blind (89% of letters identical in the initial 20 texts); the 6 and 7 March 1915 additions reviewed on a prefilled transcription.
Letter index of coincidence 0.062 (natural language, so a substitution, not a code); f and q absent; trigram hea x10.
Simulated annealing over all 26-letter substitutions, then over reciprocal substitutions only, scored by an English quadgram model; key a-u b-g c-s e-o f-j h-y i-r k-z l-t m-w n-v q-x, d p fixed.
English text enciphered with a random key recovered at 100% by the same search.

Out of sample: the key from the 1915 telegrams alone scores the blind 1916 transcriptions at -5.97 against -8.01 +/- 0.27 for 2,000 random reciprocal tables (z = 7.5), and Brice's blind 1915 re-transcription at z = 10.9; a telegram in another system stays at z = 0.6 (contributor's figures).

Read 95 = my and 98 = artillery from context; c2 = do, b2 = can, k4 = nor, 412ant = warrant as conjectures; about 15 code groups left open.
Content matches Digby's letters of 27 and 30 April 1645 (the King cannot bring the train to Rupert; Rupert should march) and Rupert's march on Oxford in May.

Correction after an outside check of the phrase 'you may come and fetch it' against the key: the groups 68 4 | 75 86 93 c-o-m-e e5 f-e-t-c-h 83 f2 give y-e-u [86][93] come IN fetch it. On the image the 4 stands at the torn edge (probably 45, so 'you'); 86 and 93 are outside the key and mark phrase ends elsewhere, so 'may' is supplied, not read; and the sign transcribed e5 is the King's clear '&' (same form as in 'friday & sonday' and 'Oncle & most', unlike his three small e5 groups), so 'and' stands as his own word. Transcription and ciphertext corrected (304 groups); page, reading.md and NOTES now print 'you [may] come and fetch it'.

texts.summary: The King keeps the Prince of Monaco in play without a treaty (1631); a sergeant-major offers Sabran the castles of Savona, a Savoyard plot that is discovered (1633); Genoa helps the Spanish fleet while France fights for Valenza (1635).

reading_review.note: v3 check 23 Oct 2026: the sweep scored lasry2022/ctts/decryption/all.txt, CTTS's raw output (spaced letters, [plaintext] placeholders; 0.0). The reading is lasry2022/READING.md: its 18 '### French' sections (clear and cipher together, image markers cut) score 0.721 on explicit holes, 0.536 plain (the manuscript's v-for-u spelling: tovchant, avtre), hole rate 0.086; the cipher runs alone (401 bold segments) 0.84 explicit, 0.712 plain, hole rate 0.129. Sentences hold. Rests on Lasry's CTTS key (ciphertext-only, 2022) completed from context in 2026; the 212 tentative name-code readings ([France?] ...) count as holes; no contemporary decipherment. v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): French of 1631-35, where the plain share is a bar too; but this writer spells by ear (secretere, trete, afaire, eloignemant, munitionere, gouuernet) and the name codes read tentatively count as holes. Rescored: the 18 '### French' sections plain 0.519 (277/534), explicit holes 0.715, hole rate 0.088 (as at v3). The plain failures are those spellings, names (Garbarin, Sauli, Fiasque, Monaco, Valence) and the name-code holes (no key material). Sentences hold. Keeps read.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 92.9% of the words of lasry2022/READING.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

title: Saint-Luc(?) to the King or Villeroy, 30 January 1586 (BnF fr. 15572 f. 43): key recovered by George Lasry

system.summary: Homophonic substitution of 20 letters plus x with 51 two-digit-labelled symbols (two or three per letter; i five, s four), 20 signs for 17 words and syllables (que, qui, est, de, et, dict, tout, faire, je, vous, lui, bien, plus, peut, pas, mal, ons), one doubling sign, one abbreviation sign and 10 nulls.
system.doubled_letters: A doubling sign [x2] after the letter (36 occurrences).
system.sibling_key: None. Saint-Luc's other ciphered letters in the volume (ff. 245, 260) use another table (Tomokiyo); f. 43 is not Mayenne-Forget's Cipher-1 or Matignon's Cipher-3 (matignon1586 NOTES).
system.notes: Sign labels are CTTS's two-digit numbers for invented symbols. 36 = et and 84 = lui are tentative.

prior_solution.where: George Lasry's own 2022 solution: Tomokiyo's cryptiana page of Lasry's solutions (GL.htm, 'An Unsigned Letter in BnF fr.15572 (1586)') publishes his key image; no plaintext published. conditions.human_role: George Lasry transcribed the three images in CTTS and recovered the key with its built-in cryptanalysis (2022); in 2026 he resolved the last thirteen signs from context with Claude Opus 5.5, edited and translated the French, and contributed it as PR 76. In this repository: merge, mechanical re-application of the key, statistical validation, prior-solution check, write-up.
tools: CTTS (CrypTool Transcriber and Solver): transcription and built-in cryptanalysis

solution.what: George Lasry transcribed f. 43 (three photographs) in CTTS: 1,315 signs.
CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis recovered the letter homophones (George Lasry, 2022); the key image was published by Tomokiyo on cryptiana GL.htm. Date within 2022 not recorded.

The thirteen signs still unassigned were resolved from context with Claude Opus 5.5 (71 = ons, 23 = q, 68 = je, 101 = vous, 70/89 = peut, 91 = bien, 100 = plus, 102 = pas, 103 = mal, 97 = abbreviation r; 36 = et and 84 = lui tentative).

George Lasry edited and translated the French and checked it against CTTS overlays of all three images (PR 76): an intelligence report in cover names (the concierge, the gardener, the stonecutters, the governor, the planter).

Merged PR 76. decode.py re-applies lasry2022/ctts/key.txt to the transcription and reproduces George's counts exactly: 1,315 signs = 1,168 letter homophones + 77 word signs + 44 doubling and abbreviation signs + 26 nulls, none unassigned. The f43a overlay checked by eye against the decode.

Prior-solution check: GL.htm carries only Lasry's key image for f. 43 ('It is solved as follows'), no plaintext; no printed decipherment found on the web; matignon1586 records f. 43 as outside the Mayenne-Forget and Matignon ciphers.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 1271 tokens, 81 types, fr-1600-letters order 4: reading -2.091 per letter; random keys -4.722 (z 9.9); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.968 (mean -3.014, z 25.7); annealer on the real text -2.203. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.091; polyphony 0.0; 44 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.203

outcome.method_basis: George Lasry recovered the homophonic table with CTTS's built-in cryptanalysis from the ciphertext alone (2022) and resolved the last signs from context with Claude Opus 5.5 (2026); no clear copy or outside key exists.

solution.what: Tomokiyo's 'St. Luc's Cipher' table (cryptiana henryiii) encoded as labels with values; nulls and the word signs kept (Brackx, #90).
f. 245r-v (cipher passages, 423 signs) and f. 260r-v (26 and 29 lines, 2,428 tokens) transcribed sign by sign from deskewed full-size line crops (Brackx with Claude Code, #90).

The margin decipherments of f. 245v (crib 1) and f. 245r (crib 2) aligned with their cipher: key corrections Δo = Monsieur du Mayne, ʞ = pour, ⊔ = la Rochelle, new signs ss and la, Ↄ = rr, crossed ʒ = h, plain 3 = m, ♀/♁ = n/p, x; letter agreement 89.3% (f. 245v) and 83.2% (f. 245r) under the corrected Essais model, shuffled-key controls 11-31%.

f. 260r-v decoded by beam search over each label's allowed values under a French character 5-gram; 741 single-value key candidates tried; corpus-word coverage 79.2% / 80.7% (controls 27-46% / 31-49%). A decoder bug that skipped lines beginning with the label # was fixed (r. 8, v. 19 restored).

Brackx's reading of f. 260r-v in the writer's spelling with every unread run sized and an English translation (#90, reply of 23 Oct 2026): Oléron, the shallops and galliots, the stone-laden ships against the palisade, the unpaid garrison, the Rochelais passports and the salt of the grand parti. 22 letters read with another value of the same label than the decoder chose.

Read bar applied (v10_relabel.measure): f. 260r 0.761 and f. 260v 0.851 of words read as sense. Letters on multi-valued labels are 40.5% / 34.5% of the text, over the 3% look-alike limit, so both pages are graded decoded, not read whatever their share; the readings are kept as partial readings with English.

Method restored: key obtained by Tomokiyo's published St. Luc table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments (read with known key); text not read, class stays not read. The 22-24 Oct reading audit had set the method to not solved because the class was not read; George Lasry (24 Oct 2026) separates the two.

outcome.method_basis: Tomokiyo's published table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments, decodes f. 260r-v into French that largely builds sentences (0.761 / 0.851 of words), but 40.5% / 34.5% of the letters fall on labels with several values chosen by a language model, so the text is decoded, not read. Method restored 24 Oct 2026 (George Lasry: a key can be mostly recovered while the text is not read): the key was obtained by Tomokiyo's published St. Luc table, corrected on the f. 245r-v margin decipherments; class stays not read, as the text does not read.

solution.what: Searched for a prior decipherment; found Tomokiyo's article of 6 Sept 2025, which reconstructs the whole cipher from the contemporary decipherment attached to DECODE R9605. Saved to tomokiyo/.
Pulled DECODE record pages R9603-R9657 and tabulated the metadata (decode/getrec.py, decode/meta.py).

Checked the catalogue entry against the records: the run is 9/23-9/26 not 9/24, every record is dated 1522 so nothing reaches the July 1523 treaty, nine of the tail records are Lope Hurtado de Mendoza not Sánchez, and almost all carry a contemporary decipherment (DECODE 'Inline Cleartext: Yes').

Transcribed Tomokiyo's nomenclator to key_codes.tsv and tested its ordering: codes are C1(16) x V(5) x C3(9) and sorting by (C1, C3, V) puts the plaintext in alphabetical order, so unassigned codes are bracketed by their neighbours.
Fetched DECODE images for R9633-R9657, the 9/26 tail that Tomokiyo's article does not cover.
Predicted the unassigned numerals of the c-block by interpolation: cef=xxvi, cif=xxvii, cof=xxviii, cuf=xxix, cab/ceb/cib=xv/xvi/xvii.

Read the two-line foot cipher paragraph of R9653 f. 299r: 'cartas de Francia de xxvi y xxvii del passado de ...', which confirms the predicted cef=xxvi and cif=xxvii. Read the clear middle of the leaf (the siege of Rhodes) from the image.
Attempted the six-line head cipher paragraph of R9653 f. 299r; ink bleed from the facing leaf leaves it not confidently transcribable at the available resolution.

Checked whether the Lope Hurtado de Mendoza letters of the same group use Sánchez's cipher. R9648 f. 260v gives code groups ending in p and z (tep, tap, xulz), finals absent from Sánchez's third-position inventory {b c d f g h l m n}; so his key is a third member of the family, not Sánchez's. Whether it is Juan Manuel's is not settled.

Read R9635 f. 20r (16 Sept 1522, outside Tomokiyo's range) in part: a full page of cipher with a patchy interlinear decipherment. Recovered 'das cartas de vuestra magestad', 'los de esta republica', 'del senor infante', 'ducados allende de los otros xviii mil', 'mas de xv mil ducados', with the glosses 'obligados ... fuessen restituydas sus bienes'. Subject: sums owed by the Signoria under the capitulation and restitution of goods seized from imperial vassals.
cab = xv, predicted from the ordering rule, attested in 'ped xig cab pol9 vud+s' = 'mas de xv mil ducados'. Third of the seven predicted numerals confirmed in text; none contradicted.

Settled the notation: pol9 = pol (mi) + the letter sign for l = 'mil' (the l sign reads as a g in this hand); g-y + lal (publica) = 'republica'; the opening nulls are padded with the meaningless clear words 'como' and 'quien', which is what Tomokiyo's 'como quierr' note under the nulls column means.

Fetched R9605 (the record Tomokiyo broke the cipher from) and found its cipher and the clerk's full contemporary decipherment on facing leaves. Aligned the end of the letter: 'plegue adios nuf pac g-y-B-4-q-4 vog veg zn-B-ai nuf' = 'plegue a Dios no lo yerre en el camino', with vog veg = 'en el' met in situ.

Two findings from that alignment: code groups are used for syllables as well as whole words (nuf is 'no' the adverb and the last syllable of cami-no), so one-group-one-word segmentation fails; and the lookalike signs separate as B = m (camino), curly-q = r (ahora), bold-infinity = g, which is the largest source of error in reading the spelled runs at DECODE's resolution.

Attempted a continuous reading of the spelled-out letter runs on R9635 f. 20r. Not achieved: separating B / curly-q / bold-infinity is a judgement call at each occurrence and guessing them yields plausible Spanish that is not what the page says. Left marked rather than filled in; the R9605 calibration is the route through.

Continued the R9605 alignment: xel def = 'del visorey', ded+xof = 'venida', pog = 'mesmo', suf = 'hago', and the spelled run for 'escrivo' fixes z=c, curly-q=r, ai=i, m=v, #=o against ground truth. Correction to the published key: va = 'despacho', not Tomokiyo's 'desponho' (not a Spanish word), which also explains his puzzled 'me desponho x-e-r-o-n que' in R9623.

Checked whether the c-block numeral run starts where assumed, by aligning the group cud against the clear at 'que fue a ...'. Inconclusive: the date there is written over a correction and reads as two dates (xxv y xxvij), so it cannot be matched to one group. cab, cef and cif are unaffected, each having been confirmed in its own context.

Aligned the opening of R9605 (f. 39r) with the first page of its 1522 decipherment (f. 42), straight through: cig='ya', vu+x+e='dixe', vam+vuc+r='embaxador', spelled Hun-gria, sa='fue', r-e-s-p-o-n+di+do='respondido', de esta + r-e + publica = 'desta republica', xa + buen+a+s = 'con buenas'. Fixes the sign table against ground truth: n=a, y-curl=e, curly-q=r, ai=i, o=x, #=o, q=s, ao=p, &=n, m=v, z=c, B=m, plural=s. Note q=s here against Tomokiyo's alphabet q=t, two similar glyphs. Carried into alpha.py with the ground-truth values marked.

Applied the calibrated sign table to the first line of the unread R9635 f. 20r. It does not unlock it: deg, feb and z-n-r resolve to nothing, though the tail ('das cartas de vuestra magestad') and the null padding are secure. This corrects an earlier diagnosis in this folder - the bottleneck is not the sign table but the step before it, turning the cursive shapes into labels. R9605's hand and R9635's differ enough that a shape read as 'd' in one is something else in the other, and a wrong label yields a code group that does not exist or has the wrong value. The alignment must be done on the image, glyph against the clerk's word above it, not by transcribing to labels first.

Corrected the model of the writing, which was the real blocker: everything is written in ordinary latin-looking cursive, with three-letter trigrams as nomenclator codes and single letters/short runs as the substitution alphabet (n=a, y=e, g=r, o/x=x, #=o, ao=p, m=u/v, z=c, B=m, 9=l, q-double-bar=s). Verified on R9605 f. 39r l. 1 against the clerk's plaintext: cig vu-o-y n dom pud ho veg = 'Ya dixe a vuestra magestad que el'.

Edition pass on R9635 f. 20r (edition/r9635_f20r.md). ll. 2-3 read continuously: 'pues en esto no se puede perder nada ... con los de esta republica'. About a third of the page read; ll. 4-5, 8-13, 15-21, 23-25 left untranscribed rather than inferred.

New code value: lel = 'puede', bracketed between lal (publica) and lol (pudi) and fixed by sense in 'no se puede perder nada'. Also observed a code group used mid-word for a syllable (perder = p-e-r + xig(de) + r), the pattern R9605 showed with cami + nuf(no) = camino.

Edition pass continued on R9635 f. 20r: ll. 4, 9 and 10 added. l. 9 gives nul(obliga)+vuc(do)+s = 'obligados', which is exactly the word the 1522 decipherer wrote in the gloss above that stretch - key, alphabet and gloss agreeing independently. Coverage now about half the page; ll. 5, 8, 11-13, 15-21, 23-25 left untranscribed. The token gta, a dozen occurrences and not a possible code (middle position not a vowel), is left unresolved rather than forced.

Edition continued: ll. 9(right), 11 and 13 of R9635 f. 20r. 'me lo que antes de ahora'; yig(capitula)+c-i-o-n = 'capitulacion'; 'que quien Inglaterra que los' with hec = Inglaterra. Coverage now about three fifths of the page; ll. 5, 8, 15-21, 23-25 still untranscribed.

Edition continued: ll. 17-21 of R9635 f. 20r. 'estos xx mil de ahora'; 'poderlo hazer porque' with suf(ha)+z-e-r = hazer and lu(por)+ho(que) = porque; 'las quales' with lul(qual)+ta(es). Codes are also run together to make one word, the mirror of the stem-plus-ending pattern. Coverage about three quarters of the page; ll. 5, 8, 15, 16, 23-25 still untranscribed.

Edition continued: ll. 22-25 of R9635 f. 20r. 'darian todos los ...'; 'no pude de ... los'; 'si no se ... en'; and the page ends opening a fresh paragraph with the three nulls and 'los de esta republica'. cag is proposed as xxx (end of the numeral run, immediately before cig 'ya') but marked probable, not certain, being one slot past the attested run. Coverage about six sevenths of the page; ll. 5, 8, 15, 16 still untranscribed.

l. 5 of R9635 f. 20r: xof veg + p-r-i-m-e-r-o + xig ta = 'da el primero de es[te]', which fixes B = m on this page independently of 'camino' in R9605. At high zoom the ending of capitulacion on l. 11 is the curly second form of c that Tomokiyo draws as backwards-3, so capitulacion is settled rather than inferred. Coverage about nine tenths of f. 20r; ll. 8, 15, 16 remain.

Last lines of R9635 f. 20r: l. 15 = 'xviii mil ducados primer[o]', l. 13 'vuestra magestad', l. 16 'das las'. Every line of the page now has a reading of some kind; the page is read throughout in substance (subject, sums, parties, drift of the argument) while a scatter of spelled runs inside partially-read lines stays open. Recorded caveat: the crops were cut by dividing the written area into 25 equal bands, so line numbers are approximate and may be out by one; the readings are anchored to their own words, not to the numbering.

Moved to R9635 f. 21 (edition/r9635_f21.md): two more full pages of cipher, denser than f. 20r. The decipherer's gloss 'obligados ... fuessen restituydas sus tierras' continues here. A paragraph written entirely in the clear, marked A in the margin, reads in full: Richard Pace (Micer Ricardo Paceo), Henry VIII's envoy at Venice, has given Sanchez an enclosed memorial and asked him to press the Emperor for the letters Pace wants for the Pope and for don Juan (Juan Manuel at Rome); Sanchez seconds it. This fixes the identification behind the code hec = Inglaterra met on f. 20r. The two leaves are not yet transcribed line by line.

Grepped Bergenroth, CSP Spain vol. 2 (1866; british-history.ac.uk pp380-519) by Salazar folio A.23-A.26 and 'Alonso Sanchez'. Fourteen of this folder's DECODE records are calendared as 'Autograph in cipher. Contemporary deciphering' (nos. 429, 439, 444?, 447?, 462, 470, 473, 476, 482, 487, 488/489, 491, 495?, 500). R9635 = no. 476 (16 Sept 1522, A.26 ff. 20-22): the abstract confirms the 18,000 ducats outstanding and the Pace memorial, and shows the 'restituydas sus tierras' gloss is the Venetians' demand that their towns be restored. May 9/24 run and R9653 (20 Nov) not calendared.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): edition/r9635_f20r.md, r9635_f21.md and read_r9635.md (cipher groups and reading of the lines done), read_r9653.md; key key_codes.tsv with calibration_r9605.md; no full transcription of either letter exists

Reading audit (George Lasry's test: can a reader build coherent sentences and translate them?). read_r9635.md, edition/r9635_f20r.md, r9635_f21.md and read_r9653.md read: f. 20r is a table of phrase fragments between untranscribed letter runs, R9653's cipher gives one phrase in its foot paragraph; what reads as sentences is the clear text (the Rhodes news, the Pace paragraph on f. 21), not decipherment. Both letters relabelled decoded, not read; class read in part -> not read, method read with known key -> not solved (key kept as a part); fraction_read 0.6 (estimated) -> 0.

Re-read brief b23, step 1: DECODE R9635, R9653 (and neighbours R9634, R9636, R9652, R9654, R9655) re-fetched logged in and every image opened. R9635's P3 right page (f. 22r) is a full clear contemporary decipherment of the letter, never examined before; transcribed (R9635_decifrado_f22r.txt). R9653's 'illegible head paragraph' is the bleed-through of an eleven-line cipher passage on f. 299v, fully legible; no decipherment of R9653 is bound or imaged (f. 300v duplicate and R9654 not imaged).

R9635: the f. 22r decipherment aligned with the cipher of ff. 20r-20v as read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key (visto que tanto, no se puede perder nada, capitulacion, el primero deste mes, obligados, allende de los otros xviii mil, mas de xv mil ducados, estos xx mil de agora, poderlo hazer porque, todos los suyos ... en Francia): all agree; the earlier edition's 'darian' is pagarian, and hec = Inglaterra is withdrawn. New values from the decipherment: deg = visto, feb = tanto, gim = suyos; tac = tenian? flagged. Reading R9635_reading.md, 0.833 explicit-hole share (20/24); state read, grade A.

R9653: the 13 cipher lines (f. 299r foot, f. 299v) transcribed sign by sign on 1.6-2.6x crops and read with Tomokiyo's key (R9653_cipher.txt): sign values ∝ = m, ꞔ/∂ = e, g# = u/v, ẗ4 = n, q = t, 3 = d, bold ∞ = g, ƀ = b, each holding at every occurrence; Ꝁo/Lo read s or t by sense (look-alikes). Reads: este embaxador y ahun la señoria tienen cartas de Francia de xxvi y xxvii del passado de Sangerman; dize que passando los ingleses a su tierra se perdieron dos naos dellos ... y los otros dieron a traves en Bretanya; nuevas sin fundamento; don Ioan Manuel. Sense-only values flagged: fef = toda, ref = Italia, zub = Adorno; feb = tanto from R9635. Open: xug, zi, tac, lud, qef, sob, ca, nu.

R9653 scored: reading body 0.842 explicit-hole share (32/38), 0.368 plain, but the cipher passages alone 0.455 (5/11) explicit holes, 0.091 plain: the second cipher paragraph (Adorno, the protonotary, Juan Manuel) has seven open code groups in four sentences. Kept decoded, not read; R9653_reading.md kept as a partial reading. 15 letters rest on a look-alike sign.

r2i: R9635 f. 22r tear (about ten words, ll. 9-11). No second copy or decipherment on the record (P1-P3 only) or the neighbouring records; the passage read sign by sign in the cipher of f. 20r ll. 11-14 with Tomokiyo's key: 'en la dicha capitulacion. Repliqueles que las tierras estavan en poder del señor infante, y respondieron que quien quiera que los tuviese vuestra magestad havia prometido restituyrlas'. New values hec = quiera (the 20 Sept 'Inglaterra' withdrawn), vac = dicha; gta = l-sign + ta = les. Reading 0.833 -> 0.913 explicit holes.

r2i: all DECODE records R9593-R9657 of Sánchez (52, Lope Hurtado excluded) fetched with images and record text; all 163 images opened on contact sheets. Decipherments found only for R9605 (known), R9613 (ff. 206r-207v, new), R9635 (known) and R9641 (ff. 187r-188r, filed under R9642, new); R9654 has no images; the rest are cipher with clear passages, no decipherment.

r2i: R9613 (18 June 1522) read from its contemporary decipherment (R9613_decifrado_f206.txt, 103 lines), first sentence checked against the cipher of f. 203r with Tomokiyo's key (hug = recebi confirmed). R9613_reading.md 0.99 explicit holes, 0.657 plain; English R9613_en.md.

r2i: R9641 (27 Oct 1522) read from the contemporary decipherment on ff. 187r-188r (DECODE R9642), checked against the cipher opening and closing (vad = duque, new). R9641_reading.md 1.0 explicit holes, 0.735 plain; English R9641_en.md. R9642 is the duplicate cipher ('es treslado de otra enbiada por via de Genova; esta va por Roma').
r2i: the remaining ~40 Sánchez letters of 9/23-9/26 not read: no decipherment imaged, sign-by-sign reading with the key not attempted in this pass (gap not-attempted).

r2o: CSP Spain 2 (Bergenroth 1866) checked entry by entry on british-history.ac.uk (nos. 380-515, date and Salazar folio of each): R9593 (5 March) not calendared; R9594 (15 March, opening 'recebi las cartas de vuestra magestad de xxiv') = no. 396, whose contemporary decipherment Bergenroth saw in the Gayangos papers ('the despatch in cipher is not extant'); the others matched as in NOTES (calendar abstracts give the gist, not the Spanish text).

r2o: R9593 (RAH Salazar 9/23 ff. 27r-27v) transcribed sign by sign from DECODE's two images on line crops at 2.0-3.5x and six-line blocks at 1.75x: 53 lines, 1,248 tokens of which 520 code groups (counted on R9593_signs.txt); date confirmed by the clear subscription 'en venecia a v de março de dxxij'.

Key values adopted: gim = suyos (R9635 decipherment + four contexts here), fef = toda (todavia twice, todas); ril = lansquenetes? entered flagged (sense and slot, five contexts). About twenty groups open; f. 27r ll. 26-33 and f. 27v ll. 11-13 do not build sentences. v2_score 0.614 explicit holes (27/44), 0.136 plain, hole rate 0.13; look-alikes ~2.5%. Kept decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: 23 Oct 2026 (b23): R9635 is read from its contemporary decipherment, a clear copy on f. 22r of the DECODE record, checked against the figures of ff. 20r-20v with Tomokiyo's 2025 key. outcome.notes: The cipher itself was already solved and published by Tomokiyo in September 2025, so this is not a break. Added here: the catalogue entry's shelfmark, date range and authorship corrected; the ordering rule of the nomenclator, and from it a c-block numeral series of which cab = xv, cef = xxvi and cif = xxvii are confirmed in text and were not in the published key; and first readings of parts of R9635 and R9653, both outside Tomokiyo's coverage. fraction_read is the share of code groups resolved on the two leaves worked; the spelled-out letter runs and the other 27 records are open. Also established that the nine Lope Hurtado de Mendoza records in the group are in a different cipher, which deserves its own target. The R9605 calibration fixes the sign values against ground truth but does not by itself unlock the unread pages: the binding constraint is the transcription of the cursive shapes, which differ between scribes, and that has to be done glyph by glyph on the image. An edition pass against the published key then began (edition/), reading about a third of R9635 f. 20r continuously and adding lel = 'puede' to the key.

texts.label: R9635, Venice, 16 Sept 1522 (RAH Salazar 9/26 ff. 20-22)
texts.summary: Alonso Sánchez, imperial ambassador at Venice, to Charles V: the money owed by Venice under the treaty ('mas de xv mil ducados', 'allende de los otros xviii mil'), restitution of goods, 'los de esta republica' (calendared by Bergenroth, CSP Spain 2 no. 476). Edited against Tomokiyo's published key; only ll. 1-3, 6, 7, 14, 22 of f. 20r and the opening of f. 21 are given, cipher groups and reading side by side.

reading_review.note: R9635_reading.md follows the contemporary decipherment of the letter, a clear court-hand copy on f. 22r (DECODE image P3, right page); checked against the cipher of ff. 20r-20v with Tomokiyo's key. r2i (23 Oct 2026): the tear across f. 22r ll. 9-11 is filled from the cipher of f. 20r ll. 11-14, read sign by sign ('en la dicha capitulacion. Repliqueles que las tierras estavan en poder del señor infante, y respondieron que quien quiera que los tuviese ...'; hec = quiera, vac = dicha, gta = l + es = les). No second copy or decipherment on the record or its neighbours. v2_score 0.833 -> 0.913 (21/23) explicit holes, 0.435 plain (period spelling). Open: four uncertain words of the decipherment ([?ya]/[?bastar], [?tenido], [?Menorami], [?Lucerna]), illegible at DECODE's resolution.

texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b23): the 'illegible head paragraph' is the bleed-through of an eleven-line cipher passage on f. 299v; with the two foot lines of f. 299r (13 lines, 274 signs) it was read sign by sign with Tomokiyo's key (R9653_cipher.txt, partial reading R9653_reading.md). The first paragraph builds sentences (the French ambassador's letters of 26-27 Oct from Saint-Germain; English ships lost on the way home, the rest driven ashore in Brittany; 'nuevas sin fundamento'), the second (Adorno, the protonotary, Juan Manuel) does not: seven open code groups in four sentences. Cipher passages 0.455 clean on explicit holes (0.091 plain); the whole body's 0.842 rests on the clear text. Blocker: no-key-material (groups absent from the published key, single contexts, no decipherment bound or imaged; the f. 300v duplicate and R9654 are not imaged).
texts.label: R9653, Venice, 20 Nov 1522 (RAH Salazar 9/26 ff. 299-301)
texts.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: the clear middle gives the news of the siege of Rhodes from the Signoria's letters (fifty thousand Turks dead, the defenders hoping for relief); the two cipher lines at the foot are read with the published key; the six-line head paragraph is illegible at DECODE's resolution.

texts.label: R9613, Venice, 18 June 1522 (RAH Salazar 9/24 ff. 203-207)
texts.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: his audience with the Signoria on the imperial reply to their peace paper (paper against paper; the Venetians complain the Emperor leaves the peace-and-league negotiation for a new truce, and that the Infante Ferdinand may enter the truce but not the peace); the Pregadi's debate on Cremona; French boasts and Lescun's news of 600 lances and 12,000 Gascons at Turin; the Turk not arming at sea, Rhodes holding out, Venice selling offices; the Viceroy of Naples at Mantua.

reading_review.note: r2i: the reading follows the contemporary decipherment, a clear copy on ff. 206r-207v of the same DECODE record (never opened before), transcribed line by line (R9613_decifrado_f206.txt); its first sentence checked against the cipher of f. 203r with Tomokiyo's key, word for word (hug = recebi confirmed). v2_score: 0.99 (104/105) explicit holes, 0.657 plain. Three uncertain words in the fast cursive ([?nescia], [?nemora], [?sus pagos]); look-alike letters 0 (the reading rests on the clear hand). CSP Spain 2 no. 429 abstracts the same letter.

texts.label: R9641 (+ duplicate R9642), Venice, 27 Oct 1522 (RAH Salazar 9/26 ff. 173-188)
texts.summary: Sánchez to Charles V: the Signoria content with the Pope's answer on quartering imperial troops in the Gera d'Adda; the papal nuncio at Venice says the Pope could bring Venice round, but the hope of an Anglo-imperial settlement with France keeps them irresolute; postscript: Girolamo Adorno's letter and the Emperor's of 26 Sept announcing Adorno's coming with powers.

reading_review.note: r2i: the reading follows the contemporary decipherment on ff. 187r-188r, filed on DECODE under R9642 (DECODE: 'Sánchez?', status N/A), transcribed line by line (R9641_decifrado_f187.txt); checked against the cipher at the opening of f. 173r and at f. 174r ('de todo esto tengo dado aviso al duque de Sessa'; new value vad = duque). v2_score: 1.0 (34/34) explicit holes, 0.735 plain. Two uncertain words ([?conversacion], [?vera]); look-alike letters 0.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution alphabet with three nulls, plus a nomenclator of consonant-vowel-consonant code groups assigned in alphabetical order of the plaintext.

diacritics.note: A 'q' with a double bar suffixed to a code group marks the plural ending -s.

system.sibling_key: Juan Manuel's 1522 Rome cipher (DECODE R9499-R9529), same design, different values; also reconstructed by Tomokiyo. R9605 and R9613 carry full contemporary decipherments on leaves facing their cipher, and are the calibration source for the hand.
