solution.what: Found the ten records in the DECODE group harvest (Salazar 9/28, author Alonso Sánchez), pulled record pages and metadata; all flagged Inline Cleartext: Yes. Fetched 32 images.

Viewed the images: no interlinear or facing decipherment; 'Inline Cleartext' means clear passages. Same hand and cipher as the 1522 despatches; letters addressed to the Emperor, not an unknown recipient.

Fetched Bergenroth CSP Spain vol. 2 (1523) from British History Online; nos. 549, 552, 554, 558 are these despatches (Salazar A-28, matching folios), each 'Autograph in cipher. Contemporary deciphering.'
Mapped each record to a CSP entry by date line, content and folio; R9670/R9674/R9690/R9770 are duplicates; R9767, R9769, R9770 (16 Aug 1523) are not calendared.
Applied the 1522 key (targets/sanchez1522/key_codes.tsv) to code groups on R9670, R9671, R9672, R9677, R9767: they read coherently; key unchanged into 1523.

Read R9767 (16 Aug 1523): clear text in full; cipher passages at code-group level, spelled runs partly. Gist: French-leaning party in Venice, the treaty's money clause, the Infante not bound to the defensive league.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked Bergenroth's CSP abstracts (R9670-R9690) and read_r9767.md; no ciphertext transcriptions; R9769/R9770 not transcribed

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): read_r9767.md and csp/bergenroth_abstracts.txt read. The seven calendared letters read through Bergenroth's coherent English abstracts of the contemporary decipherings (reviewed B, language en); R9767's cipher passages are [code] strings with … between them (gist only) and R9769/R9770 have no file. R9767, R9769 and R9770 relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept.

Re-read b34: fetched the record pages of the neighbouring DECODE records R9764-R9766, R9768, R9771, R9772 and the four images of R9768 (ff. 565-568, Alonso Sánchez, status Decrypted, never fetched before). R9768 is the second copy of R9767 (f. 565r cipher, f. 566r clear close) and f. 567r is the contemporary decipherment of R9767's two cipher passages. Opened all images of R9769 and R9770: R9769 f. 570v carries a nine-line cipher paragraph after the date (not noticed in Sept), and R9770 f. 574r is its contemporary decipherment.
Transcribed the two contemporary decipherments (R9767_decifrado_f567r.txt, R9770_decifrado_f574r.txt) and the whole clear text of the joint letter R9769 from full-resolution crops.

Aligned the cipher of R9767 f. 563r and R9769 f. 570v group by group with the decipherments (R9767_cipher_align.md, R9769_reread_log.md). All codes but one are in the 1522 key; the figures agree with the decipherments except two places in R9767 ('porque dan los' for 'por dar a los'; 'una paz' for 'paz'), where the readings follow the figures. Corrected the earlier partial decode: xug was spelled m-a-l, yol is yoh = causa, the run after suf is expremido.

New code value pem = -mos, adopted: it holds at all three occurrences (diximos in R9767; prometiessemos, procuraremos in R9769), each under a contemporary decipherment, and its alphabetical slot (between pol 'mi' and ne 'muy') fits. Proposed for sanchez1522/key_codes.tsv, not written there.

Wrote R9767_reading.md and R9769_reading.md (with English) and scored the reading bodies: R9767 0.684 (13/19) plain, 1.000 explicit holes only; R9769 0.575 (50/87) plain, failures only 1523 spellings, 1.000 explicit holes only. R9767 and R9769 marked read (grade A), R9770 read through R9769 (grade B).

outcome.method_basis: The code groups were read with Sánchez's own 1522 key (Tomokiyo, cryptiana AlonsoSanchez.htm 2025, extended in sanchez1522), unchanged into 1523; the May-June despatches were already calendared by Bergenroth (CSP Spain 2, nos. 549-558) from the contemporary decipherings.
outcome.notes: The May–June despatches were deciphered at the time and calendared in English by Bergenroth in 1866; the key was published by Tomokiyo in 2025. Added here: the records identified against the Calendar, the recipient corrected (Charles V), the 1522 key shown to hold in 1523, and (23 Oct 2026) the two uncalendared August letters read in full from contemporary decipherments found on neighbouring leaves (f. 567r on DECODE R9768 for R9767; f. 574r on R9770 for the joint letter R9769/R9770), each checked group by group against the cipher. New code value pem = -mos.

plaintext.source: A. Büchi (ed.), Korrespondenzen und Akten zur Geschichte des Kardinals Matth. Schiner II (Basel 1925), no. 541, pp. 67-72: full text, cipher passages deciphered by Büchi and T. Schiess and set in italics (the original has no decipherment). system.summary: Words and phrases of a Latin letter written in cipher and set into clear text, with a monogram for 'Vestrae Majestati' (Brewer); the sign system is not known here, and Büchi printed no key.

B XIX f. 342); keys never printed. The only sign-level fact known is Brewer's monogram for 'Vestrae Majestati'.

prior_solution.where: Büchi, Korrespondenzen und Akten II (1925), no. 541: full decipherment by Büchi and Schiess; partial reading in L&P II 2044 (1864); content abstracted in 1516 (L&P II 2045). Missed by the 22 Sept 2026 sweep, which checked L&P and Tomokiyo only.

tools: e-Helvetica (Swiss National Library) PDF of Büchi II

solution.what: DECODE record list (10,106 records, research/catalogue_harvest/decode/list.json) grepped for Vitellius and Schiner: no record. BL searcharchives: Cotton MS Vitellius B XIX 'Digitised Content: No'; the digitised hit is Galba B VI. The leaf cannot be seen online.

BHO L&P II June 1516: no. 2044 (Vit. B XIX 131, 'Hol., Lat., pp. 4, partly in cipher, not deciphered … Sense obscure') and no. 2045 (abstract, Vit. B XIX 133); Brewer's n. 4: 'Vestrae Majestati. A monogram in cipher'. BL catalogue folio list: letter now f. 129, abstract f. 131.
Tomokiyo's cryptiana Schiner item is a 1520 letter to Schiner (Saragossa, numerical cipher, solved by Nicollier, Jacquemet and Evéquoz): another correspondence and system.

Büchi, Korrespondenzen und Akten II (1925): HathiTrust behind a Cloudflare bot check (not bypassed, although the user asked); archive.org has only the old QSG series; found on e-Helvetica (nbdig-59316, vol. 2 PDF, 708 pp.).

Büchi preface pp. VIII-IX: 29 letters of vol. II partly in cipher, keys reconstructed by Büchi with Dr Schiess, all broken but no. 582. No. 541 (pp. 67-72) = this letter, 'Autograph … teilweise chiffriert, Chiffer dort nicht aufgelöst und hier in Cursiv wiedergegeben'.

Pages 67-72 rendered from the PDF (the text layer drops italics) and the italic stretches marked by eye: 14 stretches, 88 words, on pp. 67, 68 and 70; full text in buchi1925_no541.txt, stretches in cipher_passages.txt with English renderings in NOTES.

Compared with L&P: Brewer's extract gives the words of stretches 7-12 (Milan, the Empire, Bari, Galeazzo) and omits 1-6, 13, 14; the 1516 abstract (L&P 2045, Büchi 542) summarises the same ciphered content (Bari knows everything, Pace suspected, the Empire and Milan), an independent contemporary check on Büchi for 7-12.
catalogue.json grepped for other 1511-1527 entries in Schiner's circle (Sion, Schiner, Pace, Wingfield, Visconti, Colonna, Lang, Vitellius, Galba) that Büchi might also resolve: none besides 290.

Final search for any image of the leaf, to decipher it independently: the old BL viewer URL for Cotton_MS_Vitellius_B_XIX redirects to a generic collections page; the BL searcharchives query returns only the Galba B VI manifest; Wikimedia Commons and the web have no image of Vitellius B XIX. An independent solve needs a BL imaging order (paid; for the user to place).

texts.label: f. 233, Henry of Navarre to Ségur, October 1585
texts.summary: Navarre, a month after the bull of excommunication, tells Ségur in Germany to conclude promptly, if possible with Duke [John] Casimir or with his consent, to raise the largest levy he can and march it at once; Clervant is to raise the two thousand reiters he is bound to furnish under the contract with the Churches.

texts.label: f. 239, Henry of Navarre to Ségur, Montauban, February 1586
texts.summary: From Montauban: spare no means, succour us in all diligence, set every piece in motion. The postscript in another hand adds Drake's 'very great prize' (the sack of Santo Domingo, January 1586).

texts.label: f. 288v (slip), Henry of Navarre to Ségur, 1 April 1586
texts.summary: Navarre is in extreme anxiety at having no news and asks Ségur to make, if he can, the greatest levy ever made; the two thousand reiters Clervant is bound to furnish are very necessary. The levy marched in 1587 to the disaster of Auneau.

reading_review.note: Overturns the per-document C. reading.md's notes resolve most word signs from context ({gne} = Je, {na} = nouvelles/affaires, {Ra} = faictes, {qu} = vous), and with them the slip reads: "Je suis en extreme peine de n'avoir eu de vos nouvelles ...; je ne sçay [par où vous] escrire, ne à qui, ne en quel estat sont nos affaires ... faictes s'il vous est possible la plus grande levée qui ayt esté faite". Open: the date sign {e}, the name signs {H} {L}, {pe} {pu} and {qua}.

documents.shelfmark: L'Italia del Popolo no. 40 (Milan, 30 Jun 1848), Roman broadsheet reprint (Tip. Puccinelli); Cipherbrain 13 Dec 2014

plaintext.source: Spada prints only the clear covering letter and a paraphrase; Il Labaro (7 Jul 1848) printed a guess.

transcription.source: Joe's transcription (blog comment #4) checked line by line against the scan
transcription.notes: Counted as single digits (955), not as groups: the text mixes the separator 5, two-digit groups and 8XXX codes. One dropped 4 restored on line 12.

system.summary: Two-digit 64-cell table of letters, homophones and syllables over digits {0,1,2,3,4,6,7,9}, 5 as word separator, 8XXX one-part alphabetical code for words, lone 1-4 as punctuation.
system.sibling_key: Same design as the 1814 Vienna nunciature cipher (Ramliden); not used as a key.
system.notes: Code stems combine with spelled endings; one print error (4 printed as 5).

prior_solution.where: Posted as unsolved on Cipherbrain 2014; no reading in Spada or Il Labaro

No target-specific intervention recorded.

Hand refinement: alpha=o, q=o (lone q = que), 9/p=a, z=e, e/n=s, c=n, 2=l, code leh=en.

system.notes: Shapes A-I = the nine pigpen cells (A=RB, B=LRB, C=LB, D=TRB, E=box, F=TLB, G=TR, H=TLR, I=TL in archive orientation), K = stem with a middle bar, X = rare extra sign; * = inner stroke; digit = dot count. Each page has a 'cypher' note. So Butler printed the cipher passages deciphered, including f. 59 (candidate words on p. 56). The data has no word order, so his wording is unseen.

archive.org full-text search. R. S. Love, Blood and Religion (2001), quotes the f. 50 passage ('great hope, that he [i.e., Montpensier] will render himself of the Religion', cited as Edmondes to Burghley, 19 Jan and 3 Mar 1593, PRO uncalendared State Papers) and 'faith is not vendible' (f. 60v), from the letters as received; his bibliography does not list Butler. HMC Salisbury IV (1892), pp. 559-560, prints a different Edmondes letter from the camp before Laon (9 Jul 1594) with its cipher undeciphered, and none of ours. Stevenson's Unton Correspondence (1847) prints Unton's 1591 cypher, a different key.

Dating checked. Edmondes wrote the English year, which began on 25 March. Butler's running heads put ff. 50-61 in Jan-Mar 1593, and the 1895 BL Stowe catalogue starts the volume on 18 June 1592, with f. 27 (26 Sept 1592) promising the Unton cypher. So 'Tours, 3 Mar 1592' and 'Blois, 16 Mar 1592' are 1593 in modern reckoning, and the document years were corrected from 1592 to 1593.

title: Telegram to Sun Yat-sen, Swatow to Tokyo, 3 April 1916 (JACAR B03050738800)

plaintext.source: The Japanese Foreign Ministry could not read it; the file holds no solution.

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's transcription checked against the JACAR PDF (600 dpi render of frame 0296)
transcription.notes: 177 code letters per NOTES; no ciphertext file to measure. Four letters corrected on the image (gedocijiga, xitonatula, kufonemige, baxuxepeja).

system.summary: Standard Chinese telegraph code condensed to consonant-vowel syllables by a systematic table (20 consonants rotated to l, vowels e a i o u, column-major 01-00), no additive.
system.sibling_key: Same family as Yamada Junzaburō's two published condenser tables; used to define the search family.
system.notes: Ten letters (five syllables, two codes) per word; 46 of 50 distinct syllables confirmed.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo's attempts with the Yamada tables negative (blog 12 Dec 2021)

conditions.human_role: Supplied the 11-page JACAR PDF

solution.what: Syllable statistics: Yamada's 20 consonants, rare u pointing to a vowel-major table.
Brute force of the systematic condenser family scored by a Chinese character LM; winner 49 points clear.
Decoded 41 of about 44 characters.
Four doubtful codes fixed by sense and confirmed in the handwriting; content matches Mo Qingyu's March 1916 rising.
Tail checked on a 600 dpi render: the garble is the operator's; three characters unrecoverable.

Tail re-examined as a Morse transmission slip (the received sheet is clean, so the errors are the telegraph's): p (.--.) = a (.-) + n (-.) with the letter space lost, so ropezpo = ro pe za no = 返港 'returns to Hong Kong'. A Morse re-division search (morse_tail.py) of zpo gives four valid codes at one space change (港, 砉, 彼, 嫗); only 港 fits. The last word ngobunibai gives no sensible decoding with up to four space changes; 翼□ (5068) one-letter and one-element Morse slips give no word or known name.

Outside check of the sibling intercepts (sunintercepts page; not the Swatow sheet). Brice Dudout re-read our March-May 1916 condenser transcriptions on the JACAR scans. Of 47 transcribed g he checked, 30 are q on the form, because this copyist's q has its loop on the right. Of our 21 emendations, 19 are already correct on the form, so they were the model's misreadings, not clerk slips. Our 3 Apr 1916 transcription had left out a whole word. Confirmed here on our own PDFs: 0489a gyrobatapo (b, not our t); 0416b xodugoluro (x, not our r); 0416b qiheyuxifa (q, not g), settled by the twin 0416a, transcribed here and decoded in his six-vowel grid with no emendation, which ends 確否速示俾便行止; and the omitted word jobusosuji (088300 fr. 0489), which realigns the 3 Apr tail to 已澈查局非誣騙. His full list of 28 corrections is not yet checked item by item.

March 1917 forms (B03050090200 fr. 0504-0507) re-examined after the 1916 finding. 23 Mar: our transcription had left out two whole words, macorarala veyurojiji, so the 'clerk's lacuna' was partly ours. 22 code words now, matching the form, and about nine codes after 妥 are still unread. 26 Mar: the form has Qeta (capital Q) and zahu (h), so the emendations g->q and k->h were misreadings. 25 Mar: zubo's z has the clerk's x shape. The other 1917 emendations are not rechecked.

One-key review (Lasry's rule, 14 Oct 2026): this profile is the Swatow telegram of 3 Apr 1916 and its one condenser key. The credits for other keys were taken off it: Brice Dudout's decipherment of the July-November 1916 systems and his transcription corrections (y1916, sibling intercepts, not the Swatow sheet), and wanglu2016's issue #23 identifications (1917 telegrams, y1917). They stay credited in y1916/NOTES.md, y1917/NOTES.md and on the sunintercepts page, which has no profile of its own yet.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Tomokiyo's transcription and the Chinese/English decipherment copied verbatim from NOTES.md into texts/; decode_out.txt (decode.py output, codes and the recovered condenser table) linked as decryption and key

Verification 5 (plain bar, 23 Oct 2026): the text is Chinese; not scorable by the word lists; read by the reader (one unread character, last word garbled). Rescored with research/reading_audit/v2_score.py; all entries keep read; reading_review notes record both scores.

validation.notes: plaintext is Chinese (telegraph code); no letter model

outcome.method_basis: The condenser table (20 consonants rotated to start at l, vowels e a i o u, numbered column-major) was deduced from the ciphertext by analogy with Yamada's known tables, then read through the standard Chinese telegraph code; Tomokiyo's attempts with Yamada's own tables had failed.
outcome.notes: 42 of about 44 characters (港 restored from a Morse slip, M, 30 Sept 2026); the last word, about two codes, is garbled in the received copy; 翼□ second character unresolved.

credits.note: transcription of the Swatow telegram (frame 680682), checked on the image

texts.label: Swatow to 'Rosamonde Tokio', 3 Apr 1916 (JACAR B03050738800)
texts.summary: A telegram signed 'Tanaka' from Swatow to Sun Yat-sen's household in Tokyo, intercepted by the Japanese Foreign Ministry, which could not read it. It reports that Mo Qingyu declared Chaozhou independent against Yuan Shikai, that Sun's men recovered Swatow, and that Mo then came with a large force and ordered them out of the garrison headquarters.

reading_review.note: v5 check 23 Oct 2026 (plain bar, VERIFY5_BRIEF): the text is Chinese; the sweep scored the English gloss as English. The word lists cannot score Chinese; read by the reader: five sentences, one unread character (翼□) and the last word garbled, 港 restored from a Morse slip (grade M). Sentences hold. Keeps read.

title: R4306: Dutch diplomatic cipher, transcribed with CTTS and solved with Opus 5.5

Earlier riksarkivet1628 survey reports failed numerical attacks in multiple languages and rejected keys R4296/R4310. These are prior attempts, not new runs in this contribution.
Project attempt split from the catalogue-207 group entry riksarkivet1628 as its own entry riksarkivet4306 under the one-key rule; both transcriptions re-measured. No new attack.
CTTS digit selections were merged into numerical units; current supplied snapshot contains 463 selections in 35 rows. Subsequent sign corrections are recorded in the preserved source-key comments.

George Lasry confirms that Opus 5.5 solved the cipher after CTTS transcription. The working-key header describes crib dragging; the result is an alphabetical number mapping with nulls. No historical plaintext or external key supplied the recovery. Exact prompts and run settings are not reconstructed.

Matched all 463 position labels to transcription counts; counted 461 cipher elements after excluding date numerals, and reapplied the current key to exactly five manuscript lines without correcting their spelling.

Checked public DECODE metadata: Riksarkivet Chifferklaver låda II:133, three record pages, broad 1600–1699 catalogue range, blank correspondents/languages and Non-decrypted status. Image manager requires login; only the supplied cipher page is independently inspected here.

Deduplicated under one key, one entry: the project's attempted-open entry riksarkivet4306 (same record R4306) folded into this contributed entry; its transcriptions moved to project_attempt/, its page made a stub pointing to sweden4306.html, its ledger rows removed. The contributed key, reading and counts were not changed.

Opened R4306's two other DECODE views at full resolution: address leaf I25833 ('Aen Mr. ?ilick (Wilick?) ... Amsterdam', confirming the earlier survey's Amsterdam) and wrapper I25834 (II:104, '1600- Chifferbref till ... i Amsterdam'). The address leaf carries a 3-line cipher note in its right margin with codes 113 and 101.
Applied the contributed key to the address-leaf note: 'ler.,[torn]hlden / [113]naeldan / kn[101]na..mk'; all Caesar offsets of a 24-letter alphabet and the R4287 sequential key also tried: no Dutch.

A faint list on the wrapper image (Nz ..., Oz ..., Tz Rex Polon., Vz Victoria ...) matched to the last leaf of R4305 (Brandenstein 1630 key, II:132, filed next to R4306): a show-through/offset from that key, not R4306's nomenclator.

Surveyed every Chifferklaver låda II key record on DECODE for an alphabet a=30 ... y=52 with a 100+ nomenclator: the archivists' wrapper labels ('a = 7, 35, 51' etc.) of 43 records, the pages of the unlabelled and wrapperless records, and the never-downloaded R4319-R4321. None matches. R4287 ('diverse chiffernycklar ... av okänd proveniens') is a similar sequential type with another alphabet (a=2/28/10, c=31).

R4319 (Jacob du Moulin, 1650) is the same chancery template at another offset: sequential alphabet a=20 ... z=43, then an alphabetical nomenclator from 101 (101 Archangel ... 112 Ambassadeur, 113 Amsterdam; B from 120). By analogy R4306's 101-114 would be A/B-initial words. Not testable on five occurrences; offered to George as a proposal.

Checked the doubtful spots (lines 4-5 ekll|men, line 33 Mar..y) on the page image: the scribe's tailed 0 makes 30/38 and 40/43 ambiguous; no better reading can be forced. Gap reclassified as illegible.

Brett Burford (issue #47): independent keyless re-reading (own transcription, annealing with a 17th-c. Dutch model, nothing seeded) agrees with Lasry's key on all 21 values, 447/463 groups (96.5%) and 411/422 letters (97.4%); flags L12 g7, L20 g9, L23 g13 (4/9 form rather than 8), L26 g4, L34 g1. Reading the scribe's tailed o as 8 turns the address-leaf note (I25833) into Dutch: ter... / ...niet dan... / in [101] na... (42 38 34 48 33 30 = n i e t d a). Recorded as a proposal; the image could not be re-checked here on 21 Oct (DECODE cookie expired).

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): George Lasry's CTTS transcription and token file, edited Dutch reading, translation and key (key.txt), the five-line mechanical excerpt, this project's earlier transcriptions, and, as a separate file, the address-leaf note with Burford's proposed reading copied from NOTES to texts/address_note.md.

title: Beverning and Vande Perre to Boreel, Westminster, 22 Aug/1 Sept 1653 (Thurloe State Papers i.435; cryptiana unsolved item #9 a)

documents.shelfmark: Bodleian Rawlinson A (Thurloe papers) vol. v p. 240; printed TSP i.435
documents.route: Westminster -> Paris (Beverning and Vande Perre to Boreel)

transcription.source: Birch, Thurloe State Papers (1742) via British History Online
transcription.notes: Measured with --digits --skip '^(?!\d)' (cipher lines only). NOTES and analyze_out.txt give 33 distinct; the measure's 36 counts a few dot-joined runs (e.g. '22.13.', '6.20.24.') as tokens. Three passages; letters 6-33 plus codes 113 117 211 222 327 329 519 527. Plaintext Dutch or French per NOTES.

system.summary: Figures 6-33 for letters (25 symbols) with eight 3-digit code groups for words, from the new code Boreel sent.
system.sibling_key: Every 1653-60 royalist and Commonwealth key on cryptiana (Marshall, Barwick-Hyde, Stamford, Butler, Charles II intercepted, Kingston, Westrope, Hague agent/Blake) tried; none fits.
system.notes: NOTES read (a) as monoalphabetic letters plus a small code (8 code groups); the matched control shows a plain or 2-homophone Dutch/French letter cipher of this layout would have been read, so the letter part is something else (syllables, nulls, more homophones) or Birch's print is corrupt. Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the four-piece thurloe entry.

prior_solution.where: Listed as undeciphered by Tomokiyo (cryptiana item #9); Birch's transcriptions are the only online witness and carry no decipherment.

conditions.human_role: unknown
tools: apply_keys.py (period keys scored by quadgram LM)
solve_a2.py (simulated annealing, bijective and homophonic modes)

solution.what: Extracted piece (a) from Birch's Thurloe State Papers on British History Online.
Frequencies and repeats of piece (a) (analyze.py).

Applied every 1653-60 royalist and Commonwealth key from cryptiana (Marshall, Barwick-Hyde, Stamford, Butler, Charles II intercepted 1655, Kingston, Westrope, Hague agent/Blake) to piece (a) with apply_keys.py, scored by quadgram models: nothing readable.
Hill-climb on (a) with Dutch and French quadgram LMs, bijective and homophonic, 8 restarts: best -4.71 per quad, Dutch-looking fragments only.
(a) as a plain alphabetical key on 10-33 with any rotation or reversal.

Matched control for solve_a2.py on (a) (control.py, control_out.txt): synthetic texts in (a)'s exact layout (66+47+15 = 128 letters, 8 code groups), held-out Dutch/French/period-English text, 40 trials per cell, solver code unchanged. Recovered (>= 80% of letters): simple substitution 39/40 nl, 40/40 fr, 36/40 en; 25-symbol homophonic (homo, LAM 0.5, MAXH 2) 26/40 nl, 24/40 fr, 17/40 en. (a)'s own best (-4.71 nl, -4.57 fr per quad) lies below all 40 Dutch and all 40 French homophonic controls, so the negative is meaningful: (a) is long enough, and is not a <=2-homophone letter cipher of Dutch/French text as modelled.

Split under the one-key rule: pieces (b), (c), (d), each in its own cipher, moved to dugard1656, copinger1656 and waddall1656 with their ciphertext files; this entry keeps piece (a) (Beverning 1653). Shared scripts stay here.

outcome.method_basis: Every 1653-60 key on cryptiana fails on piece (a) and quadgram annealing does not read it; a matched control shows the text is long enough for the solver, so the system is not the one modelled.
outcome.notes: Originals in Bodleian Rawlinson A, not digitised; a deciphered sibling despatch would be in the Nationaal Archief (Staten-Generaal liassen Engeland), not online. Matched control run 2026-09-22 (control.py): the solver recovers synthetic texts of (a)'s layout (simple substitution 95-100%, 25-symbol homophonic 43-65% of trials), so the failure is meaningful, not a length artefact. Split on 14 Oct 2026: (b)-(d) are now dugard1656, copinger1656, waddall1656. The only commit (347fef4b5, 2026-09-15) has no model trailer.

gaps.item: (a) Beverning 1653, 136 groups
gaps.detail: Matched control shows the length suffices for the solver, which still fails: system not the one modelled. Needs the key or a deciphered sibling despatch (Nationaal Archief), and Boreel's new code for the 8 code groups.

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the page or the address leaf (PARES images 1-4, checked 2026-10-02); no edition found.

transcription.source: PARES JPEGs (record 3576586, dbCode 27138937), about 975x1385 px at zoom 10, read from crops upscaled 2x
transcription.notes: 147 two-digit figures plus two signs not in the no. 247 table: a barred theta for ll (2) and an overlined M-like sign for r (1). One doubtful group, '17.0' read 17 30. Full context in transcription_249.txt.

system.summary: Homophonic substitution on two-digit figures 12-43 in alphabetical order, used inline in clear Spanish; no nomenclator, no nulls.
system.doubled_letters: written twice (n doubled for ñ); sometimes written once
system.sibling_key: none used
system.notes: Enciphered runs stand between clear words, which gave the cribs.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo lists 1565 Malta cipher letters as undeciphered and not this one; PARES has no decipherment. 'Undeciphered' on cryptiana means no contemporary decipherment, not unsolved; whether Tomokiyo or anyone else holds this easy alphabetical key is not known.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Worked out the PARES image route (cookie jar, dbCode, zoom 10) and fetched six images.
Transcribed the figure runs digit for digit with the clear text around them.
Runs beside clear words read as 'seiscientos' and 'en tiera', fixing a c d e i l n o r s t.
Key order is alphabetical, so the remaining letters (f, x, y, z) were predicted from their neighbours and confirmed in words.
Decoded the whole letter; nonsense in the output located misread digits, which were corrected on the images.
All groups in 12-43, all 32 used, no odd runs; names such as Provana di Leinì fit the Sicilian record for July 1565.

Found the same-day companion letter EST,LEG,1394,249 (duplicate, one page) by PARES search; its cipher runs decode with the same key (entrado el socorro, Cabo Bono, Argel, las galeras con la gente a la Goleta, partiran las galeras manana), adding a barred-theta sign for ll. Not read in full.

Novelty re-examined. G. Lasry (21 Sept 2026): on cryptiana 'undeciphered' means no interlinear or nearby deciphered copy, not unsolved; unsolved material is on the unsolved page. The key was rebuilt here from two cribs in the clear text, but it is easy and may have been recovered before; the claim is a reading of this letter, not a first break.
Fetched the four PARES images of no. 249 (record 3576586) with the cookie-jar route, zoom 10; image 1 is the letter, 2 and 3 blank, 4 the address leaf.
Transcribed the 13 lines carrying figures (25 runs, 150 tokens) and the clear text around them into transcription_249.txt, line by line, appending as each crop was read.
Decoded with the no. 247 key unchanged; decode.py extended to take the two extra signs (theta = ll, M-like sign = r) without changing its no. 247 output (diffed against the committed version).
Tested the overlined M-like sign before 18 36 33 38 19 36 37 12 as 're' (giving 'reespuesta') against 'r' (giving 'respuesta'); 're' rejected.

Every run divides into Spanish words (entrado el socorro, la llegada de los, Cabo Bono, Argel, las galeras, gente a la Goleta, a mal tienpo, respuesta del Maestre, forma de ponelle mas gente por, falta, pide mas de la, agora le puedo, partiran, manana): 150/150 tokens; es-golden-age -1.67 per char word-divided, shuffled -5.89. solution.what: Took the MysteryTwister Part 5 transcript (EHum 2016) and the solved Part 4 sibling transcript (Portugal IA-1).
Mutual-information diagnostics: digit 4 behaves as a null/word separator, 8 and 5 never end words, dotted digits mostly 7/2/0. The null diagnosis was wrong (Klee: 4 = o, 9 = null).
C# lattice solver (polyphonic singles, dotted singles, 2- and 3-digit codes; 5-gram LM + KL + MDL + word coverage) on the real text: no convergent key.
Synthetic key-1-style cipher: the pure LM objective is not identifiable; dictionary coverage separates true from wrong keys.
Meister 1906 keys nos. 1-3 (Montepulciano, the Poggio key 'mandata per il Montepulciano', Piacenza 1545) applied under trigram likelihood: all score below search optima.
Exact bi/trigram partition likelihood, annealing 21 letters over 9 digits (polyphonic single-digit model), Italian: 24 runs, 24 different keys, chance-level agreement.
Same search on a 7000-letter synthetic polyphonic cipher (syn_tri.py) recovers the true key.
Plaintext Spanish: 12 runs under a Don Quijote trigram model, no convergence.
Two-digit syllables on a fixed phase (vowel slots {2,0,7,5} after the Meister key-1 dot rule): no even/odd difference.
Word-final enrichment and frequency mass put the vowel-bearing digits at {7,0,3,1}. Wrong under Klee's key (7=n, 0=s, 3=m, 1=u/v).
Partition search constrained to vowels {7,0,3,1} (vc.py): 24 runs, agreement 0.861 against chance 0.799.
Matched synthetic with the believed structure (vc_syn.py): key recovered at 0.97 and 0.93 on two seeds, so the real text was judged not a polyphonic single-digit substitution.
Lattice solver with --null=4 --vowdig=7031 --consdig=85269: Italian-looking decodes but no convergence across four seeds; the word-coverage metric shown to be gameable.

One key across all pages (chi-squared), doubled digits suppressed, 27 and 80 as dominant word-final units, 441 repeated 7-grams, BPE units mostly one to three digits: diagnosed a variable-length syllabic code with nomenclature. The one-key and one/two-digit-unit findings fit Klee's key; the syllabic/nomenclature reading did not.
Lasry-Megyesi-Kopal 2021 and Lasry-Simonetta-Biermann HistoCrypt 2025 read; the cipher was identified as an Antonio Elio polyphonic-syllabic design. This identification was wrong.
Global two-digit grid tested in three phasings (gphase.py): none exists; units are variable-length.
DECODE R92 image route probed without a login: only 200x256 thumbnails, unreadable.
Elio-design synthetic (elio_syn.py) does not reproduce the real text's consonant runs or repetition; read as evidence of a nomenclature layer.

Clear copies located (BAV Chigi L III 65 ff. ~165-190, AAV Lettere de' Principi 14 A, Naples Carte Farnesiane 723) and key volume Chigi M II 49; none digitised. Meister pp. 176-178, 222-224 re-read from scans.

EM segmentation into one- and two-digit units (41 types, incl. 80, 57, 27, 03, 73) then unit-level annealing (usolve.py): fails on real text and on its synthetic control; oracle shows a pre-fixed segmentation caps the score.
DECODE account obtained (human); George Lasry confirms by e-mail that the Part 5 manuscript has no visual separators between tokens.

Downloaded R92 (eight 400-dpi images, transcription, address leaf) and R91 (IA-1 sibling). R92 transcription byte-identical to the challenge text; no interlinear decipherment (faint writing is show-through).
Seven page agents re-read every cipher line of 070r-073r against the images (IA-2_reread.txt): 151 positions corrected, dots checked. Structural statistics unchanged.
Spain IA-1 (R91): different digit profile and no doubling suppression, so a different key.
Doubled-digit rate as a relabelling invariant: no renumbering of Meister keys 1 or 2, nor any single-digit polyphonic design, gives IA-2's rate.
DECODE searched for further Farnese/Poggio material; Camera Apostolica R23, R202-R204 fetched: Avignon keys of c. 1379, irrelevant.

Simon Klee's independent solution (published 16 Sept 2026, MysteryTwister-accepted) reviewed and accepted: split-half recoveries agree, synthetic and shuffled controls, manuscript checks, historical corroboration. Key recorded in key.md; the project's own diagnosis marked superseded.

Token mass along the numbers matches no alphabetical, column or multiplicative order; the profile matches a synthetic two-part nomenclator (310 types, 146 singletons).

tools: C# (csc 4.0): homophonic, monotone and heat-bath annealers

solution.what: HCPortal images of ff. 3r-4r (media 1448, 1449); all 8 Arcinsys images of the file: wrapper, f. 3v docket 'Schreiben an [blank] in Ziffern', f. 4v French draft reply.

Arcinsys searches across all Hessian archives for cipher items (Chiffre, chiffriert, dechiffriert, Ziffern, Geheimschrift...); HCPortal records 494-523 and all 319 keys; BLKÖ biography of the prince. No key, decipherment or sibling letter; the 1744 volumes (118 a Nr. 1973-1980) are undigitised.
45 lines transcribed from full-resolution crops (trans_p1.txt, trans_p2.txt): 717 groups, 303 distinct; two writer's corrections resolved.
The French draft on f. 4v read: the prince answers a letter of 18 January (New Year wishes, news) and promises a vacancy in his regiment; the cipher letter is most probably that letter.

Frequencies, repeats, shared contexts: flat profile (top group 2%), 879.144.X.126 x4 with X = 90/7/7/924 and a struck 9 corrected to 7 (homophones), no immediate repeats, codes under 100 used twice as often.

Letter-level homophonic synthetic of the same size and profile: a 5-gram annealer finds gibberish scoring as well as or better than the true plaintext (modern model -1234 vs -1408; 1740s model -1090.5 vs -1094.4).

Word-segmentation term (unigram 1740s word model, Viterbi) added: the true key now scores highest on the control (-2173) but annealing (12 x 20 M moves, -2340) and heat-bath sampling (-2679) do not reach it.
Letter-level annealer with the 1740s 5-gram on the real text: best -1107.5, restarts disagree, no German.
One-part (alphabetical) code: token-mass KS test against German syllabary usage rejects natural order over 1-999 (0.192 vs random 0.077) and over 100-999 (0.149).

Hessen-Kassel keys in Marburg (HCPortal; DECODE's 112 records of 1710-1799) listed; 4 d Nr. 1220 f. 12 and Nr. 1231 show column-numbered alphabetical syllabaries; Nr. 1231, 1229 (R4680) and 1237 (R4741, R4742) do not fit this letter.
Column-numbered one-part code as in the Hessian keys (units digit = column), cyclic orders and multiplicative numberings: no better fit than random numberings.

Monotone annealers (after swieten1757/msolve.py) with free codes under 100, per-digit chains, Hessian remap, heat-bath sampling: stall below the truth on alphabetical controls; fragment soup on the real text.

Two-part nomenclator synthetic after R4680 (letters with 4 homophones, 600 syllables and words) reproduces the real profile (310 types, 146 singletons, top 14); on it the true key scores -1934 / -1284 while blind runs find gibberish at -1060 / -255: the key is not identifiable from 717 groups.
New Year wish implied by the reply ('zu dem angetretenen neuen Jahre', fitting the line-1 hyphen if groups were letters): cannot be placed in a two-part code with unknown unit boundaries.

documents.shelfmark: BL Add MS 4136 f. 33 (DECODE R2989)

plaintext.source: Bain, Cal. Scottish Papers ii no. 804 prints one cipher phrase deciphered ('and says he must neidis haif it be on meinis or uthir'); it does not align with this line.

transcription.source: DECODE image IMG_R2989_I20715_P.jpg
transcription.notes: One line copied at the foot of a Throckmorton leaf; '/' separator and a '(J)' group of 5 signs.

system.summary: One line of 39 symbols in the family of the Moray-Wood 1568 cipher (x and z variants, g, o, e, f), probably a letter substitution.
system.sibling_key: Moray to Wood, 13 July 1568 (Tomokiyo's transcription, unread): same symbol families, not aligned glyph for glyph
system.notes: IC 0.069 on 39 symbols; opens and closes with the same trigram g x ob. The Throckmorton text on the same leaf (Cipher 3) and the f. 32 margin code are other systems with their own entries.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, cryptiana unsolved.htm, lists it as unidentified; Bain ii 804 prints the letter with one phrase marked as cipher, which does not align with this line

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tomokiyo unsolved.htm and project throckmorton notes: the Throckmorton text on f. 33 is read (Cipher 3); the John Wood line at its foot is open.
R2989 Wood line transcribed at 3x zoom, 39 signs; matched to the Moray-Wood symbol families.
Bain ii no. 804 gives the deciphered cipher phrase of Wood's 6 Sept 1568 letter.
Exhaustive alignment of the Bain phrase (letters, nulls, syllable signs; forward and reversed; all substrings) against the line.
HMC Salisbury i (Hatfield calendar): no entry for Wood 6 Sept 1568; Bain ii 804 is the only print.
R2989 non-uniqueness: 200 anneal restarts vs Bain ii quadgrams; 185 beat median real text, 92 mutually distinct gibberish solutions, so the 39-sign line is undetermined.

Entry split on 14 Oct 2026 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026) from wod1568, which had joined three systems on BL Add MS 4136 ff. 32-33: Throckmorton's Cipher 1 letter of 10 July 1559 (throck1559), the f. 32 marginal word-sign code (throck1559margin) and John Wood's 1568 line (wod1568). This profile keeps John Wood's 1568 line (R2989) only.

outcome.method_basis: Bain's printed cipher phrase does not align with the 39-symbol line under any tested model, and a non-uniqueness test shows that dozens of unrelated English readings fit it, so it is undetermined by its own text.
outcome.fraction_read_source: No symbol of wood_line.txt is claimed as read.
outcome.notes: Attempted, closed unread 21 Sept 2026. Needs the Hatfield original (Cecil Papers vol. 1) for a true crib. Split 14 Oct 2026 from wod1568.

texts.label: Yard to Manchester, Whitehall, 12 Oct 1699 (Yale OID 16601173)
texts.summary: Robert Yard, under-secretary, to the Earl of Manchester, ambassador in Paris: messengers wait at Dover for Mills; the Lords Justices of Ireland report disaffected persons returning and an ill design against the government, with like intimations from Scotland, all said to be carried on very privately at Saint-Germain; a letter from Lebrun at Paris enclosing one for a Mr Gray was opened at the post house.

texts.label: Yard to Manchester, Whitehall, 16 Oct 1699 (Yale OID 16601175)
texts.summary: Mills has gone by way of Rouen, so warrants are out and three messengers watch the coast, London and Dover for him and Lord Drummond's priest; directions on Fowles; no goldsmith Cockburne in Round Court; Clance the periwig maker has gone to France and should be watched.
